cues.en: an immersive multi day adventure set in the Star Wars universe. When this was first announced, everybody just called it the Star Wars Hotel. cues.en: a landlocked cruise. Aside from a brief excursion into the Star Wars themed section of Hollywood Studios, you're not meant to leave the building. So we booked the standard room, which was the cheapest and the smallest, but there were actually options for one bedroom or two bedroom suites. The website didn't even list sample prices for these, but one fan blog took one for the team and called about booking the largest suite on a random day in September, and they were quoted a price of over $12,000.
cues.zh: 孩子们最好别睡懒觉。另外我要说明一下，我买的是最基础的、不带任何额外服务的套餐。原本有很多可选的附加项目，但我都没有买。准确地说，我可能买了一些，但在我预订的时候没人跟我提过，所以我根本不知道它们存在，等知道的时候已经晚了。我预订的时候，酒店还没对公众开放，很多信息都被捂着不放，好像默认你就该知道该问什么，但显然，我不知道。老实说，整个预订过程极其令人困惑、恼火又心力交瘁。我们订的是标准间，也就是最便宜、最小的那种，但其实还有一居室和两居室套房可选。网站上连这些套房的参考价格都没列，不过有个粉丝博客为了替大家探底，打电话询问了在九月的某个随机日期预订最大的套房，得到的报价超过一万两千美元。

cues.en: There were also less extravagant add ons. For $30 per person, I could have upgraded our dinner seating to the captain's table experience.
cues.zh: 还有一些没那么夸张的附加项目。每人花 30 美元，就可以把晚餐座位升级成“船长桌”体验。

cues.en: And again, I didn't know that existed when I booked, so I didn't get to book it. And I sure wish I had.
cues.zh: 同样，我预订的时候根本不知道有这个东西，所以没订上。我真是太后悔了。

cues.en: We'll get to that. The only add on I did pay for was the memory maker. This was the one thing they did recommend to me. Basically, when I was booking, they said there would be a bunch of roaming photographers on the ship, taking both candid and posed photos of guests. The memory maker bundle was a $169,
cues.zh: 后面会讲到这个。我唯一花钱买的附加项目是“记忆珍藏”（Memory Maker）。这是他们唯一主动推荐给我的东西。简单来说，预订的时候他们告诉我，船上会有一群四处走动的摄影师，抓拍和摆拍游客的照片。“记忆珍藏”套餐售价 169 美元

cues.en: and it would allow unlimited free downloads of those photos. I correctly predicted that I would be recording video the whole time and fail to get any photos of myself, so I bought it. However, after I bought it, and just a few weeks before my trip, they rolled out another different add on where you could buy a private photo shoot for thirty minutes for $399.
cues.zh: 可以无限次免费下载这些照片。我准确地预判到自己会全程忙着录视频，最后一张自己的照片都拍不到，所以就买了。然而在我买完之后、就在出发前几周，他们又推出了另一个新的附加项目：花 399 美元可以购买一次三十分钟的私人专属拍摄。

cues.en: And from what I can tell, once Disney rolled out this more expensive private photo session, they just reassigned all photographers who would have been roaming the ship to do the private shoots instead, because it made more money. So what I'm saying is that I paid the $169
cues.zh: 而据我所知，自从迪士尼推出了这种更贵的私人拍照服务后，他们就直接把原本会在船上四处巡游的摄影师全部调去拍私人预约了，因为这个更赚钱。所以我的意思是，我花了169美元

cues.en: for memory maker, and we didn't see any photographers the entire trip, except for the ones actively engaged in private photo shoots. So I just kind of lit that money on fire, and I have pretty much no photos of my trip, but whatever. This didn't sit right with me, and I did like a sanity check on some fan groups, and found out that the same thing had happened to a bunch of people, where they just saw no photographers the whole time. So I actually called and emailed a couple different departments at Disney asking for a refund,
cues.zh: 买了“记忆珍藏”服务，结果整个行程下来一个摄影师都没见到，只看到那些正忙着拍私人预约的摄影师。所以基本上等于我把钱点火烧掉了，我的旅行几乎没留下任何照片，不过算了。这事让我心里不舒服，我在一些粉丝群里做了个调查，发现很多其他游客也遇到了同样的情况——整整一趟旅程见不到任何摄影师。于是我给迪士尼的几个不同部门打了电话也发了邮件，要求退款，

cues.en: and wasn't able to get one. They just said no. But then, I complained on my Twitter account, which has a lot of followers, and suddenly they personally called me and gave me my refund. They didn't even ask for my phone number. Like, someone at Disney did the legwork to go into the database, look up my booking info, and then find my phone number, and call me within like a day of the tweet going out. And the person who called me was really nice, and I'm thankful that he cared to resolve it. But I just always feel very cynical when I try to resolve issues through the appropriate channels available to all customers, and nobody will help me until they find out I'm an influencer.
cues.zh: 但没拿到。他们就一口回绝了。后来我在我那个粉丝众多的推特账号上发了抱怨，突然他们就亲自打电话给我，把退款退给了我。他们甚至没问我要电话号码。迪士尼的人专门去数据库里查了我的预订信息，找到了我的电话号码，在推文发出后大约一天之内就给我打了电话。打电话的那个人人很好，我很感谢他愿意把这个事解决掉。但我每次通过所有顾客都能用的正规渠道解决问题时，都感到非常心寒——没人愿意帮我，直到他们发现我是个网红。

cues.en: I spoke with several other guests who got memory maker and had the exact same problems as me, and they never got refunds. Another hidden cost was that Disney recommended Star Cruiser guests arrive one day before their booking date. Real cruises, the ones that are on boats, also recommend this. Because in both cases, time is of the essence, and you don't want your whole trip ruined because of a flight delay. Remember, $2 per person per minute, so we're not showing up late. But of course, this additional night in Florida is just another bonus expense for out of town guests. One thing that was included in the Star Cruiser price was admission to the theme park for up to seven hours,
cues.zh: 我和几位同样买了“记忆珍藏”的其他游客聊过，他们遇到了和我一模一样的问题，但从来没人拿到退款。另一个隐藏费用是，迪士尼建议“星际巡游”的客人在预订日期前一天到达。真正的游轮——就是那种开在水面上的——也是这么建议的。因为在这两种情况下，时间都至关重要，你不会想让整个行程因为航班延误而泡汤的。别忘了，每人每分钟2美元，所以我们可不能迟到。但当然，在佛罗里达多住的这一晚，对外地游客来说又是一笔额外的开销。“星际巡游”的价格里包含了一项内容：最多七小时的主题乐园入场资格，

cues.en: and there were several suggested add ons for that block of time, but those cost extra. You could book Lightsaber Building for $220,
cues.zh: 针对这几个小时有很多推荐的附加项目，但都要另外收费。你可以花220美元预约光剑制作，

cues.en: Droid Building for a $100, or reserve a table at Oga's Cantina,
cues.zh: 花100美元预约机器人制作，或者在奥加酒馆订个座位，

cues.en: food and drinks not included. For all of the above optional add ons I've listed, there was not enough availability for every guest at the hotel to get them, even if everybody was interested in booking every single one. They were all pretty limited in quantity,
cues.zh: 餐食和饮品不含在内。我列出的所有这些可选附加项目，数量都不够让酒店的所有客人都订到，哪怕每个人都想订每一个。它们的数量都相当有限，

cues.en: and first come first serve, and you had to know to book them. I guess some people got emails about these things, but because of a glitch, like half the people who booked just didn't get them. I was one of those. And even if everyone had known, they would have had to fight over these things. So it was kind of baked into the model that although all trips were expensive,
cues.zh: 先到先得，而且你还得知道要去预订。据说是有些人收到了相关邮件，但由于系统故障，大约一半预订了的人根本没收到邮件。我就是其中之一。而且就算所有人都知道了，大家还得去抢这些项目。所以这个商业模式里某种程度上是预设好的：虽然所有行程都很贵，

cues.en: the bulk of the trips would inherently be inferior in some way. Which brings me to my next point. Part four, Spirit Airlines in space. In The United States, we have an airline called Spirit Airlines.
cues.zh: 但大部分行程必然会在某方面低人一等。这就引出了我的下一个观点。第四部分：太空版的灵魂航空。在美国，我们有一家叫灵魂航空（Spirit Airlines）的航空公司。

cues.en: Everybody makes fun of it, and it's just kind of universally acknowledged that this is the cheap, awful airline that you only fly on if you have no other choice. Basically, how Spirit's business model works is their base ticket cost is insanely low. It's usually about half the price of the other airlines. But that half price ticket is going to be the worst flight of your life in the tiniest chair you've ever sat in, bringing nothing with you but the clothes on your back. This is because Spirit makes every possible amenity cost extra. Diet Coke costs extra. The little bags of pretzels cost extra. Legroom costs extra. Bags cost extra. Even carry on bags, even a purse. I actually don't think flying Spirit is a bad way to fly. If you pay for the Diet Coke and the extra leg room and the carry on luggage, it just becomes a normal flight, just like you'd experience on any other airline. And with all that stuff added on, you're not ultimately paying more than another airline, you're usually paying around the same amount. So in a practical sense, Spirit is exactly the same as every other airline, they just present the prices in a different way up front. So why does everybody hate Spirit?
cues.zh: 所有人都拿它开玩笑，大家也普遍觉得，这是一家便宜又糟糕的航空公司，只有别无选择时才会坐。基本上，Spirit 的商业模式就是把基础票价压得特别低，通常只有其他航空公司的半价。但买了这张半价机票，你就会经历人生中最糟糕的一趟航班：坐在你坐过的最窄小座椅上，除了身上的衣服什么也别带。这是因为 Spirit 把所有可能的服务都设成了额外收费。健怡可乐要加钱，那一小袋椒盐卷饼也要加钱。想要多点腿部空间要加钱，行李要加钱。连随身行李，甚至手提包，都要加钱。其实我不觉得坐 Spirit 是种糟糕的出行方式。如果你愿意为健怡可乐、多一点腿部空间和随身行李付费，那它就会变成一趟普通航班，和其他航空公司的体验差不多。把这些都加上之后，你最终花的钱也不会比坐其他航空公司更多，通常差不多。所以从实际体验来说，Spirit 和其他航空公司完全一样，只不过一开始展示价格的方式不同。那为什么大家都讨厌 Spirit 呢？

cues.en: Because of the psychology of it. Because you see that initial price, and then for each amenity you're forced to add along the way to get back to that baseline service you're used to, each thing the airline demands payment for, you feel like you're being scammed. It makes the airline look duplicitous
cues.zh: 因为这涉及心理作用。你先看到那个起始票价，然后为了恢复到你习惯的基础服务水平，每一步都得加上一个服务项目；航空公司每要你为一样东西付费，你就觉得自己被骗了。这会让航空公司显得两面三刀，

cues.en: and stingy. You're like, ugh, they really want money for a tiny bag of pretzels? Really, guys? And it's like, well, on United Airlines, the pretzels aren't really free either. They're just factored into the total cost. But you don't know that when you're paying for the ticket. So when you get the pretzels, it feels like a perk. Framing is everything. If you pay extra for every aspect of an experience across many steps of booking,
cues.zh: 而且小气。你会想：“唉，一小袋椒盐卷饼也要收钱？真的假的？”但话说回来，在 United Airlines，椒盐卷饼其实也不是免费的，只是费用已经算进总价里了。可你买票时并不知道这一点。所以拿到椒盐卷饼时，你会觉得这是额外福利。怎么呈现一切都很重要。如果你在预订过程中经历很多步骤，每一项体验都要额外付费，

cues.en: you feel taken advantage of every time it happens. It makes your relationship with the company feel antagonistic,
cues.zh: 每遇到一次，你都会觉得自己被占了便宜。这会让你和公司的关系变得像是在对立，

cues.en: as if they're trying to get away with doing as little for you as possible. And on the other hand, if you opt out of those amenities, if you don't add them on, you get a lesser experience.
cues.zh: 仿佛他们想方设法少为你做点事。另一方面，如果你不选那些服务项目，不把它们加上去，你的体验就会差一些。

cues.en: You'll have saved money, but you'll also be sitting on the same plane with all the people who did opt in to the slightly better experience,
cues.zh: 你确实省了钱，但也会和那些花钱升级体验的人坐在同一架飞机上，

cues.en: and you'll be watching them get this better service. And that doesn't feel good either. That makes you feel poor. And that is why everyone thinks Spirit Airlines is the scammy trashy airline, and they feel negatively about flying on it. So that's already pretty bad. But now, let's run a thought experiment
cues.zh: 眼看着他们享受更好的服务。这种感觉也不好受，会让你觉得自己很穷。这就是为什么大家都觉得 Spirit Airlines 是一家坑人又糟糕的航空公司，坐它的航班也让人不爽。这已经够糟了。不过现在，我们来做个思想实验：

cues.en: where Spirit Airlines charges extra for everything,
cues.zh: 假设 Spirit Airlines 什么都额外收费，

cues.en: but that base ticket is no longer half price. In fact, it doesn't even cost the same as all the other airlines. It actually costs more than everyone else is charging, and yet all those amenities still cost extra. Extra square footage, extra activities,
cues.zh: 但基础票价不再只有半价。事实上，它的票价甚至不和其他航空公司一样。它的价格比所有其他航空公司都高，可所有那些服务项目还是要额外收费。想要多一点空间，要加钱；想参加额外活动，

cues.en: extra character interactions,
cues.zh: 想和角色互动，

cues.en: your trip photos.
cues.zh: 想要旅途照片，也都要加钱。

cues.en: Hey, guys, we know you'll probably want all of these things, but each of them is gonna cost you just a little bit extra. You don't have to buy any of them, but just be aware that if you don't, there is a non zero chance that your already very expensive vacation
cues.zh: 嘿，各位，我们知道你们大概率想把这些都买齐，但每一样都得额外再花一点钱。你可以什么都不买，但要知道，如果不买，那你本来就已经贵得离谱的假期，

cues.en: is going to be just a little bit worse than it could have been. In my opinion, if the starting price is already so expensive that all anyone who brings up your product talks about is how expensive it is, it should then be all inclusive.
cues.zh: 很可能会比本该有的体验要差那么一点点。在我看来，如果起步价已经贵到所有人一提起你的产品就只聊它有多贵，那它就应该是一价全包的。

cues.en: Add ons should not exist. The already high price should cover everything. And there especially shouldn't be add ons that can only accommodate a small fraction of the guests. If you're selling something as a once in a lifetime experience,
cues.zh: 根本不应该存在什么附加收费项目。这么高的价格就应该涵盖一切。尤其不应该出现只能惠及一小部分游客的付费项目。如果你卖的是一次一生仅一次的体验，

cues.en: if an amenity cannot be provided for all guests, it should not be sold to any of them. So what I'm saying is the price seems bad, and it is. But what matters is that generates a customer experience,
cues.zh: 那某项设施如果不能提供给所有游客，就不该卖给任何一个。所以我想说的是，这个价格看起来很糟，事实也确实很糟。但更重要的是，它造就了一种顾客体验，

cues.en: which is also bad. Part five, the ship. You'll be seeing glimpses of it in all my footage anyway, but I'm sure you're curious. So first, let me walk you through all of the physical environments in this experience. All the spaces accessible to guests. First stop, the arrival terminal. Driving up was kind of interesting. We actually went to the Hollywood Studios Park and then traveled back stage. Doesn't even feel like we're supposed to be here.
cues.zh: 而这个体验同样很糟。第五部分，这艘船。反正你会在我的所有镜头里零星看到它，但我猜你们肯定很好奇。那我们先来把这次体验中所有的实体空间走一遍，也就是游客能进入的所有区域。第一站，抵达航站楼。开车过去还挺有意思的。我们其实是先到了好莱坞影城园区，然后从后台穿过去的。感觉完全不像是我们该待的地方。

cues.en: That looks like the sign. I think that's the sign. No. That's definitely it. But it's like we're backstage.
cues.zh: 那个看起来像指示牌。我觉得那就是牌子。不对，那肯定就是它。不过感觉就像我们在幕后区域。

cues.en: So we got to see the back of Star Wars land and drive past what I think are cast parking lots.
cues.zh: 所以我们看到了星战主题园的背面，还开过了我觉得应该是演职人员停车场的地方。

cues.en: Yep.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: Starcruiser.
cues.zh: 星际巡洋舰。

cues.en: Starcruiser.
cues.zh: 星际巡洋舰。

cues.en: Crazy.
cues.zh: 太疯狂了。

cues.en: So because it was a restricted area, they had a security gate and they took our IDs to make sure we actually had a reservation before we could even drive up to the hotel. When we got to the terminal, it was pretty chaotic. The Starcruiser set an arrival window of 1PM to 4PM,
cues.zh: 因为那是限制区域，设了一道安检门，他们会收走我们的证件，确认我们真的有预订，然后才能开车到酒店跟前。到了航站楼，场面相当混乱。星际巡洋舰规定的入住时段是下午1点到4点，

cues.en: but I've already shown you the cost per minute breakdown. Obviously, everybody is trying to get there and get inside as early as they can. In the story of the hotel, you must take a pod from the terminal up into space, where the star cruiser Halcyon is waiting in orbit. So in the real world, you must take a themed elevator to the lobby of the hotel, which is on the 2nd Floor. And I think that is fun. I think it's very cute. But that also means that they can only let like 10 guests into the hotel at a time, and the line has to stop for a minute in between. So with everybody arriving all at once, you can expect like a forty minute wait before you can actually get inside. For reasons I genuinely cannot understand, Disney decided not to build any kind of indoor lobby at street level. It's just a long wait in this sad outdoor queue area, and then a slightly shorter wait in this sad concrete hallway. And again, in the story, you're not on the ship yet, so I didn't expect anything super fancy here. But like in story, this space is meant to emulate an airport terminal, so why does it look sadder than that? Surely, they could have built an enclosed air conditioned lobby with some chairs, and then maybe guests could take a number instead of standing in line. Just so everybody isn't waiting in a packed outdoor queue in the Florida heat
cues.zh: 但我已经给你们看过每分钟花多少钱的账单了。显然，人人都想尽早赶到、尽早进去。在酒店的故事设定里，你必须从航站楼乘一个舱体上太空，轨道上的“哈尔希安号”星际巡洋舰就在那里等你。所以在现实世界里，你必须乘一部主题电梯才能到酒店大堂，大堂在二楼。我觉得这挺有意思的，我觉得很可爱。但这也意味着他们每次只能放大约10位客人进酒店，而且两批之间队伍还得停一分钟。所以在大家同时抵达的情况下，你可以预料到自己要等差不多40分钟才能真正进去。让我完全无法理解的是，迪斯尼竟然决定不在一楼建任何形式的室内大堂。你只能在这个凄凉的室外排队区苦等，然后再在这个凄凉的水泥走廊里稍微等短一点的时间。再说一次，按故事设定，你这时还没登上飞船，所以我并不指望这里有多豪华。但按剧情，这个空间本来是要模仿机场航站楼的，那为什么它看起来比真机场还凄惨？他们完全可以建一个有空调的封闭大堂，摆上些椅子，然后也许可以让大家取号，而不是排队站着。这样一来，大家就不用顶着佛罗里达的酷热，

cues.en: in their Star Wars cosplays, which are also warm. And I do mean packed, because there wasn't very much physical room for people to line up, which added to the chaotic vibe. I think Disney must have assumed during construction that not everybody would arrive at once, but why would they assume that? They knew how much money they were charging. I mean, they even advised everyone to get there an entire day early so they could arrive on time. The cast members brought around chilled bottles of the space to Sani. They sell in Galaxy's Edge to compensate for the heat, which was very nice. And obviously, a forty minute wait isn't the end of the world. But in every aspect of the hotel, I am keeping the price in mind. Again, this was billed as a luxury hotel. And in my opinion, this isn't a luxury hotel way to welcome guests. Plus, our trip was in March, and we were sweating in the shade. Imagine going in August. I mean, you don't have to now, because they're out of business, but whatever. Right before you get on your pod into space, you get a little out of character intro video. I think this video could have incorporated a little more guidance on the gameplay of the experience,
cues.zh: 穿着本身也很闷热的星战角色扮演服，挤在室外排队了。我是说“挤”，因为根本没有多少让人排队的实际空间，这让混乱的感觉更甚。我猜迪斯尼在建设时肯定以为大家不会同时到达，可他们为什么会这么以为？他们很清楚自己收了多少钱。我是说，他们甚至建议所有人提前一整天到达，好准时办理入住。演职人员会推着冰镇的“太空消毒水”饮料过来分发，那是他们在银河边缘园区卖的，用来缓解暑热，这倒是很贴心。显然，40分钟的等待也不是世界末日。但对于酒店的每个环节，我都把价格记在心里。再强调一次，这里可是按奢华酒店来宣传的。而在我看来，这种迎接客人的方式可不符合奢华酒店的标准。另外，我们是三月去的，站在阴凉处都还在流汗。想象一下八月来的样子。不过现在你不用想象了，因为他们已经歇业了，随便吧。就在你登上舱体上太空之前，会播放一小段跳出角色设定的介绍视频。我觉得这个视频本可以再多讲一点这次体验的玩法规则，

cues.en: but its primary function was to play a demo of the in character emergency alarm. As your adventure progresses, there will be special highly dramatic moments that will ask for everyone's intention.
cues.zh: 但它的主要功能其实是演示角色设定内的紧急警报。随着你的冒险推进，会出现一些极其戏剧化的特殊时刻，需要所有人集中注意力。

cues.en: They will be signaled with a ship wide display that looks like this.
cues.zh: 届时会通过一个像这样的全船显示屏向他们发出信号。

cues.en: Then for comparison, they play the out of character alarm and tell you the protocol for a real emergency. For example, if you're in your hotel room when a fire breaks out, the hotel doesn't have fire escapes, so you're meant to crouch in this little shame closet and press a panic button, then wait in the dark for help to arrive. Comforting. I actually thought this was such a good idea. The intro video, not the shame closet. I have criticized certain other immersive experiences in the past for failing to distinguish between real and fake emergencies.
cues.zh: 然后作为对比，他们会播放出戏警报，并告诉你真实紧急情况的应对规程。比如，如果火灾发生时你在酒店房间里，酒店没有消防逃生梯，所以你得蹲在这个小小的“丢人壁橱”里，按下紧急按钮，然后在黑暗中等待救援。真让人安心。其实我觉得这主意特别好。我说的是介绍视频，不是那个丢人壁橱。我以前批评过某些其他沉浸式体验，因为它们分不清真实和模拟紧急情况。

cues.en: But also,
cues.zh: 但话说回来，

cues.en: fake emergencies are fun, as long as you know that they're fake. So the idea of doing this video gets a chef's kiss from me. And it didn't feel like a spoiler. If anything, it made me more excited for the story, because immediately you start wondering when the alarm is going to go off. Upon arrival, everyone's luggage has to go through a security check, and all the people also have to go through a security check. These happen separately, because the bellhops take your luggage away as soon as you arrive. So they would confiscate pocket knives, scissors,
cues.zh: 假紧急情况很好玩，只要你知道它们是假的。所以我给拍这个视频的想法来了个“厨师之吻”。而且这并不像剧透。反倒让我对故事更期待，因为你马上就会开始想警报什么时候响。到达时，每个人的行李都要安检，所有人也要安检。两者是分开进行的，因为你一到，行李员就会把行李拿走。所以他们会没收小刀、剪刀，

cues.en: and anything that looks like a gun, even if it was a prop. And your journey begins.
cues.zh: 以及任何看起来像枪的东西，哪怕是道具。然后你的旅程就开始了。

cues.en: Wow. Once we made it up to the ship, individual cast members were waiting to walk each guest to their rooms. They also gave like a little mini tour as they walked with little nuggets of ship lore. That little door right there is from our founder, Chuck Jabbour.
cues.zh: 哇。我们上船后，每位客人都有演职人员等着带他们去房间。他们边走还边做了个小导览，讲了些飞船的小掌故。那边那扇小门来自我们的创始人 Chuck Jabbour。

cues.en: He wasn't in selling, so...
cues.zh: 他当时不是做销售的，所以……

cues.en: Oh, so he only needs a little... Oh, look how tiny... Exactly.
cues.zh: 哦，所以他只需要一点点……哦，看它多小……没错。

cues.en: He is not with us anymore, unfortunately. Aw. And then they pointed out where everything was in the room. And our luggage was already waiting for us in our room by the time we got inside, which I loved. That whole part of the experience did feel very deluxe to me, so we were off to a positive start. We were also presented with our m bands,
cues.zh: 不幸的是，他已经不在了。唉。然后他们给我们指了房间里各种东西的位置。我们进屋时，行李已经在房间里等我们了，我很喜欢这点。那一段体验对我来说确实很有豪华感，所以我们开局很顺利。我们还拿到了我们的 m bands，

cues.en: which in the rest of Disney World Resort are called magic bands,
cues.zh: 在 Disney World Resort 的其他地方，它们叫 magic bands，

cues.en: but these ones are special, because they look different. The band has an RFID chip in it, so you can use it as a room key. You can attach a credit card to it and use it to make purchases,
cues.zh: 但这些很特别，因为它们看起来不一样。手环里有一枚 RFID 芯片，所以可以当房卡用。你可以绑定信用卡，用它购物，

cues.en: and it also stores fast passes for rides. This is not new technology for Disney. They've been doing it at all their hotels for a while now, but I do like it. I think it's handy. So now the trip has officially begun, and it's time to take a look around. The Atrium,
cues.zh: 它还储存游乐设施的快速通行证。这对迪士尼来说不是新技术。他们所有酒店都已经这么做一段时间了，但我确实喜欢。我觉得很方便。现在旅程正式开始，该四处看看了。The Atrium，

cues.en: this is where we entered. It's a beautiful space. I like it a lot. It has a balcony, which is inaccessible to guests. Up there is where a lot of the major story elements are going to play out, so it's actors only. There are all these cushiony couches with end tables to set drinks on, and down at leg level, they also have outlets and USB ports to charge your devices while you're sitting there. I will say everybody was tripping over these low tables the entire weekend.
cues.zh: 我们就是从这里进来的。这地方很漂亮。我很喜欢。它有一个阳台，客人不能上去。上面是很多主要剧情发生的地方，所以只有演员能去。这里全是软垫沙发，旁边有小边桌放饮料；在腿的高度还有插座和 USB 接口，可以坐着给设备充电。我得说，整个周末大家都在被这些矮桌绊到。

cues.en: They are at shin height for maximum bruising. There's this little model of the Halcyon, the ship we're meant to be on, so it's a little visual aid. At various points throughout the day, they also leave out prepackaged snacks in the atrium, and they have tops in the corner for chilled and sparkling water. There are two tiny windows way up high on one end through which you can kind of see neighboring planets, or when the ship jumps to light speed, you can see the stripes. To be honest, I don't think it's the best view. I kind of envisioned the common areas of the ship having a lot more ground level windows to space. I probably envisioned that because that's what all of the concept art showed before the hotel was constructed.
cues.zh: 它们的椅子只有小腿那么高，保证你能被磕得青一块紫一块。那里还有一个小小的 Halcyon 号模型——就是我们本来要乘坐的那艘船，算是给点直观的展示。一天中的不同时段，他们还会在中庭摆放一些预包装零食，角落里还有带龙头的水机，提供冰水和气泡水。在一侧的高处有两扇极小的窗户，透过它们多少能看到邻近的星球，而当飞船跳跃到光速时，还能看到那些光条纹。说实话，我觉得这景观不怎么样。我原本想象中飞船的公共区域应该有很多齐地面的落地窗，正对着太空。我大概是受概念图影响才会有这种想象，因为酒店建造之前放出的概念艺术图全都是这么画的。

cues.en: Also, I got to eat at the space station themed restaurant in Epcot, which opened like a year before the Starcruiser,
cues.zh: 另外，我还去吃了 Epcot 那家太空站主题餐厅，它比 Starcruiser 早开了一年左右，

cues.en: and has a ton of really large space windows, and I thought that left a much more breathtaking impression. Oh, I should also mention that when the ship jumps to light speed,
cues.zh: 有很多超大的太空观景窗，给我的震撼感强得多。哦，我还得提一下，当飞船跳跃到光速时，

cues.en: I thought it would be cool if the atrium or the bridge was on some kind of hydraulic pad to give a little bit of movement when you make the jump. You know, nothing hard enough to make people stumble, but just like a little kick. And since that sounded pretty ambitious, I thought they would just put subwoofers under the floor and it would like vibrate or something,
cues.zh: 我本来觉得如果中庭或者舰桥装在某种液压平台上，让你在跳跃时能感觉到一点晃动，那会很酷。不用晃得太厉害让人站不稳，就轻轻一顿。不过这想法听起来挺有野心的，所以我猜他们顶多会在地板下装低音炮，让它震一震什么的，

cues.en: and they actually didn't do that either. When the ship jumps to light speed, it plays the sound effect, and you can see the hyperspace lines through those small distant windows, but it's not a horribly convincing effect. One feature I liked in the atrium are these big column things with projections inside. The projections are sort of rotating advertisements
cues.zh: 结果他们连这个都没做。飞船跳跃到光速时只是播放音效，你可以透过那些又小又远的窗户看到超空间光线，但效果实在谈不上逼真。中庭里有个我喜欢的设计，就是那种里面带投影的大柱子。投影放的是些循环滚动的广告，

cues.en: for things you can do on the ship, like an image of Gaia to promote her concert.
cues.zh: 宣传船上能玩的活动，比如 Gaia 的形象，用来宣传她的演唱会。

cues.en: Sometimes it's the Halcyon logo.
cues.zh: 有时是 Halcyon 的标志。

cues.en: And then at one point in the storyline, the First Order puts their logo up there, because they've taken over. I've heard a lot of discourse about whether or not the ship looks like Star Wars, mostly people saying that it does not. Obviously, that's because everybody thinks of the Star Wars aesthetic as being dingy,
cues.zh: 然后在剧情的某个节点，第一军团会把自己的标志挂上去，因为他们已经接管了这艘船。我看过很多关于这艘船到底像不像星战的讨论，大多数人都说不像。显然，这是因为大家一提到星战美学想到的就是脏兮兮、

cues.en: lived in. Everything looks like it's from the future, but also at a yard sale. On the other hand, the prequel films were dominated by green screens with smooth 2,000 CGI, and had some strikingly sterile and plastic environments.
cues.zh: 有生活痕迹的样子。一切东西都像来自未来，但同时又像是旧货摊上淘来的。而另一方面，前传电影大量使用绿幕，配上那种丝滑的 2000 年代 CGI，呈现出了许多异常冰冷洁净、塑料感十足的环境。

cues.en: The sequel trilogy mostly went back to the nostalgic dingy sci fi aesthetic, but then we also had films like Solo showing space opulence.
cues.zh: 后传三部曲基本回归了那种怀旧做旧的科幻美学，但我们也看到了像《游侠索罗》这样展现太空奢华感的电影。

cues.en: And across all films, the villain's big star destroyers looked pretty slick and generically futuristic.
cues.zh: 而在所有系列电影中，反派那些巨大的歼星舰看起来都相当炫酷，充满常见的未来感。

cues.en: So given the breadth of aesthetics across the years of movies, I wouldn't necessarily call this environment un Star Wars. However, I do think that in even approaching the concept for this hotel, Imagineers ran into a problem. If you're charging luxury prices and offering luxury service, you want to build a luxurious environment.
cues.zh: 考虑到多年来电影中美学风格的多样性，我不至于说这个环境“不像星战”。不过我确实认为，在构思这家酒店的概念时，想象工程师们遇到了一个问题：既然你收取豪华的价格、提供豪华的服务，自然想打造一个豪华的环境。

cues.en: But in Star Wars, our heroes are primarily poor people.
cues.zh: 但在星战里，我们的主角大多都是穷人。

cues.en: In fact, the rich people are usually the bad guys. One choice I found interesting is that in story, the Halcyon is meant to be an extremely old luxury cruiser with a long legacy. So that's how they explain the high republic stylings of it. This is kind of like the Titanic of the Star Wars universe if it hadn't sunk. I just mean it's an old ship. I don't know. And I speculate that that was not only done to justify the aesthetic, but to also leave the ship open for reworked storylines. Imagine an alternate timeline where this was a smashing success and tons of people went to it, and after several years, everybody who wanted to do it had already seen it. Since canonically, the ship has existed for like the entire Star Wars timeline,
cues.zh: 事实上，有钱人通常是反派。我觉得有个设定挺有意思：在故事里，“哈尔西恩号”被设定成一艘有着悠久传承的极古老的豪华游轮。这样他们就能解释它那种高风险共和国时期的风格了。这有点像星战宇宙里的泰坦尼克号——只是没沉的那版。我的意思就是它是艘老船，我也说不清。我猜测这不仅仅是为了给美学风格一个说法，也是为了让这艘船便于日后重做故事线。想象一条平行时间线：这酒店大获成功，无数人蜂拥而至，几年之后，所有想体验的人都来过了。由于在正史设定中，这艘船几乎贯穿了整个星战时间线，

cues.en: they could just do a story overhaul every couple years, set it anywhere they wanted to, and not have to make any physical alterations to the building. So they could set it during the original trilogy. They could have new original characters,
cues.zh: 他们完全可以每隔几年就大改一次故事，把它设定在任何想要的年代，而且不用对建筑做任何物理改动。比如可以设定在正传三部曲期间，引入新的原创角色，

cues.en: Luke is running around, and then at the end he fights Darth Vader,
cues.zh: 卢克到处跑，最后和达斯·维达对决，

cues.en: or like Jabba the Hutt. Personally, I would prefer Jabba. And then they could wheel him out on like a big bicycle mounted puppet, like Ursula from the Little Mermaid show. He's like, oh, I'm here.
cues.zh: 或者换个赫特人贾巴。就我个人而言，我更想看贾巴。他们可以把他装到一个类似大型双人自行车式的木偶装置上推出来，就像《小美人鱼》音乐剧里的乌苏拉那样。他来一句：哦，我来啦。

cues.en: That's
cues.zh: 这

cues.en: not even what he sounds like. I just assumed that all of this was encompassed in the original pitch for the project, and it would have happened if it had existed long enough, but I guess now we'll never know. Anyway, through a pretty window at the front of the lobby, you can see into the bridge, which has the biggest space windows. So you can kind of see that view into space from the atrium, if it's not crowded or you're on that end of the room. The bridge was not open at all times. It was mostly locked, and then they would use it for scheduled story moments for smaller groups of guests at a time. But in the evenings, when the story was over, they left it open to guests. Are we allowed to just walk her in? Probably not, but we maybe we should... Should try. This is true. Thank
cues.zh: 根本不是他本来的声音嘛。我原本以为这一切都包含在项目最初的提案里，只要它运营得够久就总会实现，但现在恐怕永远没机会知道了。对了，透过大堂前方的漂亮舷窗，你能看到驾驶舱，那里有着最大的太空舷窗。所以从中庭多少也能瞥见太空的景色——前提是那里没挤满人，或者你恰好站在房间那一头。驾驶舱并非随时开放，大部分时间都锁着，他们只在安排好的故事环节里，让小批客人分批使用。不过在晚上，当天的故事结束后，他们会把它向客人开放。我们就这么直接走进去，可以吗？多半不行吧，但也许我们该……试试看。确实如此。谢

cues.en: you.
cues.zh: 谢。

cues.en: Punch it here.
cues.zh: 在这里按一下。

cues.zh: 这

cues.zh: 些游戏机都关着，所以那段时间里面没什么可玩的，不过可以四处看看，顺便拍照。

cues.en: This is really sickly.
cues.zh: 这看起来真病态。

cues.en: It's nice. I like it. Wanna try it? It's very, thin. Oh, yeah. Yeah. It's a good feel to it.
cues.zh: 不错，我喜欢。想试试吗？它很薄。哦，是啊，手感不错。

cues.en: Off the lobby is a gift shop full of entirely in universe items. During your lightsaber training, you'll wield a lightsaber of course. Mhmm. We also learned how to deflect laser blasts with a shield just like this. I was gonna say, can't deflect a lightsaber, Shirley.
cues.zh: 大厅旁边有家礼品店，卖的全是星战世界里的商品。参加光剑训练时，你当然会挥舞光剑。嗯。我们还学了怎么用盾牌挡开激光束，就像这个一样。我正想说呢，盾牌可挡不住光剑，Shirley。

cues.en: Just lasers? It's more for laser glass. Okay. Right? If you do a lightsaber, think it would need some protection right now. What is it made of? Is it fragile?
cues.zh: 只能挡激光吗？它主要是用来挡激光束的。好吧。对吧？要是用光剑，我觉得现在得有点防护。它是什么材料做的？容易坏吗？

cues.en: No. It's very... It's pretty durable. I should get this. It's plastic. It can travel. I thought the selection of souvenirs was pretty cool, although they had no plush, which I took personally. I love that the Halcyon aesthetic has everything in gold and silver and black and it has a cool logo. I was gonna say... I like this droid. What is Yeah. He's JD Siri, so... Will we see him? So our transports are driven by JDFA.
cues.zh: 不，很……挺耐用的。我应该买这个。它是塑料的，可以带走。我觉得纪念品的选择挺不错，不过他们居然没有毛绒玩具，我可记在心上了。我喜欢 Halcyon 的风格：各种金色、银色和黑色，还有很酷的标志。我刚想说……我喜欢这个机器人。这是……对，他叫 JD Siri，所以……我们会见到他吗？我们的交通工具是由 JDFA 驾驶的。

cues.en: Oh. So you might not see him, but you'll definitely hear him. Oh. Okay. They have all these in universe clothes and accessories you can buy and immediately wear during your stay. And the quality varied, but I liked the variety. I thought there were some really clever pieces. And personally, I think that in universe items, and especially wearables, are always my favorite merch for anything. They were sold out of a lot of stuff when I went though, so that's kinda sad. And I read online that that was pretty much the case the entire time they were open. They never had everything in stock, and that sucks, because you're probably only gonna go once. I'm certainly not gonna get anything else now. I should also mention that I got this big gigantic droid for like,
cues.zh: 哦，所以你可能见不到他，但肯定能听到他的声音。哦，好。他们卖各种星战世界里的服装和配饰，你买了就能在旅途中穿戴。不过品质参差不齐，但款式挺多，有些设计也很巧妙。我个人觉得，任何作品的周边里，世界观内的商品，尤其是能穿戴的，总是最合我心意。不过我去的时候，很多东西都卖光了，有点扫兴。我在网上看到，他们营业期间基本一直都是这样：商品从来没备齐过。挺糟的，因为你很可能只会去一次。我肯定不会再买其他东西了。我还得说，我买了这个超大号机器人，花了大概……

cues.en: I think like $200
cues.zh: 我记得差不多 200 美元，

cues.en: or something stupid. I don't wanna talk about it. He's my best friend, and I love him so much. Anyway, I used the Disney resort shipping service to send him home, which they heavily advertise everywhere, because he's really big and he wouldn't fit in my luggage. And I kept my receipt, so I know I wrote my own address down correctly,
cues.zh: 反正贵得离谱。不想提了。他是我最好的朋友，我超爱他。总之，我用迪士尼度假区的寄送服务把他寄回家了。他们到处都在大力宣传这项服务，因为机器人太大了，塞不进行李箱。我留着收据，所以确定自己写的地址没错，

cues.en: but I guess when they typed it into the computer to send it to the post office, they typed a totally different address, and my droid went missing. I called a couple different departments trying to ask where my droid went and what I could do about it, and they said that there was nothing that could be done. But then after I tweeted about it on my Twitter account with a lot of followers, Disney suddenly resolved it, and they sent me a replacement. They actually overnighted it to me. cues.en: But I do think it's handy to bring a memorable prop or accessory as a conversation piece. I like how I'm giving advice as if you're gonna book it. Part eight, the food. As on a real cruise, the food is included in the price, so it's all going to be free. Well, you've already paid. It's prepaid. The only refreshments that cost extra money are the alcoholic beverages,
cues.zh: 但我确实觉得带一个有记忆点的道具或配饰当话题引子挺有用的。看我这样，好像你们真会去订似的，还在这给建议。第八部分：食物。和真正的游轮一样，餐食是包含在票价里的，所以全都免费。嗯，其实你已经付过钱了，是预付的。唯一要额外花钱的饮品是酒精饮料，

cues.en: and they have some mocktails that cost money too. I know on some real cruises, the alcohol is free, but to my knowledge on every Disney cruise, it's not free. So this was kind of expected for me. I was frankly overwhelmed by the amount of food. They do a scheduled breakfast, lunch, and dinner, and every meal is all you can eat. Outside of meal times, the bar in the atrium also has a whole separate appetizer menu you can order from, and those are also all complimentary.
cues.zh: 另外还有些无酒精鸡尾酒也要收费。我知道有些真游轮上酒是免费的，但据我所知，迪士尼的所有游轮上酒都不免费，所以这在我意料之中。说实话，食物的量多得让我有点招架不住。早餐、午餐、晚餐都是定时供应，而且每一餐都随便吃到饱。非用餐时间，中庭的吧台还有一整份单独的小吃菜单可以点，这些也是全免费的。

cues.en: I loved this cloche filled with smoke, and then they lift it up and it's full of little cheese balls and crackers. They also leave out very simple snacks in the atrium between meals, like yogurt,
cues.zh: 我特别喜欢那个罩着烟雾的餐盖，他们一掀开，里面全是小芝士球和饼干。两餐之间，中庭还会摆放一些非常简单的小食，比如酸奶、

cues.en: fruit cups, parmesan crisps,
cues.zh: 水果杯、帕玛森脆片，

cues.en: and then like some child pleasers, like cake pops and goldfish crackers. I saw some haters online being like, wow, paying that much for goldfish crackers? And it's like, okay, guys, that's obviously for toddlers.
cues.zh: 还有一些专哄孩子的东西，比如棒棒糖蛋糕和小金鱼饼干。我在网上看到一些爱吐槽的人说，哇，花那么多钱就吃小金鱼饼干？我就想说，行了吧各位，那明显是给幼儿准备的。

cues.en: But yes, they have goldfish crackers.
cues.zh: 不过是的，他们确实有小金鱼饼干。

cues.en: I did actually eat a couple. But what I'm saying is you will not be hungry on this trip. It's impossible. The breakfasts and lunches are buffet style and they have these little space trays with squares and rectangles you can slot the food dishes onto. I saw some people complain about the tiny portions on these little plates and I don't understand that because it's a buffet. If you really like something, you can grab 10. But I liked that they were kind of sample sizes. It made it feel low commitment to try everything. They also have waiters wandering around to take drink orders at the buffet service meals. The dining room drinks menu is different from the lounge menu, but the waiters at meals can bring you anything from either menu. They can also bring you normal earth cocktails if you don't want any of the crazy themed stuff, but in my opinion, you went all the way to space. You should get the themed stuff. They have a soda fountain with all the soda logos in Arrabesh,
cues.zh: 我还真吃了几块。我想说的是，这趟旅程你绝不会饿肚子。根本不可能。早餐和午餐是自助餐形式，他们还有那种太空小托盘，上面有方形和长方形的凹槽，可以把菜盘卡上去。我看到有人抱怨这些小盘子分量太少，我不理解，因为这是自助餐啊。真喜欢哪个，拿十个都行。不过我倒是挺喜欢这种试吃份量，让人没有负担，什么都敢尝一口。自助餐时段还有服务员来回走动帮你点饮料。正餐餐厅的饮料单和休息室的不一样，但用餐时的服务员两边的酒水都能给你拿。如果你不想要那些花哨的主题饮品，他们也能给你上普通的地球鸡尾酒，不过要我说，你都大老远跑到太空了，就该点主题的。他们有一台汽水机，所有汽水logo都是奥里贝什语的，

cues.en: just like in the theme park land, and they also have blue and green milk on tap. In the parks, blue and green milk is like a frozen milkshake y texture, and because it's plant based, it separates a little when it melts, which I think is kind of gross. The Star Cruiser versions of the milk are the texture of milk. I'd compare it to like an Odd Walla smoothie, a drinkable yogurt. I don't really like frozen drinks, so I way preferred the Star Cruiser version. It's actually what I was hoping the theme park version would be. Flavor wise, they're the same as the parks. The blue is fruity and the green is floral. Everyone hates the green milk, but I personally like them both. The dinners are both table service and brought out in courses on platters for the table to share. I think not everybody realized this, but the table service dinners are also all you can eat. If you have a favorite item you finished off, can you ask your waiter to bring out a whole new plate of it, and they will. Also, I'm pretty sure the dessert at the first dinner was literally the same dessert you can buy in Pandora the World of Avatar.
cues.zh: 和主题园区里的一模一样，而且还有蓝奶和绿奶可以随取。在园区里，蓝奶和绿奶是类似冰沙的质地，因为是植物基的，融化后会有点分层，我觉得有点恶心。星际巡游号上的奶就是真正的牛奶质地。我可以把它比作 Odd Walla 思慕雪，一种可以喝的酸奶。我不太喜欢冰冻饮品，所以更喜欢星际巡游号的版本。这其实正是我原本期待园区版该有的样子。口味方面，和园区里的一样：蓝色的是果味，绿色的是花香。大家都讨厌绿奶，但我个人两种都喜欢。晚餐是桌边服务，菜品按道盛在托盘里端上来供全桌分享。我估计不是每个人都意识到了，但其实晚餐也是随便吃到饱的。如果你特别喜欢某道菜吃完了，可以让服务员再端一整盘来，他们真的会端。另外，我相当确定，第一晚晚餐的甜点，和潘朵拉·阿凡达世界园区里卖的就是同一款。

cues.en: and ultimately determines how your Star Wars story
cues.zh: 并最终决定你的星球大战故事

cues.en: unfolds.
cues.zh: 如何展开。

cues.en: And it's your story. That's right. It's your story. And live out all the different storylines. They get to choose who they wanna be loyal to. The story will depend on what you do. Choose your own path. As a passenger, you get to choose your own path. Do you join the resistance? Do you join the first order? Are you a scoundrel? There's a love story on board. Do you wanna help the light side of the force? Do you wanna tap into your dark side? You're going to invite guests to become the hero of their own Star Wars adventure,
cues.zh: 而且这是你的故事。没错，这是你的故事。去体验所有不同的剧情线。你可以选择自己效忠谁。故事将取决于你的所作所为。选择你自己的道路。作为乘客，你可以选择自己的路。你要加入抵抗组织吗？你要加入第一秩序吗？还是一个无赖流氓？船上有爱情故事线。你想帮助原力的光明面吗？还是想释放你内心的黑暗面？你将邀请宾客成为他们自己的星球大战冒险的主角，

cues.en: and you can do it in whatever way you like. Ad materials showed kids helping Chewbacca
cues.zh: 而且你可以用自己喜欢的任何方式来玩。宣传材料里展示了小孩帮助丘巴卡，

cues.en: or snitching Chewbacca out to the cops and getting him arrested. The possibilities are endless. That was probably the most advertised aspect of the experience, that you would choose between a number of branching paths. As it got closer to launch, it became clearer what those paths were going to be. First order, resistance or smuggler. I've seen some people say Jedi was also a path and I would argue that it was not. You could unlock a couple Jedi scenes, but they were tangential to whatever main path you were already on. They weren't their own story track. So first, I'm going to tell you how all this is supposed to work to the best of my knowledge. The gameplay is actually split into two halves, actor based gameplay
cues.zh: 或者把丘巴卡举报给警察让他被抓走。可能性是无穷的。这大概是整个体验宣传最多的卖点：你可以在多条分支路径中做选择。随着开业临近，这些路径也越来越清晰：第一秩序、抵抗组织或者走私客。我看到有人说绝地也是一条路径，但我认为并不是。你可以解锁几个绝地场景，但它们只是附属于你已经选择的主线，并不是独立的故事线。那么首先，根据我掌握的信息，我来告诉大家这一切本应是如何运作的。玩法其实分成两部分：基于演员的玩法

cues.en: and app based gameplay. The small cast of actors are the NPCs for this experience, the non player characters. Each individual character has their own schedule set in stone, and then there is a corresponding seemingly algorithm driven app working in tandem with the human performers, which is why this schedule is so important. The same computer program that's organizing the actors is also guiding the itinerary of the hotel guests. You can interact with the characters in person, but you also use the app to receive text messages from them. So obviously, these texts aren't really coming from the actor, they're from the app, And you can reply with a menu of choices from a dialogue tree to get pre written answers. In this way, you can build affiliations with the different characters, which theoretically sets you on one of the available story paths. I feel like my viewers know that whenever I use the word theoretical,
cues.zh: 和基于 App 的玩法。一小批演员就是这个体验中的 NPC，也就是非玩家角色。每个角色都有自己固定不变的日程表，而与之配合的是一个看似由算法驱动的 App，与真人演员协同运作，这也是这份日程表如此重要的原因。同一个编排演员行程的电脑程序，也在引导酒店旅客的行程。你可以当面与角色互动，同时也可以通过 App 收到他们发来的短信。显然，这些短信并不是演员本人发的，而是来自 App。你可以通过对话树里的一组选项进行回复，得到预先写好的答案。通过这种方式，你可以和不同角色建立关系，理论上这会把你引向某一条可选的故事线。我觉得我的观众都知道，每当我说出“理论上”这个词，

cues.en: things are about to take a turn. This information has not been publicly released, but allegedly the actors have some way of syncing real time to the data in the app. Allegedly, this may be done via earpieces.
cues.zh: 事情就要有转折了。这些信息并未公开发布，但据称演员有某种方式可以实时同步 App 里的数据。据称，这可能是通过耳机实现的。

cues.en: I said earlier that all the guests are wearing these little wristbands with RFID chips. So allegedly, the characters all have proximity readers wired into their clothing. When you approach them, their reader detects your bracelet, identifies your profile in the app, and then their earpiece can feed them information about you. So we don't know exactly what would be said in these alleged earpieces, but for example, maybe it says trust level, hi, and then the actor knows to greet you warmly. They could even use this tech to remind the actors of your name if they wanted to. The proximity readers could also theoretically send data back to the app. If you spent a long time interacting with a particular character, that would boost your trust score with them and impact your story path. So let's say you've been texting a lot in the app with the AI version of the First Order General. The AI can ask you if you want to help him in his mission. You can say yes. The app can assign you tasks that don't require any actor involvement, like check that computer terminal for me, and then track whether you fulfill these tasks. The app knows the actor's schedules, so the AI version of the general can text you, meet me in the atrium at 04:30, knowing that the actor will actually be there at that time. Then when you see the actor, his earpiece tells him, name, Jenny, trust level, 80%.
cues.zh: 我之前说过，所有嘉宾都戴着带有 RFID 芯片的小手环。据说，这些角色演员的服装里都装了近距离读卡器。当你靠近他们时，读卡器会检测到你的手环，在应用里识别出你的资料，然后他们的耳机就能收到关于你的信息。我们并不知道这些据传的耳机里具体会播报什么，但比如说，可能会说“信任等级，高”，然后演员就知道要热情地跟你打招呼。他们甚至可以用这项技术提醒演员你的名字。理论上，近距离读卡器还可以把数据回传给应用。如果你和某个角色互动了很长时间，这会提升你对该角色的信任分数，并影响你的剧情路线。假设你在应用里和 AI 版的第一秩序将军发了很多消息。AI 可以问你想不想帮他完成任务。你可以答应。应用可以给你分配一些不需要演员参与的任务，比如“帮我查一下那个电脑终端”，然后追踪你是否完成了这些任务。应用掌握着演员的日程表，所以 AI 版将军可以给你发消息说“四点半在中庭见”，因为他知道演员到时候确实会在那里。等你见到演员时，他的耳机里会提示：名字，珍妮，信任等级，80%。

cues.en: And then the actor knows to say, oh, Jenny, you've been very helpful to me, well done. Thus marrying the two halves of the gameplay in a way that feels seamless on the user end. From there, the characters you've been loyal to can pull you into unique in person story moments to involve you further. Oh, here's me tricking some storm troopers into going into the brig, so that we could block them inside.
cues.zh: 然后演员就知道该说：“哦，珍妮，你帮了我大忙，干得好。”这样就以一种让用户感觉无缝衔接的方式，把游戏玩法的两个部分结合在了一起。接下来，你一直效忠的角色可以把你拉进一些独特的线下剧情时刻，让你更深入地参与其中。哦，这段是我骗几个风暴兵进了禁闭室，然后把他们锁在里面。

cues.en: Day one schedule is already programmed in for you before you arrive. You'll have training on the bridge, lightsaber training, and be seated for one of two possible dinner times. And in between those activities, you're meant to be utilizing the app and talking with the AI versions of the characters.
cues.zh: 第一天的日程在你到达之前就已经安排好了。你会参加舰桥训练、光剑训练，并被安排到两个晚餐时段中的一个。而在这些活动之间，你应该使用应用，和 AI 版的角色聊天。

cues.en: You may also have interactions with the actors while doing so. At the end of day one, the app checks all your loyalty scores to figure out which story path you're on. It then uses that information to create your day two schedule, which is more personalized and storyline specific. So when you wake up, you'll see that you already have mission assignments waiting for you for the side you're affiliated with, and you'll also be putting corresponding story scenes. So for example, if you're on the first order side, you might be asked to locate contraband cargo
cues.zh: 在此过程中，你也可能和演员有互动。第一天结束时，应用会检查你所有的忠诚度分数，判断你处在哪条剧情路线上。然后用这些信息生成你第二天的日程，更加个性化，也更贴合剧情。所以当你醒来时，你会看到你所属阵营已经给你派发了任务，你还会看到相应的剧情场景。比如说，如果你站在第一秩序这边，你可能会被要求找到违禁货物，

cues.en: and then be dropped into a couple First Order cut scenes and maybe they even mention the cargo as a reward for the task you completed. Or maybe you'll get invited to a meeting with the storm troopers or see the general get a call from the supreme leader or something like that. Something that makes you feel more directly involved with the story. I imagine there are probably five or six possible cut scenes running for each story path, so the app just schedules you into,
cues.zh: 然后被带入几个第一秩序的过场动画，说不定里面甚至会提到那份货物，作为你完成任务的奖励。或者你可能会被邀请参加风暴兵的会议，或者看到将军接到最高领袖的电话之类的。就是那种让你感觉自己更直接地参与到剧情中的东西。我估计每条剧情路线大概有五六个备选的过场动画，应用只是把你安排进其中，

cues.en: let's say, two of those per person. Then everyone gets the same finale, which is a big performance in the atrium and wraps up all the story threads. And if you've been a particularly proactive player, there are moments when the actors can shout you out by name integrated into the finale. That all sounds conceptually very clever. And if it works, sounds like a pretty fun experience, right? I think so too. Part 10, living my Star Wars story. Okay. So I'm going to be frank, the gameplay did not work for us at all. At some point, there was some kind of critical logistical failure, which broke every aspect of it. I was continually frustrated the entire time I was there, and I left extremely disappointed. In our particular experience, none of the actions we took at any point directed the course of our story in any way. And I have guesses as to how that happened, but I'm gonna get to that later. So
cues.zh: 比如每人分配到两个。然后所有人都会迎来相同的结局：一场在中庭举行的大型演出，收束所有的故事线。如果你是个特别积极的玩家，结局演出里还会有些环节，演员可以点到你的名字。这些在概念上听起来都非常巧妙。如果运作良好的话，听起来会是很棒的体验，对吧？我也这么觉得。第 10 部分，体验我的星球大战故事。好吧。说实话，这个游戏玩法在我们身上完全没跑通。在某个时间点，出现了某种关键的流程性故障，把它的方方面面全都搞崩了。我在那里的整个过程中一直很沮丧，离开时也极其失望。就我们的经历而言，我们采取的任何行动在任何时候都没有以任何方式影响我们故事的走向。我对原因有一些猜测，但稍后再讲。那么，

cues.en: here's how it went for us. I knew going in that I wanted to pick one story path, because that would be the best way to gauge how well the experience works.
cues.zh: 接下来讲讲我们的经历。去之前我就打定主意要选一条剧情路线，因为这是检验这套体验到底行不行最好的方式。

cues.en: They say it's a choose your own adventure, so I would attempt to choose. A while before the trip, I decided that I was pretty set on getting First Order, because it had been met with the most skepticism as a story path. And also, Disney is a family experience and presumably motivated not to have a losing team, so I was very curious how they would handle a villain side of the story. So at first when they turned us loose in the ship, I had no idea what to do with myself. They don't really give you any guidance, which I was initially optimistic about because I'm a pretty big escape room enthusiast,
cues.zh: 他们说这是一个“选择你自己的冒险”故事，所以我就想试着自己做选择。出发前一阵子，我就打定主意要加入 First Order，因为这条故事线最受质疑。而且，Disney 是一种家庭体验，想必不希望任何一方落败，所以我特别好奇他们会怎么处理反派阵营的故事。刚开始他们让我们在飞船里自由行动时，我完全不知道该做什么。他们基本没给任何指引。一开始我还挺乐观的，因为我很喜欢密室逃脱，

cues.en: and you're pretty much always dropped into those cold, and then you just figure out what you're supposed to do through environmental clues. I figured they would probably be using the RFID bracelets as part of the gameplay,
cues.zh: 大家几乎都是直接被丢进去，然后靠环境线索摸索该做什么。我猜他们可能会把 RFID 手环融入游戏，

cues.en: and I envisioned there being loads of like, tap points that you have to hunt for. So like, maybe if you tapped a panel in the captain's area, you could download a secret file, or you could tap a touch pad next to an item to add that item to your inventory, and then you could use it later. So I guess I was envisioning something like a point and click adventure game, but in real life.
cues.zh: 我还想象着会有很多感应点，得由你自己去找。比如，在舰长室里感应一下某块面板，就能下载一份秘密文件；或者在某件物品旁的触控板上感应一下，就能把它加入物品栏，之后再派上用场。所以我想象的应该有点像现实版的点击式冒险游戏。

cues.en: We found another purple sea urchin.
cues.zh: 我们又发现了一只紫色海胆。

cues.en: You know, like the NPCs ask you to fetch something for them, and then you explore a ship full of set dressing details and Easter eggs. Maybe you see an access card glued to a table, tap your band on it to collect it, and then you gain the ability to open a new door. Or you read a clue in a memo posted on a wall, and then text the code word to the proper character in the app, and then they give you your next task. Through that, I feel you could have some sense of discovery and forward momentum. I'm picturing something like, you need the kyber crystal, but it fell in a crate with the alien frog monster and he's guarding it. You'll need to get the droid parts to trade for the Jogen fruit to distract the alien. And then once you've collected the Jogen fruit by tapping your band on it, you tap your band next to the frog's cage, the little frog animatronic wiggles around and makes eating sounds, and it backs away from a prop of a kyber crystal, which you can see through the bars of the cage, and then the app is like, you got the crystal.
cues.zh: 你知道的，就像 NPC 会让你帮忙找东西，然后你在一艘满是布景细节和彩蛋的飞船里四处探索。也许你会看到桌上粘着一张门禁卡，用手环感应一下就能收集起来，然后就可以打开一扇新门。或者你读到墙上贴的备忘录里的线索，再在应用里把暗号发给正确的角色，对方就会给你下一个任务。我觉得这样一来，你就能感受到探索的乐趣，也知道自己在逐步推进故事。我想象的情节可能是：你需要凯伯水晶，但它掉进了一个箱子里，里面有只外星青蛙怪物守着它。你得先找到机器人零件，拿去换约根果，好引开那只外星生物。等你用手环感应约根果、把它收集起来后，再把手环靠近青蛙的笼子，小青蛙机械装置就会扭动起来，发出吃东西的声音，然后它会从笼子里的凯伯水晶道具旁退开。你隔着栏杆能看见水晶，接着应用就会提示你：“你拿到水晶了。”

cues.en: Sorry, Skippy heard me saying the name of his favorite snack.
cues.zh: 抱歉，Skippy 听见我说了它最爱吃的零食。

cues.zh: 我只好去给它拿了一份。我觉得我说的这种玩法，也能让游客之间更愿意互相合作。你们在帮 Sasa 吗？找到机器人的处理器了吗？

cues.en: Sure, friend. It's over here.
cues.zh: 当然，朋友。就在这边。

cues.zh: 他们走路就那样。但不对，玩法里没有那种东西。他们确实有个物品收集机制，

You'll scan one and the app will present you with a rudimentary puzzle. Then when you solve it, it'll be like, there's a hyperdrive in this crate. And superficially, the hyperdrive will be added to the inventory in your profile. You can't do anything with it, so
cues.zh: 我的天。哦天。我的天。基本上，它只让你扫描散落在 Star Wars 园区各处的箱子上的二维码。等等，货箱可太多了。有太多东西可以扫。你扫一个，app 就会给你一个很简单的谜题。然后你解开后，它会显示：这个箱子里有个超空间驱动器。表面上看，超空间驱动器会被加到个人资料里的物品栏。你没法拿它做任何事，所以

You just don't see it because I edit around it. Okay. Anyway, moving on. You tap your band first to begin utilizing a terminal, which at first seemed promising. cues.zh: 他直接玩消失。太尴尬了。

cues.en: While we were eating dinner on night one, Lindsay did receive a text in the app from lieutenant Croix asking her to go to the Engineering Room right away and scan some schematic for him or something. Obviously, we couldn't at that moment, because we were eating a formal multi course dinner with a show, theoretically. And in my opinion, it's a little weird the app sent us that, because like, the app knew we were at dinner, right? Like the dinner was at a specific time and for a set duration,
cues.zh: 第一晚我们吃晚餐时，Lindsay 确实在 App 里收到 Croix 中尉的消息，让她马上去工程室，帮他扫描某张图纸之类的。显然我们当时去不了，因为理论上我们正在吃一顿有表演的正式多道菜晚餐。而且我觉得 App 给我们发这个有点奇怪，因为 App 知道我们在吃晚餐，对吧？晚餐有特定时间、固定时长，

cues.en: and that was loaded into the schedule before anything else. But I figured maybe that meant the task wasn't time sensitive and we would just go when we got the chance. In the middle of the dinner show, Sammy showed up with Chewbacca trying to smuggle him across the dining room without the first order noticing. This was our first direct encounter with Sammy. When he reached our table, we tried to get in his way and get lieutenant Croix's attention. Is that the movie award? No. This is just a a normal movie named Tom. He's just... My god. I'm so scary. Nigel, it's okay. Don't don't be scared. He and Chewbacca did get caught, which was obviously a prescripted event that happens on every cruise, but it's the thought that counts. Sorry, I know my footage isn't very good, but Chewbacca is getting arrested behind that pole. Then when our check came, the waiter was like, it looks like there's something extra with your check. And it was a torn up piece of a secret message, which was very exciting. We realized that the two tables next to us also received pieces of the message, and I thought we'd have to put all our pieces together to get the message, which would be a fun bit of cooperative play. But when we put them together, we realized that it was unnecessary because they all contained equivalent information. I also looked around the room and I think I saw at least one other trio of tables that got these notes. For all I know, everybody got them, or maybe people got different ones from different characters. The secret message turned out to be weirdly from Sammy. He was like, meet me at 09:40PM
cues.zh: 而这些早就被排进日程里了。但我想，也许这说明任务不赶时间，我们有空再去就行。晚餐表演进行到一半，Sammy 带着楚巴卡出现了，想趁第一秩序没注意，把他偷偷带过餐厅。这是我们第一次直接遇到 Sammy。他到我们桌边时，我们试着挡住他，并引起 Croix 中尉的注意。那是电影奖吗？不，这只是一部叫 Tom 的普通电影。他只是……天啊，我好害怕。Nigel，没事的。别、别害怕。他和楚巴卡确实被抓了，这显然是每趟航程都会发生的剧本事件，但心意到了。抱歉，我知道我的录像不太好，但楚巴卡正在那根柱子后面被抓。后来账单送来时，服务员说：看起来你们的账单里多了点东西。那是一张撕碎的密信碎片，特别让人兴奋。我们发现旁边两桌也收到了密信碎片，我以为得把所有碎片拼起来才能得到信息，这会是个有趣的合作玩法。但拼起来后，我们发现没必要，因为每张都包含同等信息。我还环顾了房间，我觉得至少还看到另一组三张桌子也拿到了这些纸条。据我所知，可能所有人都拿到了，或者大家从不同角色那里拿到了不同的。那封密信居然来自 Sammy。他说：晚上 9:40

cues.en: in the atrium. I'm trying to get Chewbacca out of jail and I need your help. And I'm like, our help? We're the ones that got you into this mess. Clearly, we had been put on the resistance path, which made no sense. But frankly, after an evening of non starters, I was just happy to have any task at all, and it sounded like we were getting some kind of exclusive story moment, so of course, we decided we should go. But when the time came, on our way to the atrium to meet Sammy, who should we run into in the stairwell but Chewbacca,
cues.zh: 在中庭见我。我想把楚巴卡弄出监狱，我需要你们帮忙。我就想，我们帮忙？明明是我们把你害成这样的。显然我们被安排到了抵抗组织路线，这完全说不通。但说实话，在一晚上都没什么实质进展之后，只要能有个任务我就很高兴了，而且听起来像是某种独家剧情时刻，所以我们当然决定要去。但到了时间，我们正去中庭见 Sammy，结果在楼梯间撞见了谁？楚巴卡，

cues.en: already walking around free and a gaggle of kids around him. I'm not sure if they handed out dozens of those secret notes, or if this was just the crowd of kids that always follows Sammy around. According to my footage's metadata, this clip was filmed three minutes before the time we were supposed to meet Sammy in the atrium.
cues.zh: 已经自由自在地走动，身边围着一群孩子。我不确定他们是发了几十张那种秘密纸条，还是说这只是一直跟着 Sammy 的那群孩子。根据我录像的元数据，这段视频是在我们约定去中庭见 Sammy 的时间前三分钟拍的。

cues.en: So we weren't super early, but we wouldn't have been late. So I don't know what happened with Chewbacca. I guess they started early or something. Honestly, it must have been pretty early, because like, he had been in the brig downstairs.
cues.zh: 所以我们不算特别早，但也不算晚。我不知道楚巴卡那边是怎么回事，估计他们提前开始了还是怎么的。说实话，肯定相当早，因为他还待在楼下的禁闭室里呢。

cues.en: We were gonna meet in the atrium, all walk down to the brig, get him out.
cues.zh: 我们本来约在中庭碰面，然后一起走到禁闭室，把他放出来。

cues.en: But when we saw him, he was coming down the stairs, which means at some point, he had already been broken out of the brig, gone up to the atrium, and was now descending again.
cues.zh: 但当我们见到他的时候，他已经从楼梯上走下来了，这说明在某个时间点，他已经被人从禁闭室里放出来了，上到中庭，然后又开始往下走。

cues.en: And presumably in that time, a meeting happened to discuss how they were gonna break Chewbacca out. So like, what, did they start forty minutes early? But anyway, it seemed like the exciting part was already over. And And it was so crowded, we had no hope of getting a word with anybody anyway. So we just headed out, no big deal. I guess we weren't even trying to get that storyline. It just would have been nice to do something. Next, we decided to try following up on that text we had gotten during dinner from Kroy. So we went back downstairs to the Engineering Bay to scan the thing that he wanted. When we got there, we were really surprised to see that the Kroy actor was actually physically there. I'm immediately optimistic that this is going to put us in some story moment. So I'm just like, Chewbacca is walking free. I'm sorry, I never like Chewbacca, I have no reason to keep his secrets. But Croia's just like, why should I trust you? You saw him in the frig, and then he was walking around. It was the weirdest thing.
cues.zh: 而且可以推测，这期间还开了个会，讨论怎么把楚巴卡救出来。所以怎么说，他们提前了四十分钟开始？不过总之，精彩的部分好像已经结束了。而且人特别多，我们根本没希望跟任何人搭上一句话。所以我们直接就走出来了，没什么大不了的。其实我们本来也没想追这条故事线，只是能做点什么就好了。接下来，我们决定去跟进晚饭时收到的那条克罗伊（Kroy）发来的短信。于是我们又回到楼下的工程舱，去扫描他要求的东西。到了那儿，我们非常惊讶地发现，克罗伊的演员本人居然真的在那里。我立刻就乐观起来，觉得这会让我们进入某个剧情时刻。所以我直接就说，楚巴卡自由了。抱歉，我从来就不喜欢楚巴卡，我没理由替他保守秘密。但克罗伊就回了句，我凭什么信你？你亲眼看到他被关在禁闭室，然后他又在外面闲逛。这事真是诡异极了。

cues.en: I see, I see. You've come you've come here to to further the cause of the enemies who've been trying to run me around the houses. Oh. No. I I... We we really saw it. But
cues.zh: 我明白了，我明白了。你是到这里来给那些一直把我耍得团团转的敌人助纣为虐的。哦。不，不……我们真的看到了。可是……

cues.en: you will not get one around me this time. Wow. And like, come on dude, we're on your side. But obviously, the actor doesn't know that. It's not really his fault. And obviously, he hasn't got a job for us. I figured at the time, maybe the actors just aren't fully aware what's going on in the app, but whatever. We can at least do what the AI version of Croix wanted from us. Neither of us remembered exactly what that entailed, so I asked Lindsay to look at the app again. But when she pulled open her text thread with Croix, the text in question had actually been deleted. What should we do? What was the task in the app for you? Yeah. I have to pull that up.
cues.zh: 这次你休想再糊弄我。哇。我心想，拜托老兄，我们是你这边的啊。但显然，演员并不知道这一点。这也真不怪他。显然，他也不会给我们安排任务了。我当时猜想，可能演员们并不完全清楚应用里发生了什么，但无所谓。至少我们可以做 AI 版克罗伊要求我们做的事。我们俩都不记得那具体是要干什么了，所以我让林赛（Lindsay）再看看那个应用。但她打开和克罗伊的短信对话时，那条短信居然已经被删除了。我们该怎么办？应用里给你的任务是什么？是啊，我得把它翻出来看看。

cues.en: It's
cues.zh: 这

cues.en: weird because it kinda like, I think it like... Maybe
cues.zh: 很奇怪，因为有点像是，我觉得好像是……也许

cues.en: it's because we took too long to act on it, but if that mattered, why would it have sent it to us in the middle of a dinner that it knew we were at? Isn't that the whole point of the micromanaged
cues.zh: 是因为我们行动得太慢了，但如果这真的有影响，那它为什么偏偏要挑我们正在吃晚饭的时候把短信发给我们？这不就是那个被严格管控的

cues.en: schedule and the app and everything?
cues.zh: 日程表和应用这一整套东西的意义所在吗？

cues.en: So why would it have given us that task if it knew we couldn't complete it in time? I think that's probably another clue that the technology was not working as it should. So with nothing to do, we poked around a little in the engineering day and then we got bored and we left. We should do these, whatever they are. Oh, wait. We did... We'll do something.
cues.zh: 那么，如果它明知我们来不及完成，为什么还要给我们这个任务呢？我觉得这大概又是一个线索，说明这项技术运行得不太对劲。所以闲着没事，我们在工程区里瞎转了一会儿，然后就觉得无聊走了。我们应该做这些事，管它们是什么呢。哦，等等。我们做了……我们来做点什么吧。

cues.en: I really felt like I couldn't catch a break all day. Mind you, at this point, the $6,000
cues.zh: 我真觉得自己一整天都没顺过。要知道，到这个时候，这6000美元的

cues.en: experience was already half over and I felt like I hadn't even been able to dip my toes into the story,
cues.zh: 体验已经过半了，而我感觉自己连故事的边都还没摸到，

cues.en: just thwarted at every turn. Even watching back my footage now is second hand frustrating, because I so viscerally remember spending the whole day so badly wanting to engage with the game I had been promised,
cues.zh: 处处碰壁。现在回看我的录像都觉得替自己着急，因为我太清楚地记得，那一天我迫切地想投入到那个向我承诺过的游戏里，

cues.en: and not being able to. Like I said, I had hoped to be First Order, but really I'd been prepared to say yes to anything a character asked me. But obviously, I hadn't been given anything to say yes to. And whenever I thought I was being given an intro into some plot thread, it didn't work out for one reason or another. Not only did I feel like I was barred from participating, I was even barred from watching by a literal bar. After the characters went to bed and we returned to our room, Lindsay noticed that in the app, there's a tab with all the different characters.
cues.zh: 却始终做不到。就像我说的，我本来希望能加入第一军团，但其实只要角色开口求我做什么，我都准备答应。可很明显，根本没人给我任何可以答应的机会。每当我以为某个剧情线索要展开了，总会因为这样那样的原因落空。我不仅觉得自己被挡在参与之外，甚至还被一条货真价实的栏杆挡在了观看之外。角色们去睡觉、我们回到房间之后，Lindsay注意到应用里有一个标签页，列出了所有不同的角色。

cues.en: It tracks how familiar they are with you and how much they trust you. So I would imagine it's scored based on how long you spend interacting with them in person and in the app, and then whether you respond to them positively or negatively. And this screen really explained the day I was having. Okay. So mine looked like this. You'll notice that my trust score with literally every character was neutral.
cues.zh: 它会追踪他们对你有多熟悉、有多信任你。我猜这个分数是基于你与他们面对面和在应用里互动的时长，以及你对他们回应的积极或消极程度来计算的。而这个界面正好解释了我这一天的遭遇。好。我的界面是这样的。你会注意到，我和每一个角色的信任分数都是中立。

cues.en: So despite my best efforts, it was basically as if I hadn't been playing at all. Okay. Now, let's look at my familiarity scores, which are even more interesting to me. Lanca Mach and Wraith Cole look about right. They both say low familiarity.
cues.zh: 所以尽管我使出了浑身解数，效果基本上就像我根本没玩过一样。好。现在来看我的熟悉度分数，这个更有意思。Lanca Mach和Wraith Cole看起来还算合理。都显示低熟悉度。

cues.en: I was briefly greeted by Lanca Mach and I never spoke to Wraith Cole at all. So that makes sense to me. Sasha says medium familiarity,
cues.zh: Lanca Mach只是短暂地跟我打了个招呼，而Wraith Cole我压根没跟他说过话。所以这说得通。Sasha显示中等熟悉度，

cues.en: and I only met her once at lightsaber training, but she did ask me my name and interact with me a couple times. So okay. I guess that feels medium. But lieutenant Kroy also says medium, even though I've been trying to talk to him all day, both on the app and in person. And there was that time I pledged my loyalty to him and he left me on red. My familiarity with Sammy was high,
cues.zh: 我只在光剑训练时见过她一次，但她确实问了我的名字，还跟我互动过几次。所以行吧，中等还算合理。但Kroy中尉也显示中等，尽管我一整天都在努力跟他搭话，在应用里和当面都有。而且我还向他宣誓效忠过，结果他把我晾在那儿。我和Sammy的熟悉度是高，

cues.en: even though I hadn't exchanged words with him ever at any point. Meanwhile, my familiarity score with Captain Keevan was low, even though I'd made pleasant small talk with her at least three separate times that day. In the app, the AI version of Captain Keevan actually sent me a text that night saying, sorry, I know we haven't gotten much time together today,
cues.zh: 尽管我们从始至终没说过一句话。与此同时，我和Keevan队长的熟悉度却是低，尽管那天我至少和她愉快地闲聊过三次。当晚，应用里的AI版Keevan队长还真给我发了条短信，说：抱歉，我知道我们今天没怎么有时间相处，

cues.en: but yes, we have.
cues.zh: 但有的，我们明明有。

cues.en: What's going on here? When we woke up on day two and it had given us all our missions, we had a few different options. We had texts from Sammy, captain Keevan,
cues.zh: 这是怎么回事？第二天醒来，它给我们所有人都派发了任务，我们有几个不同选择。我们收到了 Sammy、Keevan 队长发来的消息，

cues.en: and Sasha. And you'll notice that not only do those missions not line up with how I'd been trying to play out the story, they don't even really make sense with my stats in the app. At that point, we just had to surrender ourselves to the idea that nothing in the story was going to make sense, and try to invest ourselves in the path we had been arbitrarily placed onto for the time we had left. Okay. So why did this happen?
cues.zh: 还有 Sasha。你会发现，这些任务不仅跟我一直想推进的剧情对不上，甚至跟我在应用里的数据也根本说不通。到那时，我们只能接受：故事里的一切都不会合理，只能在剩下的时间里，尽量投入到我们被随意安排到的这条路径上。好，那为什么会这样？

cues.en: What broke? I have a few guesses. Scenario one, the gameplay didn't actually work at all for anyone, and it was a big scam. You're all just assigned to a story path at random. With only three major story threads, it's possible that for some guests, their story path would match up with the actions they're taking by pure coincidence. The broken clock being right twice a day kind of thing. Confirmation bias would then convince them that the story was a direct result of their actions. They get a message from the resistance and say, wow, that must be because I told Captain Keevan I was a fan of Princess Leia. But in actuality, it's just what would have happened anyway, predetermined by an algorithm. That would be obviously pretty bad. I have seen other guests with the same feedback as me, that they consciously tried to get one specific path, and it didn't work at all, and they left disappointed. But I don't have like statistical data on how often this occurred, and I highly doubt Disney will ever release that information,
cues.zh: 哪里出了问题？我有几种猜测。情景一，游戏玩法对所有人其实根本不起作用，完全是个大骗局。所有人都是被随机分配一条故事线。既然只有三条主要故事线，那么对某些游客来说，他们的故事线可能纯属巧合地跟他们采取的行动吻合。就像坏掉的钟一天也会准两次。确认偏误就会让他们相信，故事是他们行动的直接结果。他们收到抵抗组织发来的消息，然后说：哇，那一定是因为我告诉过 Keevan 队长我是 Princess Leia 的粉丝。但实际上，那本来就是注定会发生的，是算法预先决定的。这显然会非常糟糕。我见过其他游客给出和我一样的反馈：他们有意识地想走某条特定路线，结果完全没用，最后失望离开。但我没有这类情况发生频率的统计数据，而且我非常怀疑 Disney 会公开这个信息，

cues.en: if they even tracked it at all. So it's impossible to really know. But I think if this problem was more widespread, it would have become more apparent, so I'm going to charitably rule this one out. Scenario two, the gameplay worked for the majority of guests, but each story path had a finite number of players it could accommodate,
cues.zh: 前提是他们真的追踪过。所以根本无法确定。但我觉得，如果这个问题更普遍，应该会更明显，所以我愿意善意地排除这一种。情景二，游戏玩法对大多数游客有效，但每条故事线能容纳的玩家数量有限，

cues.en: and so the algorithm was trained to move some players into open slots in the schedule, regardless of their story choices. The idea here is that we were just the sacrificial lambs of our trip shuffled into open spots to maintain even distribution of guests across all story scenes at the expense of our own experience,
cues.zh: 于是算法被训练成把一些玩家挪到日程里的空位，不管他们选了什么故事。这个推测的意思是，我们只是这次旅行中的牺牲品，被塞进空位，以牺牲我们自己的体验为代价，维持所有故事场景中游客人数的均匀分布，

cues.en: but facilitating
cues.zh: 但只是为了促成

cues.en: other people's choose your own adventure gameplay. The idea of this one makes me so angry. Like, I would be so upset if I found out that at this price point, they were knowingly sacrificing the interactivity for some unlucky guests just to keep the game running smoothly. But to be honest, I wouldn't be surprised at all to find out that this was the case, especially considering they designed the dining room so that some unlucky tables were behind poles. Scenario three, random glitch. It worked for some people, it didn't work for other people, Bad luck, etcetera. This is my main theory. It coincides really well with what I've heard about the way the app worked in tandem with the actors. I mean, I showed you our loyalty scores, and it certainly appears that ours wasn't tracking anything we did at all. The designers probably programmed in some kind of grandma mode, where a guest who doesn't participate in the gameplay at all and just sleeps in the room all day is randomly assigned a story path in case they wanna play later. It seems to me like whatever actions we took in the app or in person, the system just wasn't registering it ever. So maybe the app saw a lack of data, put us in grandma mode, and then randomly put us on the resistance path. I don't know how such a critical failure could happen, and honestly, this one makes me pretty mad to think about too. Like for an experience that's so dependent on an app, glitches do feel inevitable. To be honest, anyone who's familiar with Disney parks will know that they're extremely bad at building apps and always have tons of glitches. But in the theme parks, the apps just determine whether you can get through the turnstiles in a timely fashion,
cues.zh: 别人的“自选冒险”玩法。这个推测让我非常愤怒。比如，如果我发现，在这个价位上，他们为了让游戏顺利运行，明知故犯地牺牲一些倒霉游客的互动性，我会特别难过。但说实话，如果发现真是这样，我一点也不会惊讶，尤其考虑到他们把餐厅设计成有些倒霉的桌子在柱子后面。情景三，随机故障。对一些人有效，对另一些人无效，运气不好，等等。这是我的主要理论。它跟我听说的应用与演员配合运作的方式非常吻合。我是说，我给你们看过我们的忠诚度分数，显然我们的分数根本没有记录我们做过的任何事。设计师可能编了某种“奶奶模式”：一个完全不参与玩法、整天在房间里睡觉的游客，会被随机分配一条故事线，以防他之后想玩。在我看来，不管我们在应用里还是现场做了什么，系统似乎从来都没记录下来。所以也许应用看到数据不足，把我们放进了奶奶模式，然后随机把我们放到了抵抗组织路线上。我不知道这种严重故障怎么会发生，老实说，想到这一点我也很生气。对于一个如此依赖应用体验的项目来说，故障确实感觉不可避免。说实话，熟悉 Disney 乐园的人都知道，他们做应用非常糟糕，总是有大量故障。但在主题乐园里，应用只决定你能不能及时通过闸机，

cues.en: or if you can book your next fast pass. On the Star Cruiser, the app determines whether your $6,000
