The resistance starts to analyze the hyperspace tracking system. They can they can find a way to defeat it. Yeah. So with all this in mind, it's fine. People who do it will like it well enough. I don't think it's much to write home about, but it was a fine enough gameplay element for this kind of experience. And for my sister and I, it was pretty much the only time we got to participate in the story, so we were just excited to be doing something. Okay. Next, we'll look at lightsabers.
cues.zh:
比你在手机上能玩到的任何东西都原始。  
要是把这个玩法直接搬进 Dave and Buster's 的街机柜里，根本没人想玩。  
但很明显，他们给它包装了一番。  
你身处一间很酷的飞船舱室里，面前有一扇能看到太空的大窗户，而且还有真人演员进来，让你切身体会自己所做之事的重要性。  
抵抗组织开始分析超空间追踪系统。  
他们能找到击败它的方法。  
没错。  
考虑到这些，这样也还行。  
参与其中的人应该会觉得还不错。  
我不觉得它有什么特别值得称道的地方，但作为这类体验中的一个玩法元素，也算合格。  
而对我和我妹妹来说，这几乎是我们唯一能参与故事的时刻，所以只要能做点什么，我们就已经很兴奋了。  
好，接下来我们来看看光剑。

cues.en: This was the other one pushed hard in the ads. This training is taught by the Sajja.
cues.zh: 这也是广告里大力宣传的另一个。这门培训由 Sajja 主讲。

cues.en: Obviously, it's weird that Jedi training, which has largely been framed in the movies as special and spiritual,
cues.zh: 显然，把绝地训练描绘成一种特别又充满灵性的东西，这很奇怪；毕竟电影一直以来基本都是这么呈现的。

cues.en: is now being offered as a cruise ship activity like it's shuffleboard. But there is an official tie in comic explaining the backstory. You see, when the ship was new, a Jedi master saved the ship's special compass from this stupid looking evil cyborg. And the captain at the time was so grateful, he built a lightsaber training pod on board to honor her. It doesn't really make sense, but that's the explanation. So the Sajah will be teaching us beginner lightsaber techniques with the help of a training remote that shoots lasers. Sort of like the one Luke Skywalker used. But obviously, our training remotes don't fly like that, they're just attached to the wall. Useless fun fact, not all the Sajah, but a lot of the Sajah are female brunettes with vaguely Daisy Ridley esque faces. And I think that's because a lot of them are cross trained to play Rey. Or at least the Rey that's way up on the balcony in the fight scene. Probably to maximize their use of the actors, since I don't think Rey is there on day one. It might also be to like save on costs associated with lightsaber stunt training. Like, now they can just train one person instead of twice as many. But once you see it, you can't unsee it. There's rays everywhere. In this activity, everyone gets to try their hands at lightsabering,
cues.zh: 现在它被当作游轮活动推出，就像沙狐球一样。不过有一部官方联动漫画解释了背景故事。你看，这艘船刚建成时，一位绝地大师从那个长相很蠢的邪恶半机械人手里救下了船上的特殊罗盘。当时的船长非常感激，就在船上建了一个光剑训练舱来纪念她。这其实不太说得通，但解释就是这样。所以 Sajah 会借助一个会发射激光的训练遥控球，教我们光剑入门技巧。有点像 Luke Skywalker 用过的那个。但显然，我们的训练遥控球不会那样飞，它们只是固定在墙上。没用的冷知识：不是所有 Sajah，但很多 Sajah 都是棕色头发的女性，脸隐约有点像 Daisy Ridley。我觉得这是因为她们中很多人接受过交叉训练，会扮演 Rey。至少是打斗场景里站在上层阳台的那个 Rey。大概是为了最大化利用演员，因为我觉得第一天 Rey 并不在那儿。也可能是为了省下光剑特技训练相关的成本。比如现在他们只用训练一个人，而不是两倍的人。但一旦你注意到了，就再也无法忽视。到处都是 Rey。在这个活动里，每个人都能上手试试光剑，

cues.en: and there are a couple different rounds to this. In the first round, you're told that a guide light will appear ahead of the laser, you get a couple seconds to line your lightsaber up with where the laser is going to be. The laser fires, and then the lightsaber vibrates and plays a sound effect as though the laser is actually impacting it. This round is obviously really boring, and that's because in an early leaked patent for this mini game, we can see that this whole first round is simply the calibration phase in disguise. They're very braggadocious about that, like our game doesn't need calibration before gameplay can begin, because we integrate it into the gameplay.
cues.zh: 这个游戏有几轮不同的流程。第一轮里，你会被告知激光前方会出现一个引导光，你有几秒钟时间把光剑对准激光将要出现的位置。激光发射后，光剑会震动并播放音效，就好像激光真的打在了上面。这一轮显然很无聊，因为在这个小游戏早期泄露的专利里，我们能看出整个第一轮其实只是伪装成玩法的校准阶段。他们对此非常自夸，意思是我们的游戏在开始玩之前不需要校准，因为我们把它整合进了玩法里。

cues.en: And it's like, okay, but did you really? Are we are we calling this gameplay? Anyway, as is pretty obvious, the computer is leading you through a series of basic positions with your lightsaber, so it can learn your dimensions and incorporate it into the next round. When I was doing my first round, I was kind of hopping around from foot to foot, primarily because I had seen that Josh D'Amaro ad and thought he looked so uncool the way he did that, and I didn't wanna repeat his mistakes. But then the Sajah had to come by and tell me to stop wiggling around so much because I think I was in danger of compromising the calibration. But it all worked out, you'll see in a second. In the second round, the time between the guide light and the laser blast is slightly shorter, so it's marginally harder, but still not overly exciting. But now, they add two people behind the lightsaber wielder using these things. This is a reflective shield capable of blocking blaster bolts. I think canonically, this shield is built using kyber crystals like a lightsaber is. Maybe a whole bunch of kyber crystals because it lights up in different colors. I saw a lot of people saying this has crazy implications for the cannon, but I think it doesn't. Don't I think they ever say it blocks lightsabers,
cues.zh: 就像是，好吧，但你真的算在玩吗？我们管这叫玩法吗？总之很明显，电脑会引导你摆出一系列光剑基本姿势，好让它了解你的身形尺寸，并纳入下一轮。我做第一轮时，有点双脚来回蹦，主要是因为我看到 Josh D'Amaro 那个广告，觉得他那样做太不酷了，不想重蹈他的覆辙。但后来 Sajah 过来，让我别晃得那么厉害，因为我觉得自己快把校准搞坏了。不过一切都顺利，你马上就能看到。第二轮中，引导灯到激光发射之间的时间略短，所以稍微难一点，但还是没那么刺激。但现在，他们在持光剑者身后加两个人，用这些东西。这是一面能挡住爆能束的反射盾。我觉得按正史设定，这盾和光剑一样是用凯伯水晶造的。也许是一大堆凯伯水晶，因为它会亮出不同颜色。我看到很多人说这对正史设定有疯狂影响，但我觉得没有。我不认为他们说过它能挡光剑，

cues.en: just lasers, which doesn't seem like a big deal. And this thing is like really heavy and awkward to hold, so I fully understand why Jedi prefer to just carry a lightsaber and deflect blasts with that. That said, the shield is pretty uncool, right? They obviously just incorporated this into the experience to try to think of something for people to do when they're not using the lightsabers.
cues.zh: 只是激光，这看起来没什么大不了。而且这东西又重又不好拿，所以我完全理解为什么绝地更愿意只带一把光剑，用它弹开攻击。话虽如此，这盾相当不酷，对吧？他们显然只是把它塞进体验里，想给不用光剑的人找点事做。

cues.en: So they're like, two people stand behind them and catch the
cues.zh: 所以就是让两个人站在后面，接住

cues.en: extra lasers
cues.zh: 多出来的激光

cues.en: that get past their lightsabers,
cues.zh: 那些越过他们光剑的，

cues.en: and that doesn't make any sense. And I'm crouching around with this big clumsy shield, feeling like a total fool. So eagle eyed viewers might have noticed something in each round. We have that guide light letting us know where the laser blast is going to hit, but we also have these little sparkles around the training remote. These twinkly lights are divided into quadrants.
cues.zh: 这根本说不通。我拿着这面又大又笨拙的盾蹲来蹲去，感觉自己像个十足的傻瓜。所以眼尖的观众可能注意到每轮里都有点东西。我们有那盏引导灯，告诉我们激光会打到哪里，但训练遥控球周围还有这些小闪光。这些闪烁光被分成四个象限。

cues.en: So while they won't show you exactly where to aim, they do let you know the general direction the blast will go. In the first two rounds, these are redundant since we have the guide light. But in the break before the final round, the Sajah offers context for these twinkles. She doesn't acknowledge them directly, but she says that those in tune with the force can sense where blasts are about to come from. So that's what the twinkles are. In canon, they're not something we're meant to be seen with the naked eye, they are the force giving us intuition about where to block. At this point, the Saja teaches us a little chant for team morale.
cues.zh: 所以它们不会显示精确瞄准位置，但能让你知道激光大致会往哪走。前两轮里这些是多余的，因为我们有引导灯。但在最终轮之前的休息中，Sajah 解释了这些闪光的背景。她没有直接点明它们，但她说与原力共鸣的人能感知到攻击将从哪里来。所以那些闪光就是这个。按正史设定，它们不是让我们用肉眼看的东西，而是原力在给我们直觉，知道该往哪里挡。这时，Saja 教我们一句小口号，提振团队士气。

cues.en: Together. And
cues.zh: 一起挥。然后

cues.en: then she says she thinks we're ready to rely on the force to block the beam. So for the final round, the blasts come quickly with no guide light, only those twinkles to guide you. My sister was not paying attention during this explanation, but that's actually good news for me because it gave me additional insight into how the tech works. If you look closely, you'll see the major difference in this final round. In the first two rounds, we were trying to aim where the laser would go. But in this final round, the laser is actually tracking us and aiming for our blades. The computer even seems to hold its fire indefinitely until you swing into the correct quadrant. The whole concept with the force twinkles was just to get us to constrain our blade movements to a smaller area,
cues.zh: 她说，她觉得我们已经准备好靠原力去挡住激光束了。所以在最后一轮，激光发射得非常快，没有引导灯，只有那些闪烁的星光来指引你。我妹妹在讲解这一段时根本没在听，但这对我来说反而是个好消息，因为它让我额外看懂了这个技术的运作原理。如果仔细看，你会发现这最后一轮有个重大区别。前两轮里，是我们在瞄准激光会打向哪里；但在这最后一轮，其实是激光在追踪我们，瞄准我们的剑刃。电脑甚至似乎会无限期地按兵不动，直到你把剑挥进正确的象限。整个原力闪烁的设定，只是为了让我们把光剑的挥动范围限制在一个更小的区域，

cues.en: so it would be less visually apparent that the lasers were following us and not the other way around. To an unsuspecting participant,
cues.zh: 这样激光其实是在跟着我们走这一点就不会那么明显了。对毫不知情的参与者来说，

cues.en: and especially a kid, it'll look like they're doing a great job guessing the precise angle of the laser every time with lightning fast reflexes.
cues.zh: 尤其是小孩，看起来就像是他们每次都凭着闪电般的反应，精准猜中了激光的角度，表现得特别厉害。

cues.en: Since Lindsay didn't notice the twinkles, she was pinwheeling her blade all over the place, so it was very apparent to me what was going on. You can literally see the lasers correcting mid air trying to follow her. So I think conceptually, that's a fun gimmick. It allows for some sense of escalation even if individual guests would not be skilled enough to keep up. It simulates the experience of practicing and improving at something all in under twenty minutes. And I loved Arsaja. I thought she was funny and was good at retaining people's names and involving everyone in the experience. Unlike the bridge training, this one you do only once and it's never utilized again. In fact, this is the only time you'll even be holding a lightsaber on board. It's forbidden to walk around with them on the ship. I assume due to paranoia that you'll get overexcited and swing into another guest or break a prop. Even if you buy the $200 ship exclusive saber in the gift shop, you're only allowed to take it out, stand still to pose for photos, and then you're expected to store it in your room. So I guess you could say that should enhance the novelty of this experience.
cues.zh: 因为 Lindsay 没注意到那些闪烁，她的光剑到处乱挥，所以我一眼就看穿了是怎么回事。你甚至能看到激光在半空中不停修正，试图跟上她。所以我觉得从概念上讲，这是个有趣的噱头。即使单个游客的水平不足以跟上节奏，它也能营造出层层递进的感觉。它把练习和进步的体验压缩到了不到二十分钟之内。我很喜欢 Arsaja，她风趣幽默，记得住每个人的名字，能让所有人都融入体验。和桥梁训练不同，这个项目你只会玩一次，之后再也用不上了。事实上，这也是你在船上唯一一次真正握到光剑。在船上拿着光剑到处走是被禁止的。我猜是因为担心你太兴奋，挥到别的游客或者弄坏道具。就算你买了礼品店里那把 200 美元的船上专属光剑，也只允许拿出来站着摆拍几张照片，然后就该把它收进你的房间里。所以我觉得，这应该会让这次体验显得更加新奇。

cues.en: But when you imagine being the protagonist in a Star Wars movie,
cues.zh: 但当你想象自己是《星球大战》电影里的主角时，

cues.en: I don't think you're picturing doing target practice. And Disney obviously understands this, because they've already done a lightsaber training experience in the theme parks. And in that one, after teaching you some basic training positions, they parade out a Darth Vader or a Kylo Ren to duel the little kids. The show always reminded me of that scene in Space Jam, where the bad guys want to imprison Michael Jordan in their theme park and force him to let kids win at basketball. Anyway, such a story moment wouldn't work in an immersive LARP experience. Right? They can't have Kylo Ren showing up every thirty minutes. How would they make it work in the story that any of the guests get to defeat the villain, let alone all of them? But therein lies the problem, right? Even in the suspended disbelief of the story, you're still not doing anything very exciting. You're just training, so there's no suspense. It's just a mildly diverting video game demo. If it was free in the theme park and you had to wait twenty minutes to do it, I could see it being reasonably popular,
cues.zh: 我想你脑海中的画面肯定不是在打靶练习。Disney 显然也明白这一点，因为他们已经在主题乐园里做过光剑训练项目了。在那个项目里，教完你几个基础训练姿势之后，他们会押出一位达斯·维达或凯洛·伦来跟小朋友对决。那场表演总让我想起《空中大灌篮》里的那一幕：反派想把 Michael Jordan 囚禁在他们的主题乐园里，逼他故意输给小孩。不过话说回来，这样的剧情桥段在沉浸式 LARP 体验里是行不通的，对吧？总不能让凯洛·伦每三十分钟出场一次吧？在剧情上要怎么解释随便哪个游客都能打败反派，更别说所有游客都能打败他了？但问题恰恰就在这里，对吧？就算沉浸在故事的悬念里，你做的其实也没什么刺激的事。你只是在训练，所以毫无悬念。它不过是个略显有趣的视频游戏演示。如果这是主题乐园里的免费项目、排队二十分钟就能玩到，我觉得它会挺受欢迎的，

cues.en: but not something you'd go out of your way to do every time. And just like the bridge training, it doesn't really work as a featured attraction for such an expensive experience.
cues.zh: 但不会是那种你每次都特意去玩的项目。而且和桥梁训练一样，对于这么昂贵的体验来说，它作为主打项目实在不够格。

cues.en: Oh, I should also talk about the Engineering Bay. That was featured in a lot of the ads too, usually just as a visually interesting backdrop. They never indicated what you would do there, but it looked like it would be something. Before I went, I thought maybe they would schedule groups of 10 or so people at a time to go in there for a story reason, and then it could be like a miniature escape room. Like, you have to gather environmental clues and use those to put the machinery at the correct settings to achieve a goal in the story. And they could have a cast member in the room with you to keep things moving if people got stuck. We're in the Engineering Room.
cues.zh: 哦，我还得说说工程湾。它在很多广告里也出现过，通常只是当作视觉上有趣的背景。他们从没说明你在那儿能做什么，但看起来应该有点内容。去之前我以为，他们可能会以剧情为由，每次安排十个人左右进去，然后那里可以像个迷你密室逃脱。比如你得收集环境线索，用这些线索把机器调到正确设置，以达成剧情目标。还可以安排一名演职人员待在房间里，如果有人卡住就推动流程。我们进工程室了。

cues.en: I'm just fine. Okay.
cues.zh: 我没事。好。

cues.en: This is in there. Woah.
cues.zh: 这里面有这个。哇。

cues.en: What's this?
cues.zh: 这是什么？

cues.en: So I was wrong. Basically, the Engineering Bay is like an activity area with 10 or so baby level puzzles. Some are like Simon, where a terminal pings in a certain order and then you replicate it. Some of them have screens showing switches in particular positions, and then you have to move them around to match. Sometimes when you succeed at a puzzle, it rewards you by playing a sound effect or making steam shoot out or shutting off an alarm that's been sounding. Oh, my gosh. That's a carbon freezing system. That's important. But as far as I could tell, there's no story incentive to do any of that. It's just busy work. Look in here, it's the core.
cues.zh: 所以我错了。基本上，工程湾就像个活动区，有十个左右幼儿级谜题。有些像西蒙游戏：终端按某个顺序响，然后你照着复现。有些屏幕会显示开关的特定位置，你得把它们拨到对应位置。有时你解开一个谜题，它会奖励你播放音效、喷出蒸汽，或者关掉一直在响的警报。天哪。那是碳凝系统。那很重要。但据我所知，做这些没有任何剧情激励。纯粹是瞎忙活。看这里，这是核心。

cues.en: Lindsay, look, the core.
cues.zh: Lindsay，看，核心。

cues.en: Wow.
cues.zh: 哇。

cues.en: I can feel it humming. All that power. Woah. We can go in.
cues.zh: 我能感觉到它在嗡鸣。全是能量。哇。我们可以进去。

cues.en: We can inside. Go I love... Go on. I love the core.
cues.zh: 我们能进去。走，我爱……进去吧。我爱这个核心。

cues.en: Oh, fix it. Okay.
cues.zh: 哦，把它修好。好。

cues.en: Press
cues.zh: 按

cues.en: those buttons. Damn.
cues.zh: 那些按钮。该死。

cues.en: Even if you fix something, in a couple minutes it'll reset for the next person to play anyway, so you're not really accomplishing anything. I think most people figured that out because every time we went in it was pretty empty. And we'd see other people our age walking walking in, taking a look around, and quickly leaving because it wasn't very interesting. The only people sticking around were a couple moms with children under the age of four, because that's the age demographic whose interest will be held by something like this. Which it's good to have something for everyone, but at this price point, like, why didn't you just take them to the park by your house if they're getting so little out of this that you're just trying to keep them distracted. Oh, I should also point out that at foot level, there's this escape hatch, which connects the engineering room to the brig. That's cool. Look, it slides.
cues.zh: 就算你修好了什么，过几分钟它也会重置，给下一个人玩，所以你并没真正完成什么。我想大多数人都看出来了，因为我们每次进去时都挺空的。我们会看到同龄人走进来，四处看看，很快就离开，因为没那么有趣。唯一会留下来的是几位妈妈，带着四岁以下的孩子，因为这个年龄段才会对这类东西感兴趣。人人都有得玩是好事，但在这个价位上，如果他们从这得到这么少，你只是想让他们分心，那为什么不直接带他们去家附近的公园呢。哦，我还得指出，脚边有个逃生舱口，把工程室和禁闭室连起来。那很酷。看，它会滑开。

cues.en: It's a secret tunnel out of the brig.
cues.zh: 这是条从禁闭室出去的秘密通道。

cues.en: It was locked when we saw it. There must have been some story event where one of the characters locked in the brig escaped via this hatch, so that's fun to imagine.
cues.zh: 我们看到它的时候是锁着的。一定是某个剧情环节里有角色从禁闭室经这个舱门逃出去的，想想还挺有意思的。

cues.en: But we weren't part of any storyline that got to use it. I read that it's possible to get summoned to the Engineering Bay for story events, like you meet Sammy there to save the ship, or the general there to sabotage the ship. So I guess in that case, there would be an element satisfaction, like there's at least the pretense that what you're doing matters. We never got any of those events though, and even if we had happened to go to the Engineering Room while one was going on, we would have been turned away. When a room is in use for a scheduled story moment, they station someone at the door and make you tap your bracelet. So unless the app verifies you've been invited by a character, you aren't allowed entry. Anyway, since we didn't get to do that, the room seemed like kind of a pointless diversion.
cues.zh: 但我们参与的剧情线没用上它。我了解到，有些剧情事件可能会把你召到工程舱，比如你在那儿遇到 Sammy 一起救船，或者遇到将军去破坏飞船。所以我想那种情况下会有一种参与感，至少表面上让你觉得自己做的事有意义。不过我们没碰上任何这种事件，而且就算我们碰巧在剧情进行时去了工程室，也会被拦下来。房间被安排给剧情环节使用时，他们会在门口安排人，让你刷手环。除非 App 验证你被某个角色邀请过，否则不许进入。总之，既然我们没体验成，这个房间就显得像个没什么意义的岔路。

cues.en: Yes.
cues.zh: 是的。

cues.en: Finally. She's leaning in. Finally, some levers to pull.
cues.zh: 终于，她凑过来了。终于有点可以操作的机关了。

cues.en: I think I'm doing it right.
cues.zh: 我觉得我做得没错。

cues.en: My impression is that basically, you can go to the Engineering Room outside of exclusive story scenes, but there isn't really a reason to. And while we were on board, I didn't realize that that was the case, because I didn't know about those story moments we didn't get. So here again, I was frustrated and at a loss. Like, it really seems like this room is for something, but what? I must be doing something wrong. I had really figured there would be something to discover there, but nope. And there was one last thing I'd loosely call an attraction. A lot of fan pages treated this like a big spoiler, but I think they showed a clip of it in one of the ads anyway. But in the climate simulator courtyard,
cues.zh: 我的印象是，在专属剧情场景之外，你其实也可以去工程室，但根本没什么理由去。我们在船上的那段时间没意识到这一点，因为我们不知道有那些没轮到我们的剧情时刻。所以在那里我又一次感到沮丧和茫然，就好像这个房间明明是干什么的，但到底是干什么的？一定是我哪里做错了。我原本真以为那边会有什么可以探索的东西，结果并没有。还有最后一处，我勉强称之为景点的。很多粉丝网站都把这当成重大剧透，但我觉得反正广告里都放过片段了。在气候模拟庭院里，

cues.en: you saw they had all those rocks stacked up in the middle. Well, they had one interactive thing in there. The Sajja could select you for force training, and then they had some of the rocks rigged to magnets, so you could pull a rock toward you. And sometimes it would knock over all the other piled rocks, which made it look a little more dramatic. I know that sounds really simple, but this is another thing they dressed up with the performers
cues.zh: 你看到他们把一堆石头堆在中间了吧。那里有一个互动项目。Sajja 可能会选中你进行原力训练，然后他们把一些石头装了磁铁，你可以把一块石头拉向你。有时候它会把堆着的其他石头全部撞倒，看起来更有戏剧效果。我知道听起来很简单，但这是又一个靠表演者包装起来的项目，

cues.en: by
cues.zh: 通过

cues.en: having like a weirdly intimate interaction with you. I don't know. But anyway, I know this is really simple, but I do think it's a cute idea. Thanks.
cues.zh: 和你进行一种有点诡异又亲密的互动。我说不好。总之，我知道这真的很简单，但我还是觉得这是个挺可爱的点子。谢谢。

cues.en: That
cues.zh: 那

cues.en: was incredible.
cues.zh: 太不可思议了。

cues.en: How do you feel? I feel amazing. Yes. It
cues.zh: 你感觉如何？我感觉棒极了。是的。

cues.en: obviously didn't happen for us. It didn't happen for most guests. There's no guaranteed way to have this happen. You can't unlock it by doing a certain thing in your gameplay, or getting a high enough loyalty score with anyone. It's just something the employees randomly select you for based on vibes. I think they often went for really little kids, birthday boys of all ages, or you know, well known theme park vloggers. And it seems like maybe three guests get to do this per sale date. So while I think it's a cute idea, I do think it's a little frustrating that this is one of the only instances of the set being rigged with an interactive special effect, and by design, the odds of seeing it are extremely slim. Mechanically, it's a basic parlor trick, but if the ship had had a lot of small touches like this happening all the time, the overall effect would have been dazzling. Little things that move, that you feel you're interacting with, but no. Part 12, supplementary activities.
cues.zh: 这事显然没发生在我们身上。对大多数游客来说也没发生。没有什么万无一失的方法能碰上它。你不能通过在游戏流程里做某件事、或者和任何人刷到足够高的忠诚度来解锁它。它完全是员工凭感觉随机选人的。我猜他们通常选特别小的孩子、各个年龄段的寿星，还有知名的主题公园视频博主。看起来每个售卖日大概只有三位游客能体验。所以虽然我觉得这是个可爱的点子，但这也让人有点沮丧：这是整个布景中极少数装了互动特效的地方之一，而设计上撞见它的概率又极低。从机制上讲，它就是个基础的客厅戏法，但如果船上能经常有这种小细节不断上演，整体效果本来会非常惊艳。那些会动、让你觉得正在与之互动的小东西。可惜没有。第 12 部分，补充活动。

cues.en: These were getting a lot of attention online, so I had better address them, although they were a very small part of the experience. Also, tried to dress like a sage off for this part. See, I've got the sleeves. They can't all be winners. So on Star Cruiser, there are a handful of filler activities that are basically intended for you to do in your downtime between other activities. All of the activities I mentioned in this section are completely optional. They have zero impact on the story, and you will not be penalized for sitting them out, which most people did. Some of these supplementary activities carried more hidden fees. Like, had model ship building as an activity, but you had to go buy the model ship kit from the gift shop. So I don't really get it. I don't know why you wouldn't just do that when you got home. They had a mixology lesson with the bartender called the Cantina Chronicles,
cues.zh: 这些活动在网上引起了不小的关注，所以我最好还是讲一讲，虽然它们只占整个体验中很小的一部分。另外，这部分我特意打扮成了贤者的样子。看，我有袖子呢。唉，不可能每套衣服都好看。在“星际巡游者”上，有一些填充类活动，基本上是给你在其他活动之间的空闲时间玩的。这一节提到的所有活动都是完全可选的。它们对剧情毫无影响，不参加也不会有任何惩罚，大多数人也确实没参加。有些附加活动还藏着额外的收费。比如有模型飞船制作这个活动，但你得去礼品店自己买模型套件。我就不太理解了。我不知道为什么你不在家做这些。他们还有一个跟酒保上的调酒课，叫“酒馆编年史”，

cues.en: where he would make you non alcoholic versions of all the specialty drinks and then tell you in universe lore about all the ingredients. This drink would reveal
cues.zh: 他会给你做所有特调饮品的无酒精版本，然后给你讲这些原料在世界观设定里的故事。这种饮品会揭示

cues.en: if they had true intentions. So they would take a sip right before the deal and after, if it tasted so sweet, you would actually lose the ability to speak.
cues.zh: 对方是否有真心。所以他们会在交易前喝一小口，交易后再喝一口，如果味道变得特别甜，你就会失去说话的能力。

cues.en: Like a lot of the drinks had planets of origin in the Star Wars universe or ingredients were like the eggs of a creature. I know one of them had venom in it, and then they would give you a little eye dropper of antidote to chase it with. Cantina Chronicles was supposed to happen at noon on day two, and it overlapped with the theme park trip. So I really wanted to go and get all that sweet lore, but it just didn't seem reasonable. But then when I got home, I read online that a lot of guests did go out of their way to try to go to it. And on a lot of the trips, it was just canceled without warning. Like, would be sitting in the bar looking at their phones, like, shouldn't the bartender be here by now? And then before their very eyes, it would be deleted from the schedule. I would have been so mad if I skipped something else and then that happened. So I guess I'm glad I didn't go to it, but it does sound like it would have been fun if it happened. Later in the life of the Star Cruiser, they modified the Cantina Chronicles to something called Spirits of Adventure. So it was the same thing, but the drinks were all alcoholic,
cues.zh: 比如很多饮品都标注了在星球大战宇宙中的原产星球，或者原料是什么生物的卵。我知道其中一款含有毒液，然后他们会给你一个小滴管装的解药，让你接着喝下去。酒馆编年史本来安排在第二天中午，但和主题公园之行时间冲突了。所以我真的很想去听那些精彩的设定故事，但感觉不太现实。不过后来我回家后在网上看到，很多客人还是特意想赶去参加。而且在很多航次里，这个活动都不打招呼就直接取消了。就像有人坐在酒吧里看着手机，心想：酒保不是该到了吗？然后就在他们眼前，这个活动从日程表上被删掉了。如果我为此错过了别的活动，然后还碰上这种事，我肯定气死了。所以我觉得幸好我没去，但如果真办成了，听起来应该会挺好玩的。在“星际巡游者”运营的后期，他们把酒馆编年史改成了一个叫“冒险之灵”的项目。内容还是一样，只不过饮品全都换成了含酒精的，

cues.en: and that version was $49
cues.zh: 那个版本每人收费 49 美元

cues.en: per person. So it's kind of unfortunate to me that they replaced a free thing with a thing that costs money on this all inclusive trip. Anyway, then they had free activities, which were more like party games. Like, had one called know your copilot.
cues.zh: 所以对我来说挺遗憾的，在这种全包式旅行里，他们用一个收费项目替换了原来的免费项目。总之，他们还有一些免费活动，更像是派对游戏。比如有一个叫“了解你的副驾驶”。

cues.en: And to my understanding, that was like a Star Wars version of the newlywed game. There are sabacc card game lessons, and of course, that hollow sabacc table in the lounge. The table is cool because it uses a Peppers ghost illusion to make it look like there are holograms of your cards in front of you. They only have this one table, so it was usually occupied with a short line to use it, like a swing set at recess or something. But I wasn't really trying to waste precious time doing a digital card game anyway, so I was happy just to see it. Later, they ran a Sabaq tournament. I had assumed before going that the Sabaq lessons were there because some smuggler story moment involved playing Sabaq against a character actor. That actually did not happen. The Sabaq is entirely a filler activity. But if you win the tournament, you get a big commemorative coin.
cues.zh: 据我了解，那就像是《星球大战》版的“新婚游戏”。还有萨巴克牌游戏课程，当然，还有休息室里那张中空的萨巴克桌。这张桌子很酷，它利用“佩珀尔幻象”制造出全息牌就在你面前的效果。他们只有这一张桌子，所以通常都被人占用着，排队的人也不多，就像课间休息时的秋千一样。反正我也没打算把宝贵的时间浪费在玩数字卡牌游戏上，所以能看一眼我就挺满足了。后来，他们还举办了一场萨巴克锦标赛。去之前我原本以为，之所以有萨巴克课程，是因为某个走私犯剧情桥段需要你和角色扮演演员对打一局。实际上并没有这回事。萨巴克完全就是个凑数的活动。不过如果你赢了锦标赛，就能拿到一枚大大的纪念币。

cues.en: I wish I had that big coin. It's just not fair. At one point, they set up an obstacle course in the atrium and had kids race the remote controlled droids through it. They have sector set, which is space bingo. And if you win, you get the big coin. And then there are the infamous Ryloth dance lessons, where they teach you moves to the alien pop star's new song. Most of these are lame and not worth the money you've paid to be here. But as I said, most guests will not be doing these activities anyway. The way I see it, the schedule was pretty packed, and it had a lot of awkward thirty to forty minute gaps between things, where it would be hard to really know what to do with yourself. So I think these are to fill those gaps. Even though I was not interested in doing any of these, I had intended to try to make it to most of them to get footage, so you could see what they were like. And even with those intentions, I didn't make it to most of them. But I felt like walking past and seeing them happening helped add a little life to the ship. I've never been on a real cruise, but whenever I've seen them on TV, they seem to always have old people doing Pilates by the pool and playing bingo.
cues.zh: 真希望那枚大币是我的，太不公平了。有一次，他们在中庭设置了一条障碍赛道，让孩子们操控遥控机器人穿越其中。他们还有“星区宾果”，其实就是太空版宾果游戏，赢了也能拿到大纪念币。然后就是那臭名昭著的“赖洛思舞蹈课”，教你怎么跳外星流行歌手的新歌。这些活动大多很无聊，不值得你花的那些钱。但正如我说的，大多数游客反正也不会去参加。在我看来，日程排得挺满的，但各项活动之间有很多尴尬的三十到四十分钟的空档，让人很难知道该干点什么。所以我觉得这些活动就是用来填补空档的。虽然我对这些都没兴趣，但我本打算尽量多去几个拍点素材，好让你们看看是什么样子。即便抱着这个想法，我还是没赶上几个。不过我觉得，路过时看到这些活动在进行，确实给这艘“船”增添了几分生气。我从没坐过真正的游轮，但在电视上看到的游轮，好像总有一群老人在泳池边做普拉提、玩宾果。

cues.en: So I like that they have all this corny fake stuff to make it feel like a real corny cruise. I think that's cute. It was probably expected that most guests wouldn't bother with these, but that's part of why I think it's funny that they actually included them. So for that reason, I think these bonus activities are pretty charming, and they certainly don't take anything away. I'm sorry, because I feel like everyone was waiting for me to throw shade at space bingo, but I'm not going to. I think it's cute. Parts 13,
cues.zh: 所以我挺喜欢他们搞了这些老套的假玩意儿，让它感觉像一趟真正老套的游轮之旅。我觉得挺可爱的。设计者大概预料到多数游客不会去碰这些活动，但这也正是我觉得好笑的地方——他们居然真的把这些做进去了。因此，我觉得这些附加活动相当有魅力，而且丝毫不会减损体验。抱歉，我知道大家都在等我吐槽太空宾果，但我不打算这么做。我觉得它挺可爱的。第13部分，

cues.en: the schedule.
cues.zh: 日程安排。

cues.en: You may have picked up on it by now, but the Starcruiser schedule was unrelenting.
cues.zh: 你可能已经注意到了，但 Star Cruiser 的日程安排毫不松懈。

cues.en: Basically, every minute of the day was booked with something. And if you thought the schedule looked full when you arrived, you would soon discover that new things are dropped into it on the fly,
cues.zh: 基本上，一天中的每一分钟都被安排得满满当当。如果你刚到的时候觉得日程已经很满，很快就会发现还会临时塞进新的安排，

cues.en: theoretically.
cues.zh: 理论上。

cues.en: You could access it in your app, which you were expected to look at constantly.
cues.zh: 你可以在应用里查看它，而且他们要求你不断查看。

cues.en: And most of the things on it were thirty minutes or less, so we were constantly running around. Even among positive reviews, I've seen countless people talk about leaving feeling drained,
cues.zh: 而且上面大多数项目都只有三十分钟或更短，所以我们一直在到处赶。即使在好评里，我也看到无数人说离开时感到精疲力竭，

cues.en: both physically and emotionally,
cues.zh: 身心俱疲，

cues.en: which in my opinion, seems like a bad thing. Day one of Star Cruiser, you can check-in as early as 1PM,
cues.zh: 在我看来，这似乎不是好事。Star Cruiser 第一天，最早下午1点就能办入住，

cues.en: and the story ends between ten and 11PM.
cues.zh: 故事在晚上10点到11点之间结束。

cues.en: The lounge stays open till eleven, and that might be one of your only chance to spend time there, so you might want to. And we stayed up a little later than that so I could get ambient footage of the atrium when it was empty. On day two, the activity begins as early as 08:40AM.
cues.zh: 休息室开到11点，而那可能是你仅有的能待一会儿的机会，所以你可能想去。我们那天还熬得更晚一点，好让我拍到中庭空无一人的环境镜头。第二天，活动最早早上8:40就开始了。

cues.en: But if you really want your money's worth, you ought to eat the themed breakfast, so you should really start your day closer to 8AM. God forbid anyone who goes wants to shower between days one and two, wear makeup, do any kind of skincare routine,
cues.zh: 但如果你真想值回票价，就该去吃主题早餐，所以你真该在8点左右就开始一天。千万别指望去的人还想在第一天和第二天之间洗澡、化妆、做任何护肤流程，

cues.en: do their hair in the morning, spend time putting on elaborate themed costumes as Disney has encouraged them to do. God forbid anyone gets to their room at the end of the night and wants to talk to their roommates about what they've experienced thus far. It's just accepted that everybody is going to have a sleep deficit unless there's some kind of automaton that shuffles into their room at night, falls face first onto the bed, goes directly to sleep, then rises in the same clothes the following morning and shuffles directly out the door again. So if you've gotten up at 8AM, you should know that day two runs all the way until 11PM again. Day three is checkout day, and on the sample itinerary, it says checkout is at ten, but it actually ended up being earlier than that. They assigned random half hour slots in which each specific room was meant to leave, which could be hours earlier. Ours was actually one of the latest groups to leave at 9AM,
cues.zh: 早上做头发，花时间穿上迪士尼鼓励他们穿的那种精致主题服装。千万别指望有人晚上回到房间后，还想和室友聊聊自己到目前为止的体验。大家就默认每个人都会睡眠不足，除非有某种自动机器晚上拖着步子进房间，脸朝下扑到床上，直接睡着，第二天早上穿着同一身衣服起床，又拖着步子直接出门。所以如果你8点起床，要知道第二天会一路持续到晚上11点。第三天是退房日，示例行程上写10点退房，但实际结束得更早。他们随机分配半小时时段，让每个具体房间在该时段离开，可能比10点早好几个小时。我们其实是最晚一批9点离开的，

cues.en: but they started knocking on our doors at around eight to make sure we were actually awake and getting ready, because they have a really short turnaround to flip the rooms for the next crop of guests at one. Again, this doesn't feel very luxurious. I don't think I've had this happen in any other hotel I've stayed at ever. Another thing is, I really like themed environments. And even though I didn't find the environments exceptionally detailed, there were some spaces on the ship I might have liked to hang out in longer to absorb the atmosphere. As I said earlier, I thought the lounge was really cool, but I only went in there twice and neither occasion exceeded fifteen minutes. We always had to guiltily run to it, order a drink, and try to chug it before we had to get up and sprint to the next thing on our itinerary. Because on the Star Cruiser, time is very literally money. So on one of our brief visits to the lounge, we ordered some of the bar food, including the plate of beautiful cheese balls, which I love, the ones that arrived in the cloche full of smoke, and we didn't even get to finish them. If anyone can finish a cheese ball, it's us. But nope, we were already late for lightsaber training, and we had to run their drinks in hand, just like the Jedi of old. I barely even managed to get footage of that space bingo. It was happening literally while we were trying to eat the cheese balls. So I would like stand up and sprint to the other room, film some bingo, and then sprint back and keep shoveling cheese into my mouth. Everything moved at a breakneck pace, and I don't mean that as a compliment. It's not the kind of fast pace that feels thrilling.
cues.zh: 但他们在8点左右就开始敲我们的门，确认我们真的醒了、在准备，因为他们要赶在1点前翻好房间给下一批客人，周转时间真的很短。再说一次，这感觉不太奢华。我不认为我在住过的任何其他酒店遇到过这种事。还有一点，我很喜欢主题环境。虽然我觉得这些环境并没有特别精细，但船上有些空间我可能想多待一会儿感受氛围。就像我之前说的，我觉得休息室很酷，但我只进去过两次，而且两次都没超过十五分钟。我们总是内疚地跑过去，点杯饮料，赶在必须起身冲向下一个行程前猛灌下去。因为在 Star Cruiser 上，时间真的就是金钱。所以有一次我们短暂去休息室，点了些酒吧小吃，包括一盘漂亮的芝士球，我很喜欢，就是那种罩子里满是烟端上来的，结果我们甚至没吃完。要说谁能吃完芝士球，那肯定是我们。但不行，我们已经迟了光剑训练，只能手里拿着饮料狂奔，就像旧时的绝地武士。我甚至差点没拍到那个太空宾果。它就在我们试图吃芝士球的时候进行。所以我得站起来冲到另一个房间，拍点宾果，再冲回来继续往嘴里塞芝士。一切都在以极快的节奏推进，我不是在夸它。这不是那种让人觉得刺激的快节奏。

cues.en: I would describe it as frantic.
cues.zh: 我会把它形容成兵荒马乱。

cues.en: And two straight days of frantic on what is ostensibly sold as a vacation is not ideal and is very mentally taxing. I think one could have had a decent time hanging out on the ship and soaking up the ambiance and ignoring the gameplay entirely.
cues.zh: 而名义上是度假，却连续两天兵荒马乱，这并不理想，也非常耗神。我觉得一个人本可以在船上闲逛、感受氛围，完全不管游戏玩法，也能过得挺不错。

cues.en: In fact, I think most adults would happily fall into that category because I think they would surely find the simplicity of the gameplay pretty unstimulating.
cues.zh: 事实上，我觉得大多数成年人会乐意归入这一类，因为他们肯定会觉得玩法这么简单，实在挺没劲的。

cues.en: And whenever the itinerary gets posted anywhere online, everybody's first question is like, well, are you allowed to just miss stuff on the schedule? And the answer is,
cues.zh: 而且每次日程发到网上，大家第一个问题都是：嗯，你可以直接错过日程上的活动吗？答案是，

cues.en: technically,
cues.zh: 严格来说，

cues.en: yes. But practically,
cues.zh: 可以。但实际来说，

cues.en: no. By this, I mean, you're not in high school. You could have a full schedule on your phone and simply not show up for any of it. They get to choose who they want to interact with, or they get to choose to sit and watch. So there's so many different ways to engage. You don't have to participate if you don't want to. But remember, the immersive role play element was Disney's entire justification for jacking up the price so high. So if you're gonna pay to go and not do the gameplay, you might as well just throw handfuls of cash down your garbage disposal. This is like asking, can you go to your local theater and buy 20 movie tickets, only to sit in the lobby for two days straight? You probably can,
cues.zh: 不行。我是说，你又不是高中生。你手机里可以有满满一份日程，然后干脆一个都不去。他们可以选择想和谁互动，也可以选择坐着看。所以参与方式有很多种。你不想参加就可以不参加。但记住，沉浸式角色扮演元素正是 Disney 把价格抬这么高的全部理由。所以如果你花钱去了却不玩玩法，那还不如把一把把现金扔进垃圾处理器。这就像问，你能不能去本地影院买20张电影票，结果只是在两天里一直坐在大厅？你大概可以，

cues.en: but it would be really weird. But if one goes to the Star Cruiser and does participate in the gameplay, they might be sort of miserable, because they'll be running on too little sleep, never have a moment to relax, and not necessarily feel fulfilled by the events they do attend. And of course, there was no transparency about which events might be cool and have some kind of special effect or interactive element, and which events were just short story tableau,
cues.zh: 但那会非常奇怪。可如果去了 Star Cruiser 并真的参与玩法，他们可能会有点惨，因为睡眠太少、一直没机会放松，而且参加的活动也未必让人有满足感。当然，也没有透明说明哪些活动可能很酷、有某种特效或互动元素，哪些活动只是短小的故事场景，

cues.en: which you would witness from a middle distance over a sea of other guests heads,
cues.zh: 而你只能隔着其他客人的人海，从中等距离外看到，

cues.en: unless they started without you. I personally really like an active vacation. I like a theme park trip, an excursion around a city, a museum, maybe an obstacle course.
cues.zh: 除非他们没等你就开始了。我个人真的很喜欢活跃型度假。我喜欢主题公园之旅、城市游览、博物馆，也许还有障碍赛道。

cues.en: I'm not a spa person. I'm not a lie by the pool person. I'm not a get in the pool person. I'm not a pool person. I don't like pools. I can't swim. This was a bad example. My point is, I didn't think I would be easily exhausted by an experience like this, because I'm usually well prepared to be on my feet and doing exciting things all day on little or no sleep. I mentioned that our cabin was really convenient to the dining room, and I also mentioned that I didn't have much of an appetite by dinner on day two. I kind of buried the lead on that. Truthfully,
cues.zh: 我不是爱做水疗的人。我不是爱躺在泳池边的人。我不是爱下水的人。我不是泳池爱好者。我不喜欢泳池。我不会游泳。这个例子不好。我的意思是，我原以为自己不会轻易被这种体验累垮，因为我通常很能扛：只睡很少甚至不睡，也能整天站着到处跑、做刺激的事。我提到过我们的舱房离餐厅很方便，也提到第二天晚饭时我没什么胃口。这事我有点把重点埋在后面了。说实话，

cues.en: I felt really, really run down by that point in our trip. I actually got up from our table in the middle of dinner and ran back to our room, because I thought I was going to throw up. And then when I got to the room, I was like, oh, no. I'm not.
cues.zh: 到旅程那个阶段，我真的、真的觉得精疲力尽。晚饭吃到一半，我居然从桌边起身跑回房间，因为我以为自己要吐了。然后到了房间，我心想，哦不。我并不是要吐。

cues.en: That's not what this feeling is. So I just kind of, like, stood there in our doorway,
cues.zh: 这种感觉并不是那样的。我就那样站在门口，

cues.en: like, enjoying that the room was quiet. I thought about taking some Tylenol, but that wasn't what was wrong either. I was just really exhausted. So, yeah, instead, I just ended up standing in our room for a while and, like, staring at my own reflection in the mirror of our tiny bathroom, and and I gave myself a pep talk. Like, okay, it's the last night. I can't miss the finale. It's just a few more hours. And then I kind of like rallied and went back to dinner. I'm just glad this happened on our second night, so I didn't miss a second of the dinner show on night one. But anyway, I hope from what I just described, you said to yourself, that sounds like a really weird thing to have happened on a luxury vacation experience,
cues.zh: 就是，挺享受房间里那种安静的。我想过吃点 Tylenol（泰诺），但那也不是问题所在。我就是真的太累了。所以呢，我就在我们房间里站了好一会儿，盯着我们那个小浴室的镜子里自己的倒影，然后给自己打气。就像，好吧，这是最后一晚了，我不能错过压轴大戏，就再撑几个小时而已。然后我算是重新振作，回去吃晚饭了。我只是庆幸这事发生在第二晚，第一晚的晚宴表演我一点都没错过。但不管怎样，我希望从我刚才描述的这些，你心里已经在想：这听起来真的是一件很奇怪的事，居然发生在一趟奢华度假体验里，

cues.en: because it is. I have never had that happen before or since while working,
cues.zh: 因为确实如此。我在工作期间，在那之前和之后都从未遇到过这种情况。

cues.en: while traveling,
cues.zh: 在旅途中，

cues.en: anytime.
cues.zh: 随时。

cues.en: The trip just like broke my body in some unfathomable
cues.zh: 这趟旅行简直把我整垮了，累得难以形容。

cues.en: way. And like, we didn't even utilize every scheduled minute of our trip. We had the latest wake up time on the final day. On day two, we slept in a little and had a full breakfast, and we didn't even really drink. Like, there were a lot of cocktails I wanted to try because they were themed. But I I think I had two over the span of the first day and one in the afternoon on the second day. And then I just didn't have time for anymore. So I think all things considered, we were a little better equipped to handle this than others might have been, and it still ran us ragged. I really can't imagine trying to do Star Cruiser with little kids, or if you yourself have any health problems. Like, could, and you could just accept that you were going to miss a lot of things in order to fit in breaks and naps. But there again, if you don't participate in something, you're throwing away $2 per person per minute. So here again, the price becomes an issue. If the hotel was cheap or even cheaper,
cues.zh: 方式。而且，我们甚至没把行程里安排的每一分钟都利用上。最后一天我们起得最晚。第二天我们睡了个懒觉，吃了一顿丰盛的早餐，而且其实也没怎么喝。说实话，有很多主题鸡尾酒我想尝尝。但我想，第一天我一共喝了两杯，第二天下午喝了一杯。之后我就没时间再喝了。所以我觉得，总的来说，比起其他人，我们还算稍微更有准备一些，但这仍然把我们累得够呛。我真的无法想象带着小孩去玩 Star Cruiser，或者你自己有任何健康问题还去玩。比如，你可能只能接受：为了腾出时间休息和打盹，你会错过很多东西。但话又说回来，如果你不参加某个项目，你就是在白白浪费每人每分钟 2 美元。所以这样一来，价格又成了问题。如果酒店便宜，或者甚至更便宜，

cues.en: it would be way easier to say, just pay for the trip, do what you like, miss what you're not interested in, and you can always come back and do what you missed. But for what it cost, that was an entirely unreasonable
cues.zh: 说起来简单多了：只管付钱去旅行，做你喜欢的，不感兴趣的就错过，反正随时可以回来补上错过的。但就它花的代价而言，那完全不合理。

cues.en: suggestion.
cues.zh: 建议。

cues.en: Part 14,
cues.zh: 第 14 部分，

cues.en: the excursion.
cues.zh: 这次探索。

cues.en: So like many real cruises, this experience has a shore excursion
cues.zh: 所以就像许多真实的邮轮之旅一样，这次体验也有岸上观光环节

cues.en: to Batuu. Batuu is the in universe planet name for Star Wars Land in Hollywood Studios.
cues.zh: 到巴图。巴图（Batuu）是这个“星球大战”园区——好莱坞影城（Hollywood Studios）里——在剧情设定中的星球名称。

cues.en: So on day two, you have an excursion,
cues.zh: 那么在第二天，你们有一次外出游览，

cues.en: where you take a ship down to the planet.
cues.zh: 你驾驶飞船降落到行星上。

cues.en: I'm trying to tell you that you take a bus to the theme park. Not to be a hater, but I actually think it's kind of stupid that in the metanarrative, a luxury cruise liner would ever intentionally go to Batuu. In universe, this location is supposed to be a backwater planet ruled by crime lords with blaster holes all over the walls and an active military presence. They try to make an excuse by saying the Halcyon took its maiden voyage here back when the planet was nice, but I don't buy it. I understand that we have to go to Batuu, because that's what they already built for the theme park. But I personally think it would have been more immersive if they had pretended they were taking us to some place more touristy, like Nambu or Canto Bight, or maybe even Endor as a reference to the original Star Tours. And then in the story, we could be derailed by a resistance mission, or maybe the ship comes under attack and we're forced to stop in Batuu for repairs or parts or something. And the cast members could act all apologetic about the change in route, and say things like, if you do decide to go planet side, please be cautious. This is a very rough planet. I don't know. That just seems more exciting to me, and also like an easier way to tie in gameplay missions. So this was another aspect of our grueling schedule. We were supposed to catch our shuttle to Batuu at like 9AM.
cues.zh: 我想告诉你的是，你是坐巴士去主题乐园的。不是我想当黑子，但我真觉得，在元叙事里让一艘豪华游轮故意开去巴图有点蠢。在设定里，这地方本该是个穷乡僻壤的星球，由犯罪领主统治，墙上到处是爆能枪弹孔，还有军队驻守。他们想找借口，说 Halcyon 号当年星球还很不错时在这里首航，但我不信这套。我理解我们必须去巴图，因为主题乐园里已经建好了。但我个人觉得，如果假装带我们去更像旅游胜地的地方会更沉浸，比如 Nambu 或 Canto Bight，甚至可以是 Endor，致敬初代 Star Tours。然后在故事里，我们可以被抵抗组织任务打断，或者飞船遇袭，被迫停在巴图修船、找零件之类的。演职人员还可以对航线变更表现得特别抱歉，说些像“如果你真决定登陆星球，请务必小心”这样的话。这颗星球很危险。我不知道。那在我看来就是更刺激，也更容易把玩法任务串起来。所以这也是我们魔鬼日程的又一部分。我们本该在早上9点左右搭上去巴图的接驳车。

cues.en: I think they just randomly assigned different times to different cabins to try to keep the line from backing up too much, because they only had like a couple buses. But the story hadn't ended until like 11PM the night prior, and we'd gotten to sleep even later, So I wasn't going anywhere at 9AM. So this was the only time we just defied the schedule. We slept in a little longer, we got breakfast, and we were like an hour late. And it turned out it didn't matter. In fact, by taking the shuttle at 10AM, we were able to walk on with no line. There was a ton of discourse online about the shuttle. Everybody was roasting it, because they found out through leaked images of the exterior that the shuttle was a box truck. And I guess there was some perceived indignity in putting high paying guests in a box truck. To be quite honest, I don't understand that at all, and I think it's kind of stupid. Like, we all knew it wasn't gonna be a real spaceship, right? So it was obviously gonna be built in some kind of vehicle. So who really cares what kind of vehicle the themed seating area is built inside of? If they had instead scraped the innards out of a school bus or a limousine to build the exact same passenger compartment, would that make any material difference? So no, I couldn't care less that this shuttle was a box truck. Anyway, you go inside and it's themed to look like a little spaceship.
cues.zh: 我想他们只是随机给不同的舱房分配了不同的时间，好让排队的人不至于太多，因为他们大概就只有几辆巴士。不过前一晚的故事直到将近晚上11点才结束，我们睡得还要更晚，所以我根本不可能9点就出发。这是我们唯一一次没按schedule走：我们多睡了一会儿，吃了早饭，晚了差不多一个小时。结果发现根本无所谓。实际上，因为坐的是10点的接驳车，我们直接走了进去，完全没排队。网上关于接驳车有超多讨论，大家都在嘲讽它，因为有人从外观泄露图里发现这接驳车居然是一辆厢式货车。可能有人觉得让花了大价钱的客人坐厢式货车有失体面。说实话，我完全不能理解这种想法，我觉得这有点蠢。大家都知道这不可能是真的宇宙飞船，对吧？所以它显然得建在某种车辆里面。那这个主题化座舱建在什么样的车里，又有什么关系呢？如果他们当初是把一辆校车或者加长礼宾车的内部掏空，装进一模一样的客舱，那会有什么实质区别吗？所以，接驳车是辆厢式货车这事儿我完全无所谓。总之，你走进去，里面装饰成了一个小飞船的样子。

cues.en: I had heard they'd be using more simulated window tech, but they opted to instead not have any windows. I won't roast them too hard on that, because I think having simulated moving windows in a randomly jostling box would probably make everybody puke all over each other. They do have a spaceship sound play and lights flash when the engines kick on, which I thought was kind of cute.
cues.zh: 我之前听说他们会用更多模拟舷窗技术，但最后他们干脆没装窗户。我不想在这点上太吐槽他们，因为我觉得在一个随机颠簸的箱子里装会动的模拟舷窗，可能会让所有人吐得满车都是。不过引擎启动时会有飞船的音效，灯光也会闪烁，我觉得还挺可爱的。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但是

cues.en: I'm going to be honest, I was disappointed by the shuttle and here's why. I had heard from promo materials that it was going to be driven by a droid, which I guess canonically it is. But I had wrongly assumed that we would have a little window through which we would see a sliver of cockpit and then the head of a droid pilot. I wasn't expecting much, probably not a full body figure like they had in Star Tours, but they could have at least done like a head on a stick that could raise and lower and swivel side to side. We would only see a little bit of it from behind anyway, so it wouldn't need that much detail. A good example of this kind of thing is the King Kong ride at Universal Studios.
cues.zh: 说实话，我对这个接驳车挺失望的，原因是这样的。我从宣传材料里听说它会由一个机器人驾驶——按设定来说好像确实如此。但我错误地以为会有一个小窗户，透过它能看到一小片驾驶舱，然后是机器人驾驶员的头部。我本来期待不高，可能不会像《星际之旅》（Star Tours）里那样有全身人偶，但他们至少可以做个“棍子上的头”，能升降、能左右转动。反正我们也只能从背后看到一点点，所以根本不需要多精细。这类做法的一个好例子就是环球影城的金刚（King Kong）游乐项目。

cues.en: They have animatronic drivers in every truck. Actually, they have a whole cast of different animatronic drivers. They all have different names and different personalities with different dialogue.
cues.zh: 他们每辆卡车里都有机械驾驶司机。实际上，他们有一整套不同的机械司机角色。每个都有不同的名字和性格，配的台词也不一样。

cues.en: It's crazy. But no, instead in this shuttle, they have a little square area that looks like it should be a window to a cockpit, but it's opaque and doesn't open. We hear the droid that's driving talking over the comms system, and there's a little plaque indicating that if we could see him, this droid would look like Rex from Star Tours, but we never do see him. It's so sad. I'm sure they logistically could have put a droid in there, and I'm sure some Imagineers suggested it, and then corporate decided they would just rather not spend the money to do it. And that is not an attitude I want them to have for an experience that costs this much. I feel like this is just another one of those relatively small touches that could have gone a long way. Upon arrival, you disembark into this little tunnel that's blocked off for only Starcruiser guests. And in the tunnel, they have a kind of concierge setup. So you can grab free water bottles, and in our case, free loaner umbrellas because it was pouring rain. Oh my god.
cues.zh: 太离谱了。可并没有，这辆接驳车里反而有一小块方形区域，看起来像是驾驶舱的窗户，但它是封死的，也打不开。我们通过通讯系统听到驾驶它的机器人说话，还有一块小牌子说明：如果我们能看到他，这个机器人会像 Star Tours 里的 Rex，但我们始终没见到他。太惨了。我确定从后勤安排上他们完全可以在那里放一个机器人，也肯定有 Imagineers 提议过，然后公司决定宁可省这笔钱。对于这么贵的一次体验，我不希望他们抱着这种态度。我觉得这只是又一个本可以很加分、却只差一点的小细节。到达后，你会下车走进一条只对 Starcruiser 客人开放的小通道。通道里有个类似礼宾服务点的设置。你可以拿免费瓶装水；我们那次还借到了免费雨伞，因为当时下着倾盆大雨。我的天哪。

cues.en: It's
cues.zh: 这挺

cues.en: nice that they gave us umbrellas. Not
cues.zh: 好，他们给了我们雨伞。不算

cues.en: so bad. No.
cues.zh: 太糟。不。

cues.en: No.
cues.zh: 不。

cues.en: It's so bad. I know. I'm being rained on so much.
cues.zh: 太糟了。我知道。我正被雨淋得不行。

cues.en: Oh, it's cold now too. They allot a good chunk of time for the theme park. You're meant to amuse yourself there until around 2PM and the latest you can stay is four. In that block of time, the buses between the hotel and the theme park run pretty much continuously.
cues.zh: 哦，现在又变冷了。他们给主题公园留了一大段时间。你本应在那里自己玩到下午两点左右，最晚可以待到四点。那段时间里，酒店和主题公园之间的巴士几乎不间断运行。

cues.en: So if your family had never been to Star Wars Land, you would have flexibility to do all the upcharge experiences like the lightsaber,
cues.zh: 所以如果你家人从没去过 Star Wars Land，你就有余裕去做所有付费体验，比如光剑、

cues.en: the droid, the cantina,
cues.zh: 机器人、cantina，

cues.en: shopping in general. But that would be a terrible waste of your time, given how short the cruise is and how much it costs. I hope no one did that. Our plan was to only go to Batuu for the minimum time necessary to do all the stuff specific to Star Cruiser. The cruise package includes fast passes for the Millennium Falcon ride and the Rise of the Resistance ride, which is like a $20 value each, so that's something. And of course, the shuttle that takes you from the hotel to the park is a unique experience, so we had to leave the cruiser to do all that. This excursion is the first thing that happens on day two, which means when you wake up, your app has put you on one of the story paths and populated a bunch of corresponding missions for you to complete. Two of the missions are just to go on the rides. They work them into the story. So basically, you get a text from a character on your storyline saying, I need you to report to this location.
cues.zh: 还有一般购物。但考虑到航程这么短、价格这么高，那会极其浪费你的时间。我希望没人那么做。我们的计划是只在 Batuu 待最少必要时间，完成 Star Cruiser 专属的所有内容。邮轮套餐包含 Millennium Falcon 项目和 Rise of the Resistance 项目的快速通行证，每张差不多值 20 美元，所以还算有点东西。当然，从酒店到园区的接驳车本身就是独特体验，所以我们得离开 Starcruiser 去做这些。这个外出活动是第二天的第一件事，也就是说你醒来时，App 已经把你放进某条故事线，并生成了一堆对应任务让你完成。其中两个任务就是去玩项目。它们把项目编进了故事里。所以基本上，你会收到故事线里某个角色发来的消息说：我需要你到这个地点报到。

cues.en: Scan your credentials at the gate for mission coordinates,
cues.zh: 在入口处扫描你的凭证，获取任务坐标，

cues.en: by which they mean, go to the right entrance and tap your band to use the fast pass that's been preloaded onto there. They've written the rides into every story path, so everybody gets to do those no matter who is texting them. If you're a Stark cruiser guest, they give you a special pin to wear, so that employees in the theme park will know you're doing the hotel experience and can theoretically interact with you in character and stuff. Then a sound effect calls our attention back to Rey, who is now holding a holocron. So your brain fills in the blanks and you imagine you've seen it soar into her hand. Enhanced further by the NPCs placed throughout the crowd, who swing their heads in an arc as if they can see it flying. Rey's holocron is also collapsible and it comes out of the railing in front of her. cues.en: Anyway, with all that said, I don't actually think these special effects reflect a high enough budget for what they were charging. To be clear, they were cute and I liked it as a show in a vacuum,
cues.zh: 总之，话虽如此，我并不觉得这些特效所体现的预算，配得上他们收的价。说清楚点，它们挺可爱，单看演出本身我是喜欢的，

cues.zh: 第17部分，

cues.en: was it worth it? When it comes to the Galactic Star Cruiser, I've seen a lot of people be really dismissive over the subject of quality and price. Like, they're mad that it's expensive, but then they'll also say things like, who cares if it's bad? It's the new Fyre Festival.
cues.zh: 值不值？说到Galactic Star Cruiser，我见过很多人对这个项目的质量和价格特别不屑。比如，他们气它太贵，但同时又会说：烂就烂呗，谁在乎？这就是新版的Fyre Festival。

cues.en: Everybody dropping that much money on this is a millionaire who deserves to get scammed, etcetera. But in my experience, that's not at all the demographic of people who booked the hotel. From what I've encountered personally, most of the people who went were middle class families who splurged on a trip. Families do that a lot on Disney vacations,
cues.zh: 花这么多钱来住的都是活该被宰的百万富翁，诸如此类。但根据我的经验，预订这家酒店的人群根本不是这样。就我个人接触到的来看，去的大多是为一次旅行舍得花大钱的中产家庭。家庭在迪士尼度假时经常这么干，

cues.en: because these experiences have been successfully established in American culture as a rite of passage. Something you have to do at least once before your kid is grown, and that brings an implied deadline. You must find a way to get to Disney World before your child is too old to believe in the magic. Lucy at 4.5 and you,
cues.zh: 因为这些体验已经在美国文化中被成功地确立为一种人生仪式——在孩子长大之前至少要做一次的事，而这带来一个隐性的截止期限。你必须设法在孩子大到不再相信魔法之前赶到迪士尼世界。4岁半的Lucy和你，

cues.zh: 再等待，快来迪士尼乐园留下终生难忘的回忆。这里是梦想成真之地。所以在情感上，很多年幼孩子的父母会想：人生只有一次，孩子长得快，这几年太珍贵了。

cues.en: Let's drain the savings account, max out the credit cards, let's do whatever it takes to make this happen. I acknowledge that these aren't poor families. They're fortunate enough to have savings accounts and lines of credit in the first place, but they're not wealthy. And for many, taking a Disney vacation means taking on a financial burden or risk. Maybe you'll be in a precarious position the next time you have car trouble. Maybe you go into debt to pay for it. Maybe there are just material comforts in your day to day life that you sacrifice for a long time to save up. And with that in mind,
cues.zh: 那就掏空存款，刷爆信用卡，不惜一切代价也要成行。我承认这些家庭并不穷，他们起码有存款和信用额度，算是幸运的，但他们并不富裕。对许多人来说，去迪士尼度假意味着背上经济负担或风险。也许下次车子出问题时，你的财务状况会岌岌可危。也许你会为此负债。也许你在日常生活中长期牺牲一些物质享受来攒钱。想到这些，

cues.en: yeah, it does matter to me emotionally
cues.zh: 没错，从情感上讲，

cues.en: whether the people doing that get their money's worth. Obviously, the Star Cruiser was leagues beyond what even a typical Disney World trip would cost. But I believe that in rolling out the experience, Disney was essentially cashing in decades of goodwill. Disney has always had high prices, but they also have a reputation for quality. This was more than they've ever charged for an experience before, so the logic followed that this would be the greatest experience they've ever offered. Around the time it opened, the number one question I saw everyone ask about the Galactic Star Cruiser was, is it worth it? And after my own trip, I watched a lot of other people's reviews, and I saw that most of them, especially the ones who went for free, seemed to just say, if you have the money, it's worth it. And that answer is so unhelpful,
cues.zh: 这些花钱去体验的人到底值不值，对我来说确实很重要。显然，Star Cruiser的价格比普通的迪士尼世界之旅还要高出好几个量级。但我认为，迪士尼在推出这个项目时，实际上是在变现几十年积累的口碑。迪士尼的价格一直很高，但他们也有品质的口碑。这是他们有史以来对一项体验收过的最高价格，所以按理说，这应该是他们有史以来提供过的最棒的体验。在它开业前后，我看到大家问得最多的一个问题就是：Galactic Star Cruiser值不值？在我自己体验过后，我看了很多其他人的评测，发现大多数人——尤其是免费去的人——似乎都只会说：如果你有钱，那就值。这个回答实在没什么用，

cues.en: and in my opinion, willfully obtuse. Things have value.
cues.zh: 在我看来，甚至是故意装糊涂。事物是有价值的。

cues.en: Something either costs a fair amount or it doesn't. Like, I'm willing to bet that a lot of middle class families technically have access to $6,000
cues.zh: 某个东西要么要花不少钱，要么不花；这么说吧，我敢打赌，很多中产阶级家庭严格来说能拿出 6000 美元。

cues.en: in savings or in assets, But they don't wanna waste that money. If they spend it, they wanna know that they couldn't have had a better value or a better experience doing something else with it instead. Like, okay, I love Taco Bell nachos. I love them so much. At time of filming, those cost a little under $3. If someone asked me if they were worth it, I would say, yes, certainly. If tomorrow they suddenly cost $20, I would immediately be able to say, oh, mm-mm, no. No, they're not worth that. I wouldn't say, well, I really like them, so I suppose if you can afford it, they're worth it. I would say, no. They're worth around $3,
cues.zh: 无论是存款还是资产，他们都不想浪费那笔钱。如果要花，他们希望确定，拿这笔钱做别的事，不可能获得更高的价值或更好的体验。比如，我很喜欢 Taco Bell 的玉米片，真的特别喜欢。拍摄时，它们的价格还不到 3 美元。如果有人问我值不值，我会说，当然值。可如果明天它们突然涨到 20 美元，我马上就会说，呃，不，不值。不是说“我确实很喜欢，所以只要你买得起，就值得”。我会说，不，它们大概就值 3 美元。

cues.en: maybe up to 5 if I was desperate. Do not spend $20
