cues.en: on those, unless you're watching this in the future, and because of inflation, Taco Bell nachos are now that price. Hello, traveler.
cues.zh: 买那些，除非你是从未来看这个视频的，而且因为通货膨胀，Taco Bell 的玉米片也变成这个价了。你好啊，时空旅行者。

cues.en: I'm so happy you still have Taco Bell. So anyway, I think it's really interesting that a lot of people magically lost their ability to conceptualize value as soon as they were gifted an expensive trip by a big company. Listen, I know you have to play nice if you wanna stay on the p r list, but if you're not using that access to give an honest review, then what's the point of being there at all? What good are you to anybody? Have you no sense of integrity?
cues.zh:
我真高兴你们还有 Taco Bell。
总之，我觉得很有意思：很多人一收到大公司送的昂贵旅行，就神奇地失去了理解价值的能力。
听着，我知道你想留在 PR 名单上就得好好配合，但如果你不利用这种机会给出诚实的评测，那你去那儿到底有什么意义？
你对别人又有什么好处？
你难道没有一点操守吗？

cues.en: No self respect? So was it worth it? I've been to many, many theme parks, many themed experiences,
cues.zh: 不要自尊了吗？那值得吗？我去过很多很多主题公园，很多主题体验，

cues.en: paid for many, specifically Disney theme park themed experiences.
cues.zh: 花钱体验了很多，尤其是迪士尼乐园主题的体验。

cues.en: I've been a repeat customer because a lot of the time, I do think it's worth what they're charging. And I've come to understand that with Disney, you can always expect to pay inflated prices compared to what you would pay another vendor for a similar product. I can pick something up in a Disney gift shop and usually guess within a dollar what overpriced amount they're charging for it. What I'm saying is I understand the Disney price scale. I know the value of specifically Disney experiences.
cues.zh: 我之所以会反复消费，是因为很多时候，我确实觉得他们收的价格还算值得。而且我也逐渐明白，对于 Disney 来说，相比其他商家提供类似产品时的价格，你总可以预期他们会收取更高的价格。我在 Disney 礼品店里拿起一样东西，通常都能猜到他们会收多少虚高的价格，误差不会超过一美元。我的意思是，我理解 Disney 的定价水平。我知道 Disney 体验本身的价值。

cues.en: And you better believe I've seen a lot of defenders of the Star Cruiser trying to justify the price. Some of whom went for free, had friends who helped build it, or literally worked there. While I may have some personal involvement with the Star Cruiser, I feel I have a responsibility to my amazing followers and this TikTok community to quickly break down what's included so you can come to your own conclusion if it's actually worth the price tag. So anyway, they always try to do an itemized cost breakdown,
cues.zh: 你肯定也清楚，我见过很多Star Cruiser的维护者试图为它的价格辩护。其中一些人免费去的，有朋友参与建造，或者真的在那里工作过。虽然我和Star Cruiser可能有些个人关系，但我觉得有责任为我超棒的粉丝和这个TikTok社区快速拆解一下包含哪些内容，这样你们可以自己判断它到底值不值这个价。总之，他们总是想做一个逐项成本明细，

cues.en: inflating the value of each item in the column as they go. Like comparing the cost of the room to the price of Disney's most luxurious hotels, even though the Star Cruiser rooms aren't nearly as nice. And a theme park view, because you're getting views of the galaxy and going into hyperspace.
cues.zh: 一路抬高这一列中每一项的价值。就像把房间费用和迪士尼最豪华酒店的价格相比，尽管 Star Cruiser 的房间远没那么好。还有一个主题公园景观，因为你能看到银河景色，还会进入超空间。

cues.en: So when you do that, in an average of 1,250
cues.zh: 所以当你这么算，按平均每晚 1,250

cues.en: per night, that would be a total of $2,500
cues.zh: 美元的价格，总共就是 $2,500

cues.en: for both nights on the Halcyon. Forgetting that hotels charge per night, not per person. Pretending that the character story moments have the same monetary value as twenty two hours of consecutive Broadway shows. The Galactic Star Cruiser is a literal two day Broadway show that you become a part of. Doing the math because a typical theatrical show is around two hours, that's $1,650
cues.zh: ——这是 Halcyon 号两晚的价钱。这是忘了酒店按晚收费，而不是按人头。这是假装那些角色剧情时刻和连续二十二小时的百老汇演出有同等的货币价值。Galactic Star Cruiser 简直就是一场为期两天的百老汇演出，而你可以亲身参与其中。来算笔账：一场典型的戏剧演出大约两小时，也就是说你花了 $1,650

cues.en: you're paying for the live entertainment. Which, no matter how talented the performers are, is simply not the case. Pretending that your car getting valet parked once is a $200 value, even though most guests arrive by taxi anyway. And then after all this, when they still fail to match the lowest possible quoted price for a Star Cruiser trip, they'll just add something at the end like, also it's unique, which is worth the rest of the dollars. For the record, I consider all of this an exercise in futility. The entire point of flat rate bundled experiences like cruises or all inclusive resorts is that by paying for everything as a lump sum, you're meant to be getting some kind of deal. The company is also getting a deal in the sense that they know none of your trip money is going to competitors, and it's all going directly to them, which is why bundles like this are so common. I also think it's ridiculous that these cost breakdowns itemize so many of the amenities. You can't say a hotel room is worth $600
cues.zh: 来看现场演艺。而无论演员多有才华，事实都绝非如此。这是假装你的车被代客泊车一次就值 $200，尽管大多数客人反正都是打车来的。而在做完这一切之后，当他们算出的数字仍然够不上 Star Cruiser 之旅可能的最低报价时，他们就只会在最后补一句诸如“而且它是独一无二的”，好把剩下的美元给凑上。郑重声明，我认为这一切都是白费功夫。像邮轮或全包度假村这种一口价打包体验，其全部意义就在于：把所有费用一次性付清，你应该能因此得到某种实惠。公司也从中得利，因为他们知道你的旅行花销一分都不会流向竞争对手，而是全部直接进了他们的口袋，这也正是这类打包产品如此常见的原因。我还觉得这些费用明细把这么多设施服务逐项列出，实在荒谬。你不能一边说一间客房值 $600

cues.en: a night, and then also itemize the cost of the customer service, the valet parking, and the snacks in the lobby, because at any good $600 a night hotel, that stuff would be included anyway. So I promise you, I'm keeping everything in mind for my value estimate. I'm keeping in mind that the room, while tiny, is unique. I'm keeping in mind that there are interactive performers on board, that the food was yummy, that there were mini games, that we got a couple hours in the theme park, that Disney prices are inflated. Factoring it all in. And let me be frank, in my opinion, the experience I had was worth approximately
cues.zh: 一晚，然后又把客服、代客泊车和大堂零食的成本单独计价，因为在任何一家像样的 $600 一晚的酒店，这些本来都是包含在内的。所以我向你保证，我做价值估算时把一切都考虑在内了。我考虑到了房间虽然狭小，但独一无二。我考虑到了船上有互动演员、食物很好吃、有小游戏、我们在主题公园玩了几个小时，还有迪士尼的价格本来就虚高。全都算进去了。坦白说，在我看来，我这次体验的价值大约是

cues.en: total per adult. $1,000
cues.zh: 每位成年人。最多 $1,000

cues.en: maximum,
cues.zh: 封顶，

cues.en: and kids should cost less. But during Star Cruiser's entire existence, depending on whether you went in summer or winter, and depending on how many people you felt like cramming into that tiny room, you could expect to pay anywhere from two times to four times that amount. And that's just not worth it for what it was. If they had offered a hefty discount or extended the duration of the experience, I might feel differently, but they didn't, so I don't. Also, obviously, if the Star Cruiser was a cheaper experience, it wouldn't have mattered so much that the gameplay element was so unreliable. You would think of the cost as covering the underwhelming room, the nice food, and the access to the theme park rides, and the gameplay would just feel like a bonus. So you'd feel a lot more comfortable sitting it out if it wasn't your speed, and less disappointed if you tried to participate and it didn't work properly. So no, I would never say it's worth it if you can afford it. I would probably say something more like, you might have fun doing this if you're so wealthy that you don't mind being overcharged for experiences
cues.zh: 而且小孩应该更便宜。但在 Star Cruiser 存在的整个时期，根据你去的是夏季还是冬季，以及你愿意往那个小房间里塞多少人，你实际要付的钱大约是这个价的两到四倍。就它实际的样子而言，这根本不值。如果他们肯打个大幅折扣，或者延长体验时长，我的看法也许会不一样，但他们没有，所以我不改口。另外，显然，如果 Star Cruiser 是个更便宜的体验，玩法环节这么不可靠也就不会那么要紧了。你会把这笔钱看作是覆盖了平平无奇的房间、不错的食物和主题公园游乐设施的入场资格，而玩法就像个附赠的彩头。这样，如果玩法不对你的胃口，你大可以安心跳过；如果你想参与却出了故障，也不会那么失望。所以不，我绝不会说“只要你负担得起就值”。我更可能会这么说：如果你富裕到不在乎为体验被多宰

cues.en: to the tune of thousands of dollars. And even within that demographic, I would still add that the people most likely to have fun at Star Cruiser would be children ages seven to 12. Based on my own childhood playing Neopets, I believe that's the age range in which kids have the most patience for completing busy work games in exchange for meaningless points. I also think kids at that age probably wouldn't be so cognizant of how little their choices were affecting their story outcomes, so they would be harder to disappoint. I mean, when I was little, my mom would play video games and hand me a controller that wasn't plugged in, and I had fun. So the Star Cruiser is kinda like that. I think the building is small enough with only one entrance and exit that you could pretty comfortably turn kids loose and let them run around the ship on their own, which would be a huge novelty to them. All the kids I saw around age 10 looked like they were having an incredible time, and their parents were just beaming with pride, because I could tell they felt like they were super dad for setting the whole thing up. I also think the concept was broad enough that kids wouldn't even have to have an interest or familiarity with Star Wars to enjoy it. However, I would also keep in mind that kids might have an equivalent amount of fun if you book them a weekend at the Great Wolf Lodge for like a $100 a person. Or if you're really determined to spend $5,000,
cues.zh: 几千美元，那你也许会玩得开心。即便在这个人群里，我仍要补充一句：最有可能在 Star Cruiser 玩得开心的是七到十二岁的孩子。基于我自己小时候玩 Neopets 的经历，我相信这个年龄段的孩子最有耐心去完成那些琐事小游戏，以换取毫无意义的积分。我也认为这个年龄的孩子大概不太会意识到自己的选择对剧情走向的影响有多小，所以他们更难失望。我小时候，我妈玩游戏时会塞给我一个没插线的手柄，我也玩得很开心。Star Cruiser 就有点像这样。我觉得这栋楼面积不大，只有一个出入口，所以你完全可以放心地放手让孩子自己在船上跑来跑去，这对他们来说是件超级新鲜的事。我见到的所有十岁左右的孩子看起来都玩得特别开心，而他们的父母满脸骄傲，因为我能感觉到他们觉得自己安排了这一切，简直是最棒的爸爸。我还觉得这个概念的包容度够广，孩子就算对《星球大战》没有兴趣或了解也一样能玩得尽兴。不过我也要提醒一句：如果你给孩子订个大狼屋（Great Wolf Lodge）的周末，大概每人 $100，他们可能也能收获同样多的快乐。或者，如果你真心铁了心要花掉 $5,000，

cues.en: you can just give it to them in cash and let them go ham at Chuck E. Cheese. At least that way, they'd earn it all back in finger traps and novelty giant pencils. So I guess my point is that it would be truly hard to justify this expense, even if you fell within the best possible highly specific demographic.
cues.zh: 你完全可以直接给他们现金，让他们去 Chuck E. Cheese 尽情玩。至少这样，他们还能靠手指陷阱和新奇巨型铅笔把这些钱全赚回来。所以我想说的是，这笔开销真的很难合理化，哪怕你正好属于最理想、极其精准的那类目标人群。

cues.en: And here's my supporting evidence.
cues.zh: 这是我的佐证。

cues.en: The hotel went out of business. If the value of something is what people are willing to pay, I can objectively say the Disney company charged too much for this experience, because time showed that the majority of people on this earth were not willing to pay it. And yet, I should say that Star Cruiser did earn itself something of a cult following among a small number of people who went. In my time researching Star Cruiser, I noticed an interesting phenomenon throughout the fan groups. One talking point I've seen reiterated again and again is that even though Star Cruiser closed, it was a perfect product. It was too pure for this world, or the mainstream wasn't nerdy enough to appreciate it, or it wasn't advertised well enough, or it was totally worth the money. It wasn't Disney's fault. All you broke boys couldn't afford it. It was screwed by the marketing and the haters online,
cues.zh: 这家酒店倒闭了。如果一件东西的价值就是人们愿意为它付多少钱，那我可以客观地说，迪士尼公司对这次体验收费过高，因为时间证明，这个世界上大多数人并不愿意付这个价。不过我也得说，Star Cruiser 确实在一小批去过的人当中收获了一种小众的狂热追随。在我研究 Star Cruiser 的那段时间里，我注意到粉丝群里有一个有趣的现象。我一次又一次看到被反复提起的一个论调是：虽然 Star Cruiser 关门了，但它是个完美的产品。它对这个世界来说太纯粹了，或者主流人群不够宅、欣赏不来，或者它宣传得不够好，或者它完全值这个钱。这不是迪士尼的错。都是你们这些穷哥们付不起。它是被营销和网上的黑子搞砸的，

cues.en: but actually everyone who went unanimously loved it. The thing is, that's just not true. Over the year and a half the Star Cruiser was open, I saw loads of comments from people who were very excited to go and left extremely disappointed. And wouldn't you know it, a lot of them had the exact same issues I did. General issues with the app glitching or freezing. Character performers being too swamped to interact with. Arriving five minutes early to a scheduled story moment, only to find that it had begun fifteen minutes early and they'd missed it entirely. Beginning a dialogue tree in the app, only to get left unread by the AI, barring them from joining any storylines. Performing actions in the gameplay, which didn't appear to register in their profiles. Story outcomes that seemed random. Some guests went to guest services during their trip and were able to have these issues corrected. But sometimes doing so wasted hours of an experience where every second counts. And of course, there were other times when the IT department tried to help and simply wasn't able to and gave up. Plenty of people went home feeling like they had missed out on the experience and like they weren't able to properly participate in the story. The more I read, the more I realized that even guests who initially said they had a great time would later admit that the gameplay had not worked right for them. And I find this crucial to mention, because again, the gameplay is ostensibly the entire justification for the inflated price of this experience. In fact, not to put anyone on blast by playing clips, but if you watch a lot of the vlogs from people who enjoyed it, many of these people seem not to have even attempted the gameplay at all. A lot of people just took photos, hung out at the bar all day, or even did unsanctioned scavenger hunts they'd organized for their own group. And I'm not going to say none of that is fun, but how can you then say that's worth $6,000
cues.zh: 但实际上，每个去过的人都一致爱它。问题是，这根本不是真的。在 Star Cruiser 开放的一年半里，我看到大量评论来自那些一开始很兴奋要去、最后却极其失望的人。你猜怎么着，他们中很多人遇到的问题和我一模一样。普遍问题是 app 出故障或卡死。角色演员太忙，根本没空互动。提前五分钟到达预定好的剧情时刻，却发现它提前十五分钟就开始了，他们完全错过了。在 app 里开始一个对话树，结果被 AI 已读不回，导致他们无法加入任何剧情线。在玩法中执行动作，却没在个人资料里记录。故事结果看起来随机。有些游客在旅程中去找游客服务处，能够把这些问题修好。但有时候这么做会浪费好几个小时，而这段体验里每一秒都很宝贵。当然，也有其他时候，IT 部门试图帮忙，却根本帮不上，只好放弃。很多人回家时觉得自己错过了这次体验，觉得自己没能真正参与进故事。我读得越多，就越意识到，就连一开始说自己玩得很开心的游客，后来也会承认玩法对他们并没有正常运作。我觉得这点必须提，因为再说一次，玩法表面上正是这次体验定价虚高的全部理由。事实上，我不想放片段来公开点名谁，但如果你看很多觉得好玩的 vlog，其中不少人似乎压根没尝试过玩法。很多人只是拍照、整天泡在酒吧，甚至自己给同行的人组织未经官方允许的寻宝活动。我不会说这些都不好玩，但你怎么能说它值 6000 美元

cues.en: when you could do all of that at your local Dave and Buster's? Despite the apparent frequency of the gameplay issues, whenever I saw people mention them in the fan groups, they would be quickly shouted down by other fans. They were often polite, but they would tell them that these issues were simply their own fault for somehow playing the game wrong. No one else has had these problems you're talking about, so clearly it's on you. You get what you put into it, so maybe you didn't try hard enough. You ruined your experience by trying too hard. You weren't a big enough nerd to appreciate it. You're a lying hater who's only pretending the Star Cruiser is bad probably because you're jealous you couldn't afford it. The app doesn't do anything. You need to talk to the actors. The actors don't do anything. You need to use the app. You played the game wrong. You were supposed to pick one specific storyline to follow. You played the game wrong, you were not supposed to pick one specific storyline to follow. You must not have had an exciting enough costume. And my personal favorite,
cues.zh: 而你完全可以在本地 Dave and Buster's 做所有这些事？尽管玩法问题明显很常见，但每当我在粉丝群里看到有人提到这些问题，他们很快就会被其他粉丝压下去。他们通常还算礼貌，但会告诉对方，这些问题纯粹是他们自己的错，因为不知怎么地把游戏玩错了。除了你，没人遇到过你说的这些问题，所以显然是你的问题。你投入多少就得到多少，所以也许是你不够努力。你因为太努力而毁了自己的体验。你不够宅，欣赏不来。你是个撒谎的黑子，只是假装 Star Cruiser 很糟糕，大概是因为你嫉妒自己付不起钱。app 什么都不管用，你得去和演员互动。演员什么都不管用，你得去用 app。你把游戏玩错了。你应该选一个特定剧情线来跟。你把游戏玩错了，你不该选一个特定剧情线来跟。你一定是没穿足够精彩的服装。还有我个人最喜欢的，

cues.en: you must have the wrong personality.
cues.zh: 那你一定是性格不对。

cues.en: Finally, failing all other ways to blame the customer, people will just say, oh, it sounds like you were just unlucky.
cues.zh: 最后，在把所有其他怪罪顾客的办法都用尽之后，人们只会说，哦，听起来你只是运气不好。

cues.en: That's too bad because it was great for everyone else. And they say this as if it's acceptable for so many people to be unlucky in a way that breaks a $6,000
cues.zh: 那太糟了，因为对其他人来说它很棒。他们说这话，就好像那么多人以毁掉一次价值6000美元体验的

cues.en: experience. So I'm just preparing you, if you see any die hard fans making any of these excuses in the comments, they're not good enough. Besides, none of them even apply to me. I dressed up, I'm good at immersive games,
cues.zh: 方式走霉运，是可以接受的。所以我只是先提醒你，如果你在评论区看到任何死忠粉用这些借口，那些借口都不成立。再说，它们没有一条适用于我。我认真打扮了，我也擅长沉浸式游戏，

cues.en: and I have possibly one of the best personalities in the world. I'm also going to go ahead and predict this now. This same demographic of people are going to see the words Star Wars Hotel in my video title and say, that just goes to show she knows nothing about it and she probably didn't even go, because she called it a hotel when it's so much more than that. Nothing she says even matters because we know she's so ignorant. They say this all the time, even though it literally is a hotel and Disney first announced it as a hotel and the general public knows it as the Star Wars Hotel. If I call my video this, no one's gonna click it, are they? So I can't wait to be gatekept for calling this what everyone knows it as and what it literally is. You're probably wondering where this defensiveness would even come from. From them, not from me, I'm not defensive. These people didn't build the hotel with their bare hands. Why do they care if I didn't like it? Firstly, I think it's just the sunk cost fallacy. If you've invested a lot of time into being a fan of something, you feel the need to defend it unconditionally.
cues.zh: 而且我大概是世界上性格最好的人之一。我现在就大胆预测一下。同一类人看到我视频标题里的 Star Wars Hotel 几个字，就会说：这就说明她根本不懂，而且她可能根本没去过，因为她居然叫它酒店，而它远不止是酒店。她说什么都不重要，因为我们知道她太无知了。他们总这么说，尽管它字面上就是酒店，Disney 最初也以酒店之名公布，公众也把它叫作 Star Wars Hotel。如果我把视频这么命名，没人会点，对吧？所以我迫不及待地等着，因为用大家都知道的、字面上也正确的名字称呼它而被指手画脚。你可能想知道这种防御心态到底从何而来。来自他们，不是我，我可不防御。这些人又不是亲手建了这家酒店。我不喜欢又关他们什么事？首先，我觉得这不过是沉没成本谬误。如果你花了大量时间成为某事物的粉丝，就会觉得自己必须无条件捍卫它。

cues.en: Secondly, for profit. Many of the vocal defenders of Star Cruiser are themselves theme park vloggers or podcasters.
cues.zh: 其次，为了利益。许多公开为 Star Cruiser 辩护的人本身就是主题公园视频博主或播客。

cues.en: This is a content genre whose biggest selling point is often encouraging your fans to live vicariously through you, as you go to Disney World every day and do experiences they can't afford. In this way, the better the products looks, the more successful your vlogs will be. It's also a field where early access to new offerings can make or break your channel, so people desperately want to get on the media list, and those on it desperately want to stay on it, which doesn't happen if you're critical. Some of the foremost Star Cruiser influencers were even themselves travel agents who sold Star Cruiser packages.
cues.zh: 这种内容类型最大的卖点，常常是鼓励粉丝通过你间接体验——你每天去 Disney World，玩他们负担不起的项目。这样一来，产品看起来越好，你的视频博客就越成功。这个领域里，抢先体验新项目能成就也能毁掉你的频道，所以人们拼命想进媒体名单，进了名单的人又拼命想留在上面；如果你爱批评，就留不住。一些最顶尖的 Star Cruiser 网红本人就是销售 Star Cruiser 套餐的旅行社代理。

cues.en: So one could argue that there's an even more direct monetary incentive to make it look good. But I care most about the final reason. The price of the experience has forced fans to be very defensive over their decision to go. If you book a $5,000 theme park experience and then mention it to a random coworker,
cues.zh: 所以可以说，把它说得好看还有更直接的金钱激励。但我最在意最后一个原因。这项体验的价格迫使粉丝极力为自己去的决定辩护。如果你预订了一次5000美元的主题公园体验，然后随口告诉一个同事，

cues.en: they're probably going to be like, you're nuts. Everyone is talking about how this thing is way too expensive and will never be worth it. So once that's out there, you now have to enjoy this experience. Because if you go and then come home and are like, it wasn't that good or even it was just okay, you worry that you'll look like a fool. And to that I say, I don't think any of you guys are fools. I mean, you were fooled in a literal sense, but that's not embarrassing.
cues.zh: 他们大概会说，你疯了。所有人都在说这东西太贵了，永远不值。所以一旦说出口，你现在就必须享受这次体验。因为如果你去了，回家后说“没那么好”，甚至“就还行”，你会担心自己看起来像个傻瓜。对此我想说，我不觉得你们任何人是傻瓜。我是说，你们确实在字面意义上被耍了，但那并不丢人。

cues.en: It's Disney that should be embarrassed for taking advantage of their fans. So by all that I mean,
cues.zh: 该羞愧的是迪士尼，它利用了自己的粉丝。所以我的意思是，

cues.en: no.
cues.zh: 不。

cues.en: It wasn't worth it. Part 18,
cues.zh: 这不值得。第 18 部分，

cues.en: why did it fail? After about six months of being open, that first wave of super fans and influencers who wanted to book the Galactic Star Cruiser dried up. Theme park busybodies noticed that the booking page on the website had more and more availability as time wore on. Guests visiting reported that the hotel was often running at half capacity,
cues.zh: 它为什么失败了？开业大约六个月后，第一批想预订 Galactic Star Cruiser 的超级粉丝和网红就消退了。主题公园圈内人注意到，随着时间推移，网站预订页面上的空位越来越多。到访客人反映，这家酒店经常只有一半入住率，

cues.en: which was very apparent because they would cut the two dinner seatings down to one, and you could still see visibly empty tables at that one dinner seating. Staff also started to report that their hours were being cut. Pretty much everyone following the story had correctly predicted that the Star Cruiser would see totally full bookings for only a few months, while theme park news outlets and influencers got their fill, and then interest would wane. But because it was so widely predicted, everyone just assumed that Disney also expected this to happen, and they probably baked it into their initial price structure. Maybe it just cost so much because they didn't expect it to be booked all the time. And if Disney did want the hotel to be full, everyone just assumed they would adjust the prices lower, and that would bring the interest back up, and then they could reach some kind of equilibrium.
cues.zh: 这一点非常明显，因为他们会把两场晚餐缩减成一场，而那一场晚餐上仍能明显看到空桌。员工也开始反映自己的工时被削减。几乎所有关注这件事的人都准确预测过，Star Cruiser 只会有几个月的满订期——主题公园新闻媒体和网红先来体验，然后兴趣就会减退。但正因为大家都这么预测，所有人都想当然地认为迪士尼也预料到了，并且很可能已经把这一点算进初始定价结构里。也许它之所以这么贵，只是因为他们没指望它一直满订。而如果迪士尼确实想让酒店满房，大家就觉得他们会把价格调低，这会重新拉回兴趣，然后达到某种平衡。

cues.en: But none of that ever happened. It's surprising to me how little Disney appeared to try to salvage this project. Even as sales declined, they refused to budge on the prices. They did offer some discounts in the last six months of operation,
cues.zh: 但这些都没有发生。让我惊讶的是，迪士尼似乎几乎没怎么尝试挽救这个项目。即使销量下滑，他们也拒绝在价格上让步。运营最后六个月，他们确实提供了一些折扣，

cues.en: but those were only for Disney Visa card holders and members of their time share program.
cues.zh: 但只面向 Disney Visa 卡持卡人和其分时度假计划会员。

cues.en: And even then, it was only when booking for specific dates. So yeah, it seemed like all along Disney really had expected this hotel to keep costing over 5 k and keep selling out. An unfathomable level of hubris in my opinion. When this didn't prove to be true, I predicted that Disney was going to stay the course for a few more years, and then retool the story and kind of relaunch the experience. You know, they could reuse all the effects, but set it in a new time period, and have characters like Darth Vader and the Mandalorian showing up. Then the people who had already booked the first time would have incentive to come back, and they would presumably unlock a whole new demographic of people who don't care about the sequels. But nope,
cues.zh: 而且即便如此，也只适用于预订特定日期。所以是的，看起来迪士尼一直真的指望这家酒店持续收费超过 5k 并且一直售罄。在我看来，这是难以理解的傲慢。当事实证明并非如此时，我预测迪士尼会再坚持几年，然后调整故事、某种程度上重新推出这个体验。你知道，他们可以复用所有特效，但把背景设定在新的时间段，让 Darth Vader 和 Mandalorian 这样的角色出现。这样，第一次已经预订过的人会有动力回来，而且他们大概还能开拓一个全新的、不在乎续集的人群。但没有，

cues.en: they decided to just throw in the towel altogether. The news of the closure was very abrupt,
cues.zh: 他们决定直接彻底放弃。关闭的消息非常突然，

cues.en: as in they announced it in May and it was going to happen in September. This means at the time of the announcement,
cues.zh: 也就是说，他们在 5 月宣布，而关闭将在 9 月发生。这意味着在宣布时，

cues.en: there were already dates on the booking calendar and guests had already reserved spots for dates which would now be canceled. So Disney immediately froze bookings on the website. They called any guests with existing reservations beyond the closing date and offered them either refunds or the first chance to rebook. And then once all those rebookings were done, very few spots remained for any new guests looking to book a room. And obviously, there was demand for that because a lot of people were kind of curious about the Star Cruiser, but thought they would have forever to decide to go. When they reopened booking to the public, all the remaining reservations were booked in a matter of hours. So as you can see, the last minute announcement of the closure screwed over both Disney and the fans. If Disney had announced a pending closure and given everybody like a year to get their fill of Star Cruiser, they probably would have been booked up that whole year. By closing it as suddenly as they did, they were leaving money on the table. This also seemed to be a snap decision. In March 2023, Disney announced that instead of offering as many consecutive cruises as possible running one after the other, they would start to offer only two bookings per week, with three days in between where the Star Cruiser sat empty. But when they announced that, they said the schedule change would take effect in October
cues.zh: 预订日历上已经有日期了，客人也已经预订了如今将被取消的日期名额。于是迪士尼立刻冻结了网站上的预订。他们给所有预订日期超过关闭日期的客人打电话，提供退款或优先重新预订的机会。等这些重新预订都完成后，面向想订房的新客人剩下的名额已经很少。显然，这方面是有需求的，因为很多人对 Star Cruiser 有点好奇，但以为自己永远有时间决定去。当他们向公众重新开放预订时，所有剩余预订在几小时内就被订完了。所以你看，最后一刻才宣布关闭，把迪士尼和粉丝都坑了。如果迪士尼提前宣布即将关闭，并给大家比如一年时间去体验够 Star Cruiser，那它很可能那一整年都会被订满。像他们这样突然关闭，等于白白错失了收入。这似乎也是个仓促决定。2023 年 3 月，迪士尼宣布，他们不再尽可能连续排满航次、一个接一个运行，而是每周只提供两次预订，中间空三天，Star Cruiser 就闲置着。但宣布时，他们说时间表变更将在 10 月生效

cues.en: They even rolled out this new calendar on the booking website. So clearly at that point, they didn't yet anticipate that in October 2023, the Star Cruiser would no longer exist. New merchandise products popped up in the gift shop throughout the final year, like this action figure of the AI droid from the console in the guest rooms. This didn't even become available until July 2023. In early May of twenty twenty three, guests of the hotel reported seeing executives and Imagineers visiting the Star Cruiser. One assumes this must have been to assess how things were running or consider improvements.
cues.zh: 他们甚至还在预订网站上推出了这套新日历。所以很明显，在当时，他们还没预料到 Star Cruiser 会在 2023 年 10 月不复存在。最后一年里，礼品店不断推出新的商品，比如这款客房控制台里的 AI 机器人玩偶。直到 2023 年 7 月，这款玩偶才正式上市。2023 年 5 月初，酒店住客报告说，他们看到高管和 Imagineers 到访 Star Cruiser。有人认为，他们此行应该是为了评估运营情况，或是考虑改进方案。

cues.en: Maybe in hindsight, that could have been a sign trouble in that the Imagineers could have been brainstorming ways to try to save it. But it doesn't feel like something they would bother with if they already knew the closure was imminent. And yet, the permanent closure was announced just two weeks after that visit. Executives obviously chose the abrupt closure date because the fiscal year ended on September 30, and Disney's plan was to write the entire hotel off as a loss. The loss of the hotel would bring in a $300,000,000
cues.zh: 现在回头看，这或许是个麻烦的信号，说明 Imagineers 可能正在集思广益，想办法挽救它。但如果他们已经知道酒店即将关闭，那就很难想象他们还会费心做这些事。然而，那次访问仅仅两周后，永久关闭的消息就公布了。高管们显然选择了这个突然关闭的日期，因为财年在 9 月 30 日结束，而 Disney 的计划是把整家酒店作为亏损核销。酒店的亏损可以带来 3 亿美元的

cues.en: tax break, and they wanted it for that year. So in my opinion, the reasons the Star Cruiser failed were obvious. From the moment it was announced, everyone predicted it would fail. The marketing sucked. Not a lot of people even understood what it really was. It was way too expensive to an extent that the only buzz it received was mockery of the price tag. And this is all a surprise to no one. So I think the more constructive question is, why couldn't it be safe? The Star Cruiser was a project with so many fatal flaws, I think it would have been very difficult to salvage. Built by a company so confident in their inability to fail, that they left no flexibility for adjustments down the line. The biggest obstacle to this experience's marketability was the ridiculous cost. So one of the most obvious moves to save the project would have been to lower the cost. Unfortunately,
cues.zh: 税收减免，而他们希望把这笔减免计入当年的财务报表。所以在我看来，Star Cruiser 失败的原因显而易见。从它公布的那一刻起，所有人都预料到它会失败。营销做得很糟。甚至没多少人真正理解它到底是什么。它贵得离谱，以至于它获得的唯一热度就是人们嘲笑它的价格。而这一切完全不让人意外。所以我认为，更有建设性的问题是：为什么它没能被挽救？Star Cruiser 是一个存在如此多致命缺陷的项目，我认为要挽救它会非常困难。它由一家自信到认为自己绝不会失败的公司打造，因此没有为日后的调整留下任何弹性。这个体验项目能否被市场接受，最大的障碍就是荒谬的高价。所以，挽救项目最显而易见的办法之一，就是降低价格。遗憾的是，

cues.en: while building it, Disney was so confident in their ability to command a high price that they blocked off most avenues to ever do so. The physical building itself was constructed with very high prices in mind. It has only a 100 rooms with a maximum occupancy of about 500 guests. The atrium is built to accommodate that number of guests with very little wiggle room. The only dining room can hold half the capacity of guests and relies on two separate dinner seating times with staggered lunches and breakfasts. Any hotel in the world has a baseline cost to run just by existing. A minimum number of cleaners, servers, and concierge you need on staff, a baseline cost to keep the lights on, and in this case, they're also paying the actors. Disney is accustomed to high profits on all their hotels.
cues.zh: 在建造过程中，Disney 对自己能够收取高价充满信心，以至于堵死了今后这么做的大多数途径。建筑本身就是按照高价运营的思路建造的。它只有 100 间客房，最多容纳大约 500 名住客。中庭的设计就是为了容纳这么多住客，几乎没有多少余量。唯一的餐厅只能容纳一半的住客，因此必须分成两轮晚餐，并错开午餐和早餐的用餐时间。世界上任何一家酒店，只要存在，就有一套基本运营成本。你需要配备最低数量的清洁人员、服务员和礼宾人员，还要承担维持照明等设施运转的基本成本，而在这个案例中，他们还要支付演员的薪酬。Disney 习惯于从旗下所有酒店中获取高额利润。

cues.en: So with only a 100 rooms, they would need to charge a lot per room just to make it worth their while. But they can't simply add more rooms to lower the average cost, because then they'd need to do a total overhaul of the rest of the structure. Common areas such as the atrium, the lounge, the activity rooms, the landings on each floor are fairly small. There are only two elevators with which to navigate between themed floors, and only one functional elevator through which to access the lobby. I know it looks like there are two, but reportedly the left elevator is actually just a dummy elevator. It's a maintenance access door. The atrium can hold the current maximum occupancy of hotel guests, but when it does, it feels pretty crowded. They rely on the gameplay a lot of the time to disperse the crowds into different areas of the ship, so you don't notice how physically small it is. So they can't drop the price without adding more rooms, but they can't add more rooms without remodeling the bulk of the building to make a bigger bigger atrium, bigger lounge, probably several additional dining rooms unless guests are willing to eat dinner at very odd times. And for the record, I'm not telling you all this to justify Disney's prices. This is an unsolvable problem,
cues.zh: 所以只有 100 间客房的话，他们就得把每间房的价格定得很高，才值得经营。但他们不能单纯增加客房来降低平均成本，因为那就得彻底改造建筑的其他部分。中庭、休息室、活动室和每层楼的休息平台等公共区域都相当狭小。主题楼层之间只有两部电梯，而通往大堂的可用电梯只有一部。我知道看起来有两部，但据说左边那部其实只是摆设，是一道维修通道门。中庭能容纳酒店目前允许的最多住客，但人一多就会显得相当拥挤。他们很多时候得靠游戏环节把人群分散到飞船的不同区域，这样你才不会注意到它实际上有多小。所以他们不能降价，除非增加客房；但要增加客房，就得重新规划建筑的大部分区域，打造更大的中庭和休息室，还可能得增设好几个餐厅，除非客人愿意在很奇怪的时间吃晚饭。顺便说一句，我讲这些并不是要替 Disney 的定价辩护。这是个无解的问题，

cues.en: but it was entirely
cues.zh: 但这完全是

cues.en: voluntarily of Disney's making. But as it stands, they've got these problems baked directly into the loaf, and there's no easy solution. So if they can't add more rooms to drop the price, they could sweeten the deal by lengthening the voyage,
cues.zh: Disney 自己心甘情愿造成的。现在，这些问题已经成了它们设计的一部分，没有简单的解决办法。所以，如果他们没法增加客房来降价，或许可以延长航程，让体验更划算，

cues.en: even if for one additional day. But no, they can't do that either. They've already got a tricky situation with the character driven story elements, in that the character performers are limited to eight hour shifts. In case you didn't pick up on it, they solved this problem on day one by having you arrive in the late afternoon, and on day two by sending you into the theme park for half the day. That's right. The theme park excursion was just a distraction.
cues.zh: 哪怕只多一天也好。但不行，这也做不到。角色扮演剧情本来就有个棘手的问题：演员每班最多工作八小时。你可能没注意到，他们第一天让你在下午晚些时候抵达，第二天又安排你半天去主题乐园，正是为了解决这个问题。没错，去主题乐园只是为了转移你的注意力。

cues.en: I know you didn't notice at the time because the gameplay was so compelling, but if they added a third day, how would they distract you then? I personally would have appreciated downtime,
cues.zh: 我知道当时游戏体验太吸引人，你没留意到，但如果他们加上第三天，该怎么转移你的注意力？我个人倒是很乐意有些自由活动时间，

cues.en: but if everyone has downtime simultaneously,
cues.zh: 但如果所有人同时休息，

cues.en: we've run back into the issue of both the rooms and the common areas being far too small. Another easily preventable issue. I've seen a lot of people saying, maybe now that it failed, they'll just get rid of the role play element and open as a normal hotel, but they can't. Every other Disney hotel offers constantly running shuttle buses, taking guests to and from the theme parks and shopping center. Disney never bothered implementing this service for the Star Cruiser because they assume you're going to stay all day, and then also because it would cost more money. But if the hotel isn't a LARP experience, one assumes you're going to spend most of your day outside. The problem is the Star Cruiser was built backstage of one of their theme parks. Remember, security had to stop our taxi at the gate and check everyone's IDs before we could approach? Doing this with a full bus of tired theme park guests all coming back at once after the fireworks show would be possible, but it would also be a logistical nightmare and an additional expense.
cues.zh: 我们又会碰到客房和公共区域都太小的问题。这又是一个本来完全可以避免的问题。我看到很多人说，也许失败之后，他们会干脆取消角色扮演体验，把这里改成普通酒店，但他们做不到。Disney 的其他酒店都有班次密集的穿梭巴士，接送住客往返主题乐园和购物中心。Disney 从没给 Star Cruiser 安排这项服务，因为他们以为你会在里面待上一整天，而且这么做也要花更多钱。但如果酒店不再提供真人角色扮演体验，人们自然会把大部分时间花在外面。问题在于，Star Cruiser 建在其中一个主题乐园的后台区域。还记得吗？安保人员得在入口处拦下我们的出租车，检查所有人的证件，我们才能继续前行。要是换成一整辆载满玩累了的游客、烟花表演结束后同时返程的巴士，当然也不是办不到，但物流上会是一场噩梦，还得增加额外开支。

cues.en: Finally, the Star Cruiser lacks basic amenities all the other Disney hotels provide, like a pool and a fitness center. And you'll recall that the rooms are very small. This means that without the role play elements, not only would the hotel not command a very high price tag, it would reasonably be valued lower than any other hotel on property. The only way to balance out low room value would be to add a lot more rooms, and now we're back to all the problems with the building that I just told you about. Funnily enough, if you do want to stay at a version of the Star Cruiser that's just a hotel, you can still do that. In 2022, French theme park Futuroscope
cues.zh: 最后，Star Cruiser 缺少其他迪士尼酒店都提供的基本设施，比如泳池和健身中心。你还记得那些房间非常小。这意味着，如果没有角色扮演元素，这家酒店不仅无法定出很高的价格，合理估值也会低于园区内任何其他酒店。要平衡低房间价值，唯一办法就是增加大量房间，而这样一来，又回到我刚跟你们说过的这栋建筑的所有问题。有趣的是，如果你确实想住一个只是酒店的 Star Cruiser 版本，你仍然可以做到。2022 年，法国主题公园 Futuroscope

cues.en: opened the hotel station Cosmos,
cues.zh: 开设了酒店站 Cosmos，

cues.en: which looks suspiciously familiar. A room there will run you about $250
cues.zh: 它看起来眼熟得可疑。那里一间房大约要 250 美元

cues.en: a night, and they're actually bigger than the rooms in Star Cruiser. Aesthetically, the decor is so similar to Star Cruiser, it feels legally actionable,
cues.zh: 一晚，而且它们实际上比 Star Cruiser 的房间还大。从审美上看，装饰和 Star Cruiser 如此相似，感觉都能告侵权了，

cues.en: in my opinion. So it's very funny to me that the hotel station Cosmos was the one to stand the test of time. As for the physical remains of the Star Cruiser, in a 2023 interview, Parks chairman Josh D'Amaro assured fans that something would be done with it after the closure. But he gave no indication as to what, which to me says that he didn't actually know, and also probably was lying. If I had to look to the future of the hotel, here's my theory. I think they might open it up as an expensive dining location. You know, guests will make dinner reservations,
cues.zh: 在我看来。所以我觉得非常搞笑的是，经受住时间考验的偏偏是酒店站 Cosmos。至于 Star Cruiser 的实体遗留，2023 年的一次采访中，乐园主席 Josh D'Amaro 向粉丝保证，关闭后会对它做点什么。但他没有说明要做什么，这在我看来说明他其实也不知道，而且很可能是在撒谎。如果我必须展望这家酒店的未来，我的推测是这样。我认为他们可能会把它开放成一个昂贵的餐饮场所。你知道，客人会预订晚餐，

cues.en: check-in at the gate in Star Wars Land, and then board the spaceship themed buses to the hotel. But they probably have to build more of these or a bigger bus to accommodate everybody arriving at once. I acknowledge that the guests having to be transported by bus is an extreme hassle, but it's not practical to have people driving up and it's not walkable from anywhere, so don't I think there's anything else they could do for that element. When guests arrive, the wings of the building containing the hotel rooms will either be blocked off and used for storage, or demolished and converted back to parking lot space. The command bridge will be a photo op. The lightsaber training pod will be closed, because I can't think of a way for them to incorporate it while still putting through a high volume of people. Guests will eat in the dining room. They will watch a live singer, which they will all be able to see, because they will no longer be seating people in the corner booths. Will they, Disney? Will they? And then the alarm will sound. They'll be told the ship has been boarded by the First Order, and go to the atrium to watch an abridged version of the finale. Basically, just the Rey and Kylo Ren fight using the special effects that are already installed. While they're watching the finale, a new group of guests is entering the dining room. Rinse and repeat three to four times per night. And then they charge like, probably approaching $200
cues.zh: 在星球大战园区的大门办入住，然后登上飞船主题巴士去酒店。但他们大概得造更多这种巴士，或者更大的巴士，才能容纳同时到达的所有人。我承认客人必须坐巴士接送是极大的麻烦，但让人开车过来不现实，而且从任何地方都走不到，所以我不认为这个环节他们还能有别的办法。客人到达时，建筑里包含酒店房间的两翼会被封起来用作仓库，或者拆掉改回停车场空间。指挥桥会成为拍照点。光剑训练舱会关闭，因为我想不出他们如何在仍要接待大量人流的同时把它纳入流程。客人会在餐厅吃饭。他们会看一位现场歌手演唱，而且所有人都能看到，因为他们不会再把人安排在角落卡座了。会吗，迪士尼？会吗？然后警报会响起。他们会被告知飞船已被第一军团登舰，然后去中庭观看缩减版的终章。基本上就是 Rey 和 Kylo Ren 的打斗，用已经装好的特效。他们看终章时，新一批客人正进入餐厅。如此反复，每晚三到四次。然后他们收费，大概接近 200 美元

cues.en: per person for the experience. Adults get one alcoholic beverage for free, and then it's like $99 for kids. The only other possible outcome is that it'll sit abandoned,
cues.zh: 每人，体验价。成人免费获得一杯酒精饮料，然后小孩大概 99 美元。唯一其他可能的结果就是它会被闲置，

cues.en: growing mold. They'll use the dining room to host manager meetings, or maybe new hire training seminars,
cues.zh: 长出霉菌。他们会用餐厅举办经理会议，或者也许新员工培训研讨会，

cues.en: and the hotel rooms for storage of bubble wands and balloons. That's the laziest solution, so that feels the most likely to me. Maybe that's what Josh meant by something. Part 19, the cast members. Cast member usually refers to actors, but in Disney vernacular, it's every employee who works there. And I just wanted to do a section on this to say, anytime the Star Cruiser felt deluxe to me, anytime I felt they had gone above and beyond to give a good experience, it was entirely through the efforts of individual cast members. It's kind of like that line from Jurassic Park where John Hammond says they spared no expense. In this case, I felt like Disney spared lots of expenses,
cues.zh: 酒店房间则用来存放泡泡魔杖和气球。那是最懒的解决方案，所以我觉得那最有可能。也许 Josh 说的“做点什么”就是这个意思。第19部分，演职人员。演职人员通常指演员，但在迪士尼用语里，它指所有在那里工作的员工。我只是想做一节内容来说：每当 Star Cruiser 让我觉得豪华，每当我觉得他们为了提供好体验而超越期待，那完全是通过一个个演职人员的努力。有点像《侏罗纪公园》里 John Hammond 说的那句“他们不惜成本”。在这个例子里，我觉得迪士尼省了很多成本，

cues.en: too many. But by contrast, I felt that the cast members spared no effort. I would like to think that maybe Disney paid them well above the going rate to reflect this extra level of service they provided, but I know in my heart they probably didn't. They were probably just like, you'll earn more in tips. You're lucky to work here. Which, if true,
cues.zh: 省得太多了。但相比之下，我觉得演职人员不遗余力。我愿意相信，迪士尼也许给了他们远高于市场水平的工资，以反映他们提供的额外服务水平，但我心里知道，他们大概没有。他们大概只会说：你可以多赚点小费。你能在这里工作算你幸运。如果这是真的，

cues.en: boo. Anyway, let's highlight a few examples. In most cases, I was trying not to film people's faces unless they were a character performer, but I'll show footage where I have it. The merchandise cast members were so fun. This guy gave me a whole in character guided tour of the store and everything in it. And he told me in character about how he runs a Gaia fan club on his home world, and then we talked a little about how we were both from Coruscant. I am the biggest Gaia fan of the whole galaxy. What's your favorite song? My favorite song? Probably Hainanea or Coaxial. Hainanea's classic. Yes. Yeah. The next day, I had a long conversation with these two gift shop cast members about stuff that was happening around the ship. They were really funny. You don't think it's a stowaway.
cues.zh: 嘘。总之，让我们重点看几个例子。大多数情况下，我尽量不拍别人的脸，除非他们是角色扮演演员，但有些素材我会展示。周边商品店的演职人员太有趣了。这家伙给我做了一整套角色内的商店导览，介绍了店里的一切。他还以角色身份告诉我，他如何在母星经营一个 Gaia 粉丝俱乐部，然后我们聊了聊我们俩都来自 Coruscant。我是全银河最大的 Gaia 粉丝。你最喜欢的歌是哪首？我最喜欢的歌？大概是 Hainanea 或 Coaxial。Hainanea 是经典。是的。是啊。第二天，我和这两个礼品店演职人员聊了很久，聊飞船周围发生的事。他们真的很搞笑。你不觉得它是偷渡者吗？

cues.en: Again, Wookie, like, seven feet tall super. Right. How would they do They would
cues.zh: 再说，丘巴卡那种伍基人，差不多有两米多高，对吧。他们会怎么弄？他们会

cues.en: leave fur everywhere. Think if we actually had a bookie, I would notice. We would have noticed already. I kept coming back to look at the jewelry display because they were all sold out, and one of the cast members actually got manager approval to sell me the display model. So I got the very last one on the ship. This cast member in Batuu had customized his own outfit outfit for a little shoulder pork. On our first visit to the lounge, our waitress brought out our drinks, and then also brought out a little dish of water for Skippy to drink. And the other employees behind the bar were really setting a great mood. They knew all the alien songs playing over the speakers, and were singing and dancing along.
cues.zh: 弄得毛掉得到处都是。想想看，如果真有个伍基人在船上，我们肯定会发现的，其实早就该注意到了。我一直忍不住回到珠宝展示柜前看，因为那些都卖光了，结果有位演职人员专门去请示经理，批准把展示样品卖给我。所以我买到了全船最后一件。在巴图星，有位演职人员给自己的服装做了改装，就为了装一只小肩膀丘巴卡。我们第一次去酒廊的时候，服务员不仅端来了我们的饮品，还给斯基皮端来一小碟水喝。吧台后面的其他员工也特别会营造气氛，音响里放的每一首外星歌曲他们都会唱，还跟着又唱又跳。

cues.en: Our waiter Miguel at both dinners remembered our drink orders and had them waiting for us when we arrived the second night. He also told us the in universe details about all the food and brought me that extra Mustafarian cheese. I went out into the atrium at night to film it while it was empty. I asked if I could step up on one of the little benches, and obviously, I couldn't. I don't know why I asked. But then while I was filming, the cast member disappeared and came back with a little step stool to stand on instead. It was so nice. Now, this isn't really exclusive to Star Cruiser. I think Disney cast members tend to be this enthusiastic and helpful across the board. But it was an integral part of the experience, so I still think it's worth remarking upon. I should also mention that for the opening team, the vast majority of the Star Cruiser's hospitality staff were apparently kids doing the Disney College Program. Today,
cues.zh: 两顿晚餐都是我们的服务员米格尔，他记得我们的点单，第二天晚上我们一到，饮品就已经备好了。他还给我们讲每道菜的星战世界观细节，还给我多上了一份穆斯塔法里安奶酪。晚上我跑到中庭去，趁没人的时候拍些画面。我问能不能站上那小长椅去拍，当然不行了。我也不知道我为什么要问。但就在我拍摄的时候，那位演职人员悄悄离开，回来时搬来了一个小踏凳让我站。真的太贴心了。虽然这算不上星际巡航号独有的特色，我觉得迪士尼的演职人员普遍都这么热情周到，但它是整个体验不可或缺的一部分，所以还是值得一提。还要说一下，开幕团队里，星际巡航号的绝大部分酒店服务人员 apparently 都是参加迪士尼大学实习项目的学生。今天，

cues.en: we are going to surprise some of our college program participants.
cues.zh: 我们要给几位大学实习项目的参与者一个惊喜。

cues.en: They are gonna be part of our opening team of the Star Wars Galactic Star Cruiser. I'm so excited. There's a lot of good energy. This means that they were young workers, juggling shifts with classes.
cues.zh: 他们将成为星球大战银河星际巡航号开幕团队的一员。我太激动了，现场气氛特别好。这就意味着，他们都是年轻的工人，要一边上课一边轮班。

cues.en: For many of them, this was probably their first job ever in their entire lives. With such a new product and so many moving parts, they must have been constantly solving issues.
cues.zh: 对很多人来说，这可能是他们人生中的第一份工作。面对这么全新的产品和这么多复杂的环节，他们肯定得不停地解决各种问题。

cues.en: And given the cost of the experience, the emotional stakes would have been much higher. So with that in mind, I think it's even more admirable that they did such a good job. But I also think it was really unfair of Disney to put them in that position in the first place. It's also weird because like, that must have been a cost cutting measure. Right? College program is part time. It doesn't come with health benefits, and the kids are housed by Disney, the cost of which is deducted from their paycheck. On top of all that, they have a lower base pay than regular employees. What's worse, allegedly, Star Cruiser invented a work position called Roamer. This would be a catch all role responsible for pretty much every task in the hotel. Concierge,
cues.zh: 考虑到这个体验的价格，他们承受的情感压力会大得多。所以想到这一点，他们能做得这么好就更让人敬佩了。但我也觉得，迪士尼一开始就让他们身处这种境地，实在不太厚道。而且这也很奇怪，因为这显然是一种削减成本的措施，对吧？大学实习项目是兼职，没有医疗保险，住宿由迪士尼提供，费用从他们的工资里扣。除此之外，他们的基本工资还比正式员工低。更糟糕的是，据说星际巡航号还发明了一个叫"漫游员"的岗位。这是个什么活都得干的全能角色，几乎负责酒店里的所有任务。礼宾，

cues.en: food, housekeeping,
cues.zh: 餐饮，客房清洁，

cues.en: and bell services, or as I like to call it, smuggling luggage. This structure is obviously beneficial to employers,
cues.zh: 还有行李服务——或者按我的说法，就是走私行李。这种架构显然对雇主有利，

cues.en: making each individual employee more expendable, and also ensuring you can pack as many into a single shift as possible. Requiring a single job position to juggle so many different responsibilities would of course command a higher hourly rate.
cues.zh: 让每个员工都更容易被替代，也确保一个班次能塞进尽量多的人。要求一个岗位承担这么多不同的职责，按理说理应拿到更高的时薪。

cues.en: But not if you hire a bunch of students who are new to the hospitality industry, who have no basis for comparison and can't tell when you're asking too much them. And sure enough, of the 80 or so cast members hired onto this roamer job, allegedly only about 10 were full time experienced workers, with the rest being college program students. The other issue is, and I'm not saying that the college program students provide worse service than other employees,
cues.zh: 但如果你雇的是一群刚入行酒店服务业的学生，他们没有比较基准，也看不出你什么时候要求过高，那就不行了。果不其然，在这个 roamer 岗位上雇的约80名演职人员中，据称只有约10名是全职有经验的员工，其余都是大学项目学生。另一个问题是——我不是说大学项目学生提供的服务比其他员工差——

cues.en: but they're indisputably the cheapest labor available to Disney. So here again, why was Disney so determined to take the cheapest route on every aspect of the Star Cruiser? Anyway, I just hope that none of these people found themselves out of a job because of Disney's incompetence in launching this doomed hotel. But in my experience, when attractions close, Disney just shuffles the cast members to other locations around the resort, so they're probably okay. But sadly, I can't assume the same is true for the character performers. They had an especially difficult job, not comparable to anything else in the theme parks. They had to memorize collective hours worth of scenes and work in two day blocks where they were on stage for eight hour shifts each day. They also had to familiarize themselves with the schedule to ensure they were at the right place at the right time, and be skilled at improv,
cues.zh: 但无可争辩的是，他们是迪士尼能获得的最廉价劳动力。所以，回到同样的问题：为什么迪士尼在 Star Cruiser 的每个方面都如此坚决地走最便宜的路线？总之，我只希望没有人因为迪士尼搞砸了这家注定失败的酒店开业而失业。但根据我的经验，景点关闭时，迪士尼只是把演职人员调到度假区其他地点，所以他们可能没事。但遗憾的是，我不能假定角色演员也是如此。他们的工作格外艰难，主题公园里没有别的工作能与之相比。他们必须记住累计数小时的戏份，并以两天为一组工作，每天在台上演满八小时。他们还得熟悉日程，确保在正确的时间出现在正确的地点，并且擅长即兴表演，

cues.en: and retain information like guest names and relationships to the characters. Despite all this, these actors allegedly have the exact same rates as other performers around the parks. These salaries aren't public information, so maybe that's just a rumor, but that is the word on the street from people who alleged to be the employees. So if this is true, Lieutenant Croix takes on this massive workload for Star Cruiser, only to make the exact same rate as Gaston, who must only memorize two songs for a thirty minute stage show.
cues.zh: 还要记住客人姓名以及他们与角色的关系等信息。尽管如此，据称这些演员的薪酬标准与园区其他演员完全相同。这些薪资并非公开信息，所以也许只是传言，但这是自称员工的人传出的说法。所以如果属实，Lieutenant Croix 为 Star Cruiser 承担了如此巨大的工作量，拿到的薪酬却和 Gaston 完全相同，而 Gaston 只需要为一场30分钟的舞台剧记住两首歌。

cues.en: That's part of why I get so miffed at people insisting that, yes, the Star Cruiser price is fair, because it's exactly like a bunch of Broadway shows in a row. It's not. But also, do you think your money is going directly to Captain Keevan? Do think she's getting paid as much per day as a lead in a Broadway show makes for several performances? Because I don't. And after all this, these actors were the first to be punished when the star cruiser underperformed.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么我对那些坚持说“没错，Star Cruiser 的价格很公道，因为它就像一连串百老汇演出”的人如此恼火的部分原因。并不是。而且，你觉得你的钱会直接进 Captain Keevan 的口袋吗？你觉得她每天拿到的报酬，能比得上百老汇主演演好几场的收入吗？因为我不这么认为。而经历这一切之后，当 Star Cruiser 表现不佳时，这些演员却最先受到惩罚。

cues.en: Actors are cast with roles in mind, so they aren't as easy to reassign as a house keeping employee. So instead, they were allegedly hit with waves of layoffs.
cues.zh: 演员是按角色选定的，所以不像客房清洁员工那样容易重新调配。因此，据称他们反而遭遇了一波又一波裁员。

cues.en: First, when the staffing was scaled back due to low demand, and then again when the Star Cruiser was closed completely. And I realize that this is sort of the nature of acting as a profession. It's not the most stable job. But when the Star Cruiser did close, it did so very abruptly. Reportedly, a lot of the main character performers were hired on a year long contractual basis,
cues.zh: 一开始是因为需求低迷而削减人手，后来 Star Cruiser 彻底关闭时又是一次。我明白这在某种程度上就是表演这个职业的常态，它不是最稳定的工作。但当 Star Cruiser 真的关闭时，来得非常突然。据报道，很多主演角色的表演者都是以一年期合同聘用的，

cues.en: at which point their contracts may or may not be renewed. So they probably had a long term expectation of when they'd be out of a job, and they probably didn't expect it to be in September 2023. Allegedly, when the decision to close the Starcruiser was made, the cast were given very little warning, only finding out they would be losing their jobs in a staff meeting a handful of minutes before the media announcement, and just before starting a long shift. Even though so much was asked of them, and they really rose to the occasion, I feel like the cast members were the first ones thrown under the bus when the star cruiser failed through no fault of their own.
cues.zh: 届时合同可能续签，也可能不续。所以他们大概率对自己的失业时间有个长期预期，而且很可能没想到会是在2023年9月。据称，当关闭 Starcruiser 的决定做出时，演员们几乎没有得到任何预警，只是在员工会议上、比媒体官宣早几分钟才知道自己要失业了，而且当时还正要开始一个很长的班次。尽管公司对他们要求那么多，他们也确实不负众望，但我觉得，当 Star Cruiser 因与他们毫无关系的失误而失败时，演员成员们成了第一批被推出来背锅的人。

cues.en: And, that feels bad. Part 20,
cues.zh: 而且，这让人很不舒服。第20部分，

cues.en: you've been robbed. I'm not talking about the cost of the cruise. If I was, this section would have been called, I've been robbed. No. You've been robbed. We've been robbed, all of us. I mentioned way back in part one that Disney has been marketing the idea of themed immersive experiences for years. And one land they pitched as immersive was Star Wars Galaxy's Edge. I said that, but then I changed the subject. I put a pin in it, but I didn't tell you about the pin. It was a surprise, like when you step on a pin. Pandora the world of Avatar was pitched as immersive. Star Wars Galaxy's Edge was pitched as immersive. And at the end of the day, they're both about equally immersive. They both have large set pieces with really tall structures.
cues.zh: 你们被坑了。我说的不是这次巡航的价钱。如果是的话，这一节就该叫“我被坑了”。不，是你被坑了。我们都——我们所有人——被坑了。我在很早的第一部分就提到，迪士尼多年来一直在营销“主题化沉浸式体验”这个概念。其中一个被宣传为沉浸式的园区就是 Star Wars Galaxy's Edge。我虽然这么说了，但随后就换了话题。我把这事暂时搁置了，却没告诉你这根“针”是什么。它是个“惊喜”——就像你踩到图钉时的那种。Pandora the world of Avatar 被宣传为沉浸式，Star Wars Galaxy's Edge 也被宣传为沉浸式。而说到底，它们俩的沉浸程度差不多。它们都有大型布景和非常高的建筑。

cues.en: They both have rides. They both have themed food and themed merchandise. And in the case of Pandora, that is roughly what was promised. But when they announced Galaxy's Edge, they promised much more. It was meant to be the most immersive theme park land ever built, unlike anything you've seen before. Encounters that enhance the story,
cues.zh: 它们都有游乐设施，都有主题餐饮和主题商品。而就 Pandora 而言，宣传的大致也就是这些。但公布 Galaxy's Edge 时，他们承诺的要多得多。它本应是有史以来建造过的最沉浸式的主题乐园园区，和你以前见过的任何东西都不一样。能增强故事体验的邂逅，

cues.en: roaming droids and aliens you can interact with. This new 14 acre land
cues.zh: 可以互动的四处游走的机器人和外星人。这片全新的14英亩园区

cues.en: will be occupied by many inhabitants, humanoids, aliens, and droids. Now the inhabitants of this remote frontier town, one of the last stops before wild space, will operate every store and restaurant. This outpost is filled with characters,
cues.zh: 将由许多居民占据——类人生物、外星人和机器人。这个偏远边境小镇的居民——它是进入荒野空间之前的最后几站之一——将经营每一家商店和餐厅。这个前哨站里到处都是角色，

cues.en: alien creatures and droids. Now, you might have seen a favorite little droid rolling around in that video, and yes, BB-eight is one of the characters you can find there. Each experience will literally be out of this world,
cues.zh: 到处都是外星生物和机器人。你可能在那个视频里看到一个受人喜爱的小机器人滚来滚去——没错，BB-8 就是你在那里能找到的角色之一。每一种体验都真的会“超乎尘世”，

cues.en: like this big fellow up here. A personal reputation score score that follows you throughout the land and impacts your day. For you, our guest, every encounter will bring more of the Star Wars story to life in a place
cues.zh: 就像上面这位大块头。一个跟随你走遍整个园区、影响你一整天体验的个人声望分数。对于你——我们的游客——每一次邂逅都会让 Star Wars 的故事在这样一个地方更加鲜活地呈现，

cues.en: you can explore like never before. This is a living place, a place where your choices matter, and a place where you can even earn a reputation. Each guest is success...
cues.zh: 让你以前所未有的方式去探索。这是一个鲜活的场所，一个你的选择至关重要的地方，一个你甚至可以赢得声望的地方。每位游客……

cues.en: Is
cues.zh: 是

cues.en: successful when they complete their mission. Harko,
cues.zh: 当他们完成任务时，就算成功。Harko，

cues.en: whoever that is. It might even end up on the list of a local bounty hunter.
cues.zh: 不管那是谁。它甚至可能出现在当地赏金猎人的名单上。

cues.en: I hear that Harko's here is someone you particularly don't wanna mess with. If your name ends up on his list, well, that might truly be a problem when you show up at the local cantina. Early plans featured a dinner show venue called the Kalicory Club, and some of the concept art is available to the public in the Galaxy's Edge art book. During construction, they appear to have cleared the land necessary for the Kalicory Club, before pulling back at the last minute and building the much smaller cantina,
cues.zh: 听说Harko可不是好惹的。要是你名字上了他的名单，去当地cantina的时候可能真要倒霉了。早期方案里有个叫Kalicory Club的晚餐秀场地，一些概念艺术图收录在《Galaxy's Edge》艺术书里，已经公开了。施工期间，他们似乎已经为Kalicory Club清理了土地，但最后一刻却撤回计划，改建了小得多的cantina。

cues.en: leaving the extra plot of land as a parking lot backstage.
cues.zh: 把多余的那块地留作后台的停车场。

cues.en: In 2017, Imagineers test drove interactive droids around Tomorrowland for a couple days, then abandoned that project as well. In 2023, they rolled out these little two legged guys, but they immediately said they were only going to be used for special events and would not be a permanent fixture, and called them like an experiment. And to me, it was just code for we built this to impress shareholders, and you're not going to see them on the regular. Once in a blue moon, you can catch an r two d two rolling around, but I've been told that that droid is actually the same model that's for sale in the adjacent Droid Depot gift shop, so that's really just a product demo. In 2014, before Galaxy's Edge was even announced, Disneyland rolled out two limited time interactive games. The first was Legends of Frontierland.
cues.zh: 2017年，Imagineers 在明日世界试运行了几天互动机器人，之后又放弃了那个项目。2023年，他们推出了这些小个子双足机器人，但马上就说它们只会用于特别活动，不会长期驻留，还把这说成是一种实验。在我看来，这其实就是委婉地表示：我们造这个是为了给股东留下深刻印象，你平时是看不到它们的。难得一遇的时候，你能碰到一个 R2-D2 在到处转悠，但我听说那个机器人其实是旁边 Droid Depot 礼品店在售的同款，所以那真的只是个产品演示。2014年，在 Galaxy's Edge 还没公布之前，迪士尼乐园就推出了两款限时互动游戏。第一款是 Legends of Frontierland。

cues.en: The story of the game was that two different factions were fighting for territory in a Western gold town. As a player, you had to choose which territory to support and buy land for your side. You could earn wooden nickels in a lot of different ways, running errands for characters, gambling at the saloon, or turning in a fugitive for a bounty. At the end of each day, a winner would be announced based on guest input. And the stakes would be raised by having character actors on each side of the conflict who you would interact with during your missions. These actors would then lead the day end finale ceremony. In Adventureland, they had the adventure trading company, which worked on a different system. You would pay money for a particular quest, and then at the end, you would win a tangible item, these little totems, which were said to have mystical properties. Some were really simple to get, like you would just buy a themed food and an item came with it. But others were much more involved. You'd pay for the quest in a gift shop, be handed an activity booklet, and then go around adventure land looking for solutions to various puzzles. Like decoding the ancient writing in the Indiana Jones temple, or talking to the jungle cruise skippers to complete a training course. Then you'd bring the completed booklet back to claim your prize. Both games were well received by guests, and Imagineers later confirmed that they were both actually covert play tests for possible interactive elements at the forthcoming Galaxy's Edge. But when the land opened,
cues.zh: 这个故事背景是，在西部淘金小镇上，两个不同阵营为了争夺地盘而战。作为玩家，你必须选择支持哪一方，并为你的一方购买土地。你可以通过很多方式赚得木制代币，比如替角色跑腿、在酒馆赌博，或者抓捕逃犯领取赏金。每天结束时，会根据游客的参与情况宣布当天的获胜方。而且双方阵营都有角色演员，你在执行任务的过程中会与他们互动，这让博弈更加激烈。这些演员还会主持每天闭园时的压轴仪式。在冒险乐园里，有一个“冒险贸易公司”，它采用的是另一套玩法。你花钱购买某个特定任务，完成后就能赢得一件实体物品——这些小图腾据说拥有神秘力量。有些很容易拿到，比如你只要买一份主题食品，就会附赠一件。但另一些则复杂得多。你在礼品店付费领取任务后，会拿到一本活动手册，然后要在冒险乐园各处寻找各种谜题的答案。比如破译印第安纳·琼斯神庙里的古代文字，或者与“丛林巡航”的船长们交谈来完成一项训练课程。最后你把填好的手册带回来，就能领取奖励。这两个游戏都深受游客好评，后来幻想工程师也证实，它们其实都是为即将开园的“星球大战：银河边缘”可能加入的互动元素而进行的秘密测试。但当这个园区开放时，

cues.en: neither concept was present. The only gameplay that materialized was the Star Wars data pad app game, which we've all agreed sucks. And what gets me about the app game is, you can very much see echoes of Legends of Frontierland in it, but it's an incomplete game. You complete tasks to earn in game money, but instead of tasks that incorporate the environment, you're just scanning QR codes and then completing repetitive puzzles on your phone, and you can't do anything with the money. You can hack the control panels and chips for the resistance, and you might be rewarded with a feeble beeping sound effect, but there's never any consequence to what you've done. This is all speculation, but I'd imagine that all of this was meant to culminate in the same way as Legends of Frontierland. Guests would earn points or territory for either the First Order or their assistance, and then at the end of the day, they could have actors come out and in a story moment, they would reveal who had won. But if that was the plan, it was never implemented,
cues.zh: 这两个概念都没有出现。唯一真正落地的游戏内容，就是《星球大战》的数据板应用游戏，而我们都同意它很糟糕。让我觉得最遗憾的是，你确实能在这款应用游戏里看到《Legends of Frontierland》的影子，但它是个没做完的游戏。玩家完成任务来赚取游戏内货币，但这些任务并没有利用环境，而只是让你扫描二维码，然后在手机上反复完成一些解谜；而且这些钱也没有任何用途。你可以为抵抗组织入侵控制面板和芯片，可能得到的奖励只是一声微弱的哔声，但你的行为从来不会带来任何后果。这些都只是推测，但我猜这一切原本是要像《Legends of Frontierland》那样收尾的。游客可以为第一秩序或抵抗组织赚取积分或领地，然后在一天结束时，演员们会出场，在一个剧情环节中揭晓哪一方获胜。但如果这确实是原计划，那它从未真正实现。

cues.en: probably because Disney is trying to cut back on actors to save money. So instead, you feel like you're playing half a game, or like a third of a game, very little of a game, and no reputation score either. No role play element. Instead of filling the land with character actors, the CEO realized it would be cheaper to just tell the cashiers and food service workers that they get to be part of the story by using in universe vernacular,
cues.zh: 可能是因为迪士尼想削减演员来省钱。于是你会觉得自己只玩到半个游戏，或者三分之一、一点点游戏，而且没有声望分数。也没有角色扮演元素。CEO没有让园区里到处是角色演员，而是意识到更省钱的做法是直接告诉收银员和餐饮服务人员：他们可以用世界观内的用语，成为故事的一部分，

cues.en: and then brag about how revolutionary it is that everyone in the land is in character, even though they're not being compensated for the extra labor and guests are getting a lesser experience. Even elsewhere in their parks, Disney has started laying off most of the live performers who used to sing and dance because they were deemed too expensive. Only characters who do photo ops are safe because Mickey Mouse and Cinderella directly earn their keep by selling Genie Plus front of the line access and PhotoPass digital photo packages.
cues.zh: 然后吹嘘这有多革命性：园区里每个人都在角色里，尽管额外的劳动没有报酬，游客得到的体验却更差。甚至在Disney其他园区，他们也开始裁掉大部分过去唱歌跳舞的现场演员，因为觉得太贵。只有负责拍照互动的角色安全，因为Mickey Mouse和Cinderella靠卖Genie Plus免排队通道和PhotoPass数字照片套餐直接带来收入。

cues.en: Looking through the Star Wars Land art book, there's so much art for interactive alien citizens, and none of those made it to opening. I was especially surprised to see this female Rhodian character.
cues.zh: 翻看Star Wars Land设定画册，里面有大量互动外星居民的艺术图，但没有一个在开园时实现。尤其让我惊讶的是这个女性Rhodian角色。

cues.en: It seems that even a costume like Iwani was originally intended for the theme park, but scrapped for budgetary reasons. Every promised feature that would have made Star Wars Land unique was cut, not because any of it would have been impossible to implement, but because each one would have cost Disney just a little bit extra. Roaming droids cost money to repair. Actors, puppeteers, singers, they all cost marginally more per hour than a food service worker, because they have better unions. You can build a game into the land, but any pieces that move or interact, well, there go more maintenance costs. And if you want the app game to culminate in anything, that would probably be a skit, and that would mean more actors. Why build a bigger restaurant with more square footage, when you can instead save money by making a smaller building and enacting a rule where guests have to leave after forty minutes? Who cares if it's a worse experience? You'll still get their money. Why have a singer at the cantina? We already covered how singers are expensive. So what do we ultimately get at Galaxy's Edge? A themed courtyard, themed food, rides, and gift shops. The barest minimum expectations for a theme park land. It's no more impressive than anything they were building fifty years ago, just physically much bigger and emptier. And guest feedback has reflected this, with many calling the land a highly themed shopping mall with little to do. Then, less than three years after the underwhelming opening of Galaxy's Edge, they roll out the Galactic Star Cruiser. The hotel contains everything that was promised in that first announcement for Galaxy's Edge. A roaming droid, an interactive alien, character actors, reputation score, app integration, a dinner show with an alien singer named Gaia. In fact, if you look back at the concept art for the Kallikori club, you'll see that it actually appears to have an identical layout to the dining room on the Galactic Star Cruiser, just reskinned in clean colors. Over at the sides, you can even see those poles that blocked my view. And not only did the hotel cost extra,
cues.zh: 看起来连Iwani这样的服装原本也是为主题公园设计的，但因预算原因被砍。所有本会让Star Wars Land独一无二的承诺功能都被砍掉，不是因为其中任何一个无法实现，而是因为每一个都会让Disney多花一点钱。游荡机器人要花钱维修。演员、操偶师、歌手，每小时成本都比餐饮服务人员略高，因为他们的工会更强势。你可以在园区里做游戏，但任何会动或能互动的部件，维护成本又上去了。如果你想让App游戏有个高潮，那大概得是一段短剧，也就意味着更多演员。为什么要建一个面积更大的餐厅？你完全可以建小一点，再规定游客40分钟后必须离开，以此省钱。体验更差谁在乎？你照样能拿到他们的钱。为什么要在酒馆里安排歌手？我们已经说过歌手很贵。那Galaxy's Edge最终给了我们什么？主题庭院、主题餐饮、游乐设施和礼品店。一个主题公园园区的最低限度期望。并不比他们五十年前建的东西更惊艳，只是物理上大得多、空得多。游客反馈也反映了这一点，很多人说这个园区就是个高度主题化的购物中心，没什么可玩。然后，在Galaxy's Edge反响平平地开业不到三年后，他们推出了Galactic Star Cruiser。这家酒店包含了当年Galaxy's Edge首批公告里承诺的一切。游荡机器人、互动外星人、角色演员、声望分数、应用整合、由外星歌手Gaia出演的晚餐秀。事实上，回头看Kallikori club的概念图，你会发现它的布局似乎和Galactic Star Cruiser的餐厅一模一样，只是用干净色彩重新换皮。在两侧，你甚至能看到那些挡住我视线的柱子。而且这家酒店不仅要额外花钱，

cues.en: it cost a lot extra. More than any hotel Disney had ever offered before. Incomparable to the pricing structure for any themed entertainment ever offered by any company. Disney likes to pretend that Galaxy's Edge was never supposed to be more than it is. That it was always meant to be complemented by the Galactic Star Cruiser. What's pretty amazing is to think about being in the rooms, seeing concept art years ago, while we're building Galaxy's Edge with this in mind. But I haven't forgotten the truth. Galaxy's Edge was publicly announced in August 2015 and promised all of these features to guests complete with concept art. If the Galactic Star Cruiser was always part of the plan and developed simultaneously,
cues.zh: 还贵得多。比Disney以往提供的任何酒店都贵。和任何公司推出过的主题娱乐定价结构都无法相提并论。Disney喜欢假装Galaxy's Edge从来就不该比现在更多。假装它一直就该由Galactic Star Cruiser来补充。很妙的是去想象在房间里，看到多年前的概念图，而我们建Galaxy's Edge时正想着这个。但我没忘记真相。Galaxy's Edge于2015年8月公开宣布，并连同概念图向游客承诺了所有这些功能。如果Galactic Star Cruiser一直是计划的一部分并同步开发，

cues.en: why wasn't it announced at the same time? Why didn't they clarify then that the land's coolest features would exist only as DLC for the hotel guests? It wasn't until April 2017 that Disney distributed those first market research surveys about a Star Wars hotel. And at that point from the concept art they released with the survey, we can see that they didn't know what the building was going to look like yet, didn't know what it was going to cost, didn't have a full picture of it. So no, it doesn't really seem to me like the Galactic Star Cruiser was always part of the plan intended as a compliment to Galaxy's Edge. It seems to me like they had fully planned out Galaxy's Edge and logistically figured out the technology and budget it needed. And then someone internally seems to have said, wait,
cues.zh: 为什么没有同时宣布？为什么当时不澄清，园区最酷的功能只会作为酒店住客的DLC存在？直到2017年4月，Disney才分发最早那批关于Star Wars酒店的市场调研问卷。而从他们随问卷发布的概念图看，当时他们还不知道建筑会是什么样，不知道会花多少钱，也没有完整图景。所以不，我实在不觉得Galactic Star Cruiser一直是计划的一部分、本意是补充Galaxy's Edge。在我看来，他们当时已经完整规划了Galaxy's Edge，并从运营上算出了所需技术和预算。然后内部似乎有人说，等等，

cues.en: what if we just take away all the coolest parts and put them in a big locked building, And to get into that building, people have to give us a lot more money. I think the depth of storytelling, the amount of play,
cues.zh: 如果我们把所有最酷的部分拿掉，放进一栋上锁的大楼里会怎样？而要进入那栋楼，人们得给我们多得多钱。我觉得叙事深度、可玩内容量，

cues.en: the amount of engagement that a that a person is gonna experience, I don't think you're gonna question the cost. I actually think you're just gonna have a lot of fun. I also find it notable that the Disney parks used to have a popular interactive children's show called Jedi Training Academy,
cues.zh: 一个人将获得的沉浸感，我觉得你不会去计较花费。我其实觉得你就是会玩得很开心。我还注意到，Disney 乐园曾有一个很受欢迎的互动儿童节目，叫 Jedi Training Academy，

cues.en: which predated even the opening of Galaxy's Edge. Kids would put on little robes and be handed training lightsabers, run through a number of drills and then face off against a dark side opponent. Kids like to do it, and adults like to watch it because it was cute. The last remaining version of that show was canceled in June 2020, probably due to the pandemic. But even after Disney World started relaxing all its COVID precautions, the show never returned. Months later, the experience disappeared altogether from the website, and in July 2022, they quietly removed all physical signage from the park. And so I think it's interesting that here we see a similar experience,
cues.zh: 它甚至早于 Galaxy's Edge 开业。孩子们会穿上小长袍，拿到训练光剑，完成一系列训练，然后与黑暗面对手正面对决。孩子们喜欢参加，大人喜欢看，因为很可爱。这个节目最后仅存的版本于 2020 年 6 月取消，可能因为疫情。但即使 Disney World 开始放宽所有 COVID 防疫措施，这个节目也再没回归。几个月后，这个体验从网站上彻底消失，2022 年 7 月，他们又悄悄拆掉了园区里所有实体标牌。所以我觉得有意思的是，这里我们看到了一个类似的体验，

cues.en: again moved behind the paywall of the Galactic Star Cruiser. This isn't only a pattern in the Star Wars part of the parks either. This has become the new philosophy of the Disney theme parks. More and more amenities that used to be free are now being put behind paywalls. I told you about the m bands earlier, and how they've had this technology at the hotels for a while. Well, you used to get a magic band free with a hotel booking to use as your room key, but now they make you buy them. The fast pass system used to be free, now it costs extra, and it doesn't include every ride anymore. The good rides are a la carte, you have to buy those separately. Meanwhile, lines keep getting longer and longer because now that Disney can monetize long lines, corporate actually wants them to be long. The FastPasses actually have variable pricing, which is updated live in the app. So the longer the lines are, the more they can charge. And of course, they oversell the passes, because now they have an incentive to do so, so those lines aren't even actually short anymore. They fire all the atmosphere entertainment and close all the little diversions, because they'd rather everybody just pile into those lines, because the longer the lines, the more they can charge. Why build new rides? Why increase capacity? It's actually better for your bottom line if you don't anymore.
cues.zh: 它再次被放到了 Galactic Star Cruiser 的付费墙后面。这也不只是乐园里 Star Wars 区域的模式。这已经成为 Disney 主题乐园的新理念。越来越多过去免费的服务，现在都被放到了付费墙后面。我之前讲过 MagicBand，也讲过酒店里用这项技术已经有一阵子了。过去订酒店会免费送一个 MagicBand 当房卡用，但现在他们让你花钱买。FastPass 系统过去免费，现在要额外付费，而且不再包含所有游乐项目。好项目要单点收费，得单独买。与此同时，队伍越来越长，因为现在 Disney 能把长队变现，公司其实就希望队伍长。FastPass 其实是浮动定价，在 App 里实时更新。所以队伍越长，他们就能收越多钱。当然，他们还会超卖 FastPass，因为现在有动机这么做，所以那些队伍其实也不再短了。他们解雇所有氛围娱乐人员，关掉所有小分流项目，因为他们宁愿大家都挤进那些队伍，因为队伍越长，他们就能收越多钱。为什么要建新项目？为什么要增加容量？其实不再这么做，对你的利润反而更好。

cues.en: Why do anything above the bare minimum? Ride photos used to be free for pass holders, now they cost extra. Buses from the airport used to be free for Disney hotel guests, now they cost extra. Even the baskets of free bread they used to bring out at the expensive restaurants. Now you have to buy those as an appetizer.
cues.zh: 为什么要做任何超出最低限度的事？游乐项目照片过去对年卡用户免费，现在要额外收费。从机场出发的巴士过去对 Disney 酒店住客免费，现在要额外收费。就连昂贵餐厅过去会端上来的免费面包篮，现在也得作为开胃菜花钱买。

cues.en: So that's the dirty secret behind the Galactic Star Cruiser.
cues.zh: 这就是 Galactic Star Cruiser 背后的内幕。

cues.en: It wasn't an idea conceived to explore a new frontier and immersive experiences.
cues.zh: 它并不是为了探索新的边界、打造沉浸式体验而诞生的创意。

cues.en: It was just a lot of ideas they already had, had already promised us, some which they had already implemented,
cues.zh: 它不过是把他们已有的许多创意拿出来，其中一些早就向我们承诺过，也已经实现了，

cues.en: which were then taken away, paywalled. It wasn't driven by curiosity
cues.zh: 然后又把这些东西收回去，设成付费项目。这一切并非出于好奇

cues.en: or inspiration.
cues.zh: 或灵感。

cues.en: It was born of pure greed, Disney's boldest experiment and exorbitant upcharges.
cues.zh: 它纯粹是贪婪的产物，是 Disney 最大胆的实验，也是最离谱的额外收费项目。

cues.en: The Disney parks have always been more expensive than their direct competition,
cues.zh: Disney 乐园的票价一直都比直接竞争对手贵，

cues.en: even when parks like Universal Orlando started to roll out equally impressive attractions. And the reason people were willing to pay more for Disney was that even though the base cost was more expensive,
cues.zh: 即使 Universal Orlando 这样的乐园也开始推出同样令人惊艳的景点。人们愿意为 Disney 多花钱，是因为虽然基础票价更高，

cues.en: all of those little amenities were included, and that made people feel good. And now, people go, they pay the high base cost, and then they pay all the little extra costs. Because really, why have an expensive mediocre vacation when you could have an extra expensive adequate vacation?
cues.zh: 但那些小小的便利服务都包含在内，让人觉得很值。而现在，人们去了，付了高昂的基础费用，还要为各种小项目额外掏钱。说到底，既然能过一次贵上加贵、还算过得去的假期，何必只过一次昂贵又平庸的假期呢？

cues.en: They've already bought in, they might as well pay extra. But when they pay extra,
cues.zh: 他们已经投入了，干脆再多花点钱。但多花钱之后，

cues.en: they feel bad about it. And in some ways, this business model has been successful, because like I said, people are buying the amenities. Everybody's buying the magic bands and the bread baskets. Everybody's getting that fast pass add on, and in some cases, they're paying extra to ride individual rides. And Disney is super happy because they get more money. Who cares how people feel if they're still giving Disney the money? I'm not going to pretend Disney is a smile factory. Obviously, they've always been a for profit business at the end of the day. But I have to wonder what the long term implications of this business model will be. The Thompson family might fly in from Iowa for their trip in 2024,
cues.zh: 他们心里却不舒服。从某些方面来说，这种商业模式确实奏效了，因为正如我所说，大家都在购买这些便利服务。所有人都买了魔法手环和面包篮。所有人都加购了 FastPass，有些情况下还会为单项游乐项目额外付费。Disney 当然高兴，因为他们赚到了更多钱。只要人们还在掏钱，感受如何又有什么关系？我不会假装 Disney 是个制造笑容的工厂。显然，说到底，他们一直都是一家营利企业。但我不禁想知道，这种商业模式长期来看会带来什么后果。Thompson 一家可能会在 2024 年从 Iowa 飞来度假，

cues.en: and discover that they need to shell out extra money to go on the rides that they want, and begrudgingly do so. But will that make them want to come back in 2027?
cues.zh: 结果发现，想玩那些项目还得额外掏钱，于是虽不情愿，还是付了钱。但这会让他们想在 2027 年再来吗？

cues.en: The profits are high now, but what will they look like in three to five years? Maybe Disney doesn't care about that. Maybe if you set the price high enough, you can afford to have every family on earth come only one time, feel kind of bad about their trip, and never return. Or maybe Disney's right and they're too big to fail, and people won't like it, but they'll just keep coming back and paying more and more for the same old things that used to be free and feeling worse and worse about it. But I personally believe that eventually,
cues.zh: 现在利润很高，但三到五年后会是什么样？也许 Disney 根本不在乎。也许只要定价足够高，就算全世界每个家庭只来一次，觉得这趟旅行不太愉快，之后再也不来，也无所谓。又或者 Disney 是对的，他们大到不会倒，人们虽然不喜欢，却还是会一再回来，为过去免费的老项目付越来越多的钱，心里也越来越不舒服。但我个人认为，最终，

cues.en: if Disney doesn't course correct, they're going to hit a ceiling. And I think the Galactic Star Cruiser was only the first symptom of that. I think it felt the strain first, because it was so much more expensive. It was the ultimate monument to this age of Disney inflation,
cues.zh: 如果 Disney 不及时调整策略，他们终究会撞上天花板。我认为 Galactic Star Cruiser 只是最早出现的征兆。它最先感受到了压力，因为它的价格实在高得多。它是 Disney 通胀时代的终极纪念碑，

cues.en: a singular product we can all point to as the moment Disney's new more hostile business strategy became so painfully obvious.
cues.zh: 也是一个独一无二的产品，让我们都能指着它说：这就是 Disney 转向更具敌意的经营策略、并让这一变化变得痛苦而明显的时刻。

cues.en: The very first time a luxury cruise ship has ever been symbolic of the hubris of man. And this isn't to say that along the way, there weren't individual artists and actors and employees who were inspired and did give it their all. I feel sad for their sake that all their work has been for nothing. I even feel sad for this building, thinking of it sitting empty and sad, gathering dust, maybe used as storage or a corporate meeting space. It's haunting. It was a unique experience, and now it will be gone, and that's sad. But that doesn't mean it was worth the price. It doesn't even mean it was good. In fact, if the Galactic Star Cruiser had succeeded, it would have only emboldened Disney to keep charging more and offering less. It's a project that might have been catastrophic on a consumer level for the future of Disney parks. And for that reason, it deserved to fail, and I'm glad it's dead. Also, I'm still mad they sat me behind a pole.
cues.zh: 这是有史以来第一次，一艘豪华邮轮成为了人类狂妄自大的象征。这并不是说，一路上没有个别艺术家、演员和员工满怀热情、全力以赴。我为他们感到难过，因为他们所有的付出都白费了。我甚至为这栋大楼感到难过，想到它空荡荡、冷冷清清地积满灰尘，也许被当成仓库或公司会议室。这真令人唏嘘。它曾是一种独一无二的体验，现在它就要消失了，这很让人难过。但这并不意味着它值那个价钱，甚至不意味着它做得好。事实上，如果 Galactic Star Cruiser 成功了，只会让迪士尼更加有恃无恐地继续漫天要价、偷工减料。这个项目对消费者来说可能是灾难性的，甚至会危及迪士尼乐园的未来。正因如此，它理应失败，我也很高兴它死了。另外，他们让我坐在柱子后面这件事，我还是很生气。

cues.en: Alright, everybody. Put your hands in the air. Even you guys behind the call.
cues.zh: 好了，各位，把手举起来。连线另一头的各位也一样。

cues.en: What the?
cues.zh: 什么情况？

cues.en: They split it. Oh. It's really about checkout. No. It's
cues.zh: 他们把它拆开了。哦。其实都是关于退房的。不。这是

cues.en: really just about checkout and, like, telling us when we have to leave.
cues.zh: 真的就是关于退房，就是告诉我们什么时候必须离开。

cues.en: Is this Cora just an interest check if you guys were still trying to do a...
cues.zh: 这个 Cora 只是做个意向调查吗，如果你们还打算做一个……

cues.en: Do this one before?
cues.zh: 之前做过这个吗？
